name: West Eifel Volcanic Field
summary: The West Eifel Volcanic Field of western Germany, SW of the city of Bonn, is a dominantly Pleistocene group of 240 scoria cones, maars, and small stratovolcanoes covering an area of about 600 km2.

name: Chaine des Puys
summary: The Chaîne des Puys, prominent in the history of volcanology, form a N-S-trending chain of basaltic and trachytic cinder cones, basaltic maars, and trachytic lava domes in France's Massif Central that has been active into the Holocene.

name: Olot Volcanic Field
summary: The Olot volcanic field (also known as the Garrotxa volcanic field) occupies the NE corner of Spain south of the Pyrenees Mountains about 90 km NNE of Barcelona.

name: Calatrava Volcanic Field
summary: The Calatrava volcanic field lies in central Spain near Ciudad Real.

name: Colli Albani
summary: The Colli Albani (Alban Hills) complex immediately SE of Rome contains a large Pleistocene stratovolcano with a 10 x 12 km caldera formed during an eruptive period with six major explosions that produced at least 280 km3 of ejecta between about 560,000 and….

name: Campi Flegrei
summary: Campi Flegrei is a 13-km-wide caldera that encompasses part of Naples and extends to the south beneath the Gulf of Pozzuoli.

name: Vesuvius
summary: One of the world's most noted volcanoes, Vesuvius (Vesuvio) forms a dramatic backdrop to the Bay of Naples.

name: Ischia
summary: The Ischia volcanic complex forms a rectangular, 6 x 9 km island immediately SW of the Campi Flegrei area at the western side of the Bay of Naples.

name: Palinuro
summary: Palinuro seamount in the Tyrrhenian Sea north of the Eolian Islands rises nearly 3,000 m to within 70 m of the surface and has an open summit crater.

name: Stromboli
summary: Spectacular incandescent nighttime explosions at Stromboli have long attracted visitors to the "Lighthouse of the Mediterranean" in the NE Aeolian Islands.

name: Panarea
summary: The mostly submerged Panarea volcanic complex lies about midway between Stromboli and Lipari in the eastern part of the Aeolian Islands.

name: Lipari
summary: Lipari, the largest of the Aeolian Islands, is located immediately north of Vulcano Island.

name: Vulcano
summary: The word volcano is derived from Vulcano stratovolcano in Italy's Aeolian Islands.

name: Etna
summary: Mount Etna, towering above Catania on the island of Sicily, has one of the world's longest documented records of volcanism, dating back to 1500 BCE.

name: Campi Flegrei del Mar di Sicilia
summary: Campi Flegrei del Mar di Sicilia (Phlegraean Fields of the Sicily Sea) is composed of a group of submarine volcanoes SW of Sicily.

name: Pantelleria
summary: The island of Pantelleria is constructed above a drowned continental rift in the Strait of Sicily and has been the locus of intensive volcano-tectonic activity.

name: Marsili
summary: The Marsili seamount is a 50-km-long volcanic ridge in the southern Tyrrhenian Sea within a back-arc basin about 75-85 km NW of the Aeolian arc volcanoes.

name: Methana
summary: Methana volcano consists of a basaltic andesite to rhyodacitic lava dome complex forming the Methana Peninsula in the Sarronian Gulf on the NE side of Peloponnesus.

name: Milos
summary: Mílos and adjacent small islands have grown from submarine and subaerial volcanism that initially was dominantly andesitic and basaltic, but ended with predominately rhyolitic eruptions.

name: Santorini
summary: Santorini (Thera), in the Aegean Sea, has steep-walled caldera rim with villages that overlook an active volcanic island in the center of a caldera bay.

name: Kolumbo
summary: The submarine Kolumbo volcano is about 15 km NE of the center of the Santorini caldera.

name: Nisyros
summary: The easternmost volcano of the Aegean arc forms the 9-km-wide island of Nisyros, which is truncated by a 3-4 km wide caldera.

name: Kula
summary: The Kula volcanic field, the westernmost area of young volcanism in Turkey, lies about 450 km WNW of its closest Holocene neighbor in central Turkey, the Karapinar volcanic field.

name: Hasandag-Keciboyduran Volcanic Complex
summary: The Hasandag-Keçiboyduran volcanic complex in Central Anatolia includes the massive double-peaked Hasan Dagi stratovolcano, which has undergone four episodes of caldera collapse, the latest of which formed a 4-5 km wide caldera at the summit.

name: Erciyes Volcanic Complex
summary: The Erciyes Volcanic Complex at the northern end of the Sultansazligi Basin in central Anatolia is dominated by the massive eroded Erciyes Dagi stratovolcano at the approximate center of a radial monogenetic volcanic field 32 km in diameter, extending….

name: Karaca Dag
summary: Karaca Dag (also known as Karacalidag) is a broad basaltic shield volcano in SE Turkey about 100 km N of the Syrian border.

name: Nemrut Dagi
summary: Nemrut Dagi is the westernmost of a group of volcanoes near Lake Van in eastern Anatolia and the only one that has erupted in historical time.

name: Tenduruk Dagi
summary: Tendürek Dagi, also known as Tendürük Dagi, is an elongated shield volcano that rises above the Dogubayazit plain, near the Iranian border south of Mount Ararat.

name: Ararat
summary: Mount Ararat, also known as Agri Dagi, is Turkey's highest and largest volume volcano.

name: Elbrus
summary: Elbrus, the highest peak of the Caucasus Mountains of SW Russia, is a large glaciated stratovolcano.

name: Kazbek
summary: The glacier-covered Kazbek stratovolcano in the Caucasus Mountains of Georgia, just south of the border with Russia, has produced long lava flows down flank valleys.

name: Samsari Volcanic Center
summary: The Samsari Volcanic Center consists of more than 20 volcanoes extedning about 40 km N-S along the Samsari Ridge, part of the Dzhakheti Highland of southern Georgis, about 90 km WSW of Tbilisi.

name: Aragats
summary: Aragats is a large andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano in NW Armenia about 40 km NW of the capital city of Yerevan.

name: Ghegham Volcanic Ridge
summary: The Ghegham Volcanic Ridge, located in west-central Armenia between the capital city of Yerevan and Lake Sevan, contains as many as 127 volcanic centers, lava domes and pyroclastic cones, of Pleistocene-to-Holocene age.

name: Vaiyots-Sar
summary: The Vaiyots-Sar pyroclastic cone is located in the southern Armenia province of Vayots Dzor in the western Vardenis Volcanic Highland south of Lake Sevan (Karakhanian et al., 2002); previous names such as Dar-Alages or Daly-Tapa are of Russian origin.

name: Porak
summary: The mid-Pleistocene Porak volcano lies in the Vardenis volcanic highland about 20 km SE of Lake Sevan.

name: Tskhouk-Karckar
summary: The Tskhouk-Karckar volcano group of cones and lava flows is located in the NW and central part of the Syunik Volcanic Upland along the Armenia/Azerbaijan border about 60 km SE of Lake Sevan.

name: Tair, Jebel at
summary: The basaltic Jebel at Tair volcano rises from 1,200 m depth in the south-central Red Sea, forming an oval-shaped island about 3 km long.

name: Zubair Group
summary: The 5-km-long Jebel Zubair Island is the largest of a group of small islands and submerged shoals that rise from a shallow platform in the Red Sea rift.

name: Zukur
summary: Zukur (Zugar), the northernmost large island of the Zukur-Hanish island group in the southern Red Sea, is formed of Holocene basaltic pyroclastic cones and spatter cones that issued youthful-looking pahoehoe lava flows.

name: Hanish
summary: The Hanish Islands are formed from a series of volcanic vents along a NE-SW trend, and include the Holocene Great Hanish, Little Hanish, and many other small islands and submarine shoals.

name: Alid
summary: Alid is an isolated, dissected volcano in the central Danakil depression.

name: Dallol
summary: Numerous phreatic explosion craters are present across the Salt Plain NNE of the Erta Ale Range in one of the lowest areas of the desolate Danakil depression.

name: Gada Ale
summary: Gada Ale (also known as Kebrit Ale), the most prominent volcano at the northern end of the Erta Ale Range, is formed of interstratified lava flows and hyaloclastites.

name: Alu-Dalafilla
summary: The summit region of Alu, ~5 km NW of the Dalafilla stratovolcano, is an ellipsoidal volcanic horst, elongated NNW-SSE, and formed primarily of older basaltic lava flows.

name: Bora Ale
summary: Bora Ale is a complex volcano located near the center of the Erta Ale Range.

name: Erta Ale
summary: The Erta Ale basaltic shield volcano in Ethiopia has a 50-km-wide edifice that rises more than 600 m from below sea level in the Danakil depression.

name: Ale Bagu
summary: Ale Bagu, also known as Ummuna, is an elongated stratovolcano located SW of Erta Ale volcano.

name: Hayli Gubbi
summary: Hayli Gubbi is the southernmost volcano of the Erta Ale Range.

name: Dubbi
summary: Dubbi, located east of the Erta Ale Range and south of the crystalline basement rocks of the Danakil Alps, is a large volcanic massif that rises above the western shore of the Red Sea.

name: Nabro
summary: The Nabro stratovolcano is the highest volcano in the Danakil depression of northern Ethiopia and Eritrea, at the SE end of the Danakil Alps.

name: Mallahle
summary: Mallahle is the central of three NE-SW-trending stratovolcanoes (along with Asavyo and Nabro) in the Danakil horst SW of Dubbi volcano.

name: Sork Ale
summary: Sork Ale is a silicic stratovolcano located in the Danakil horst SW of Dubbi volcano.

name: Asavyo
summary: Asavyo, also known as Bara’Ale, is the SW-most of three large silicic stratovolcanoes (along with Mallahle and Nabro) constructed along a NE-SW-trending line in the Danakil horst.

name: Mat Ala
summary: Mat Ala is a low shield volcano in the southern Tat Ali Range, east of Afderà volcano.

name: Tat Ali
summary: Tat Ali volcano is the dominant feature of the Tat Ali Range, east of Lake Afrera.

name: Borawli
summary: Borawli stratovolcano rises above the eastern shore of Lake Afrera, also known as Lake Giulietti.

name: Afdera
summary: Afderà is an isolated rhyolitic stratovolcano located between the Erta Ale, Tat Ali, and Alayta ranges.

name: Ma Alalta
summary: The Ma Alalta stratovolcano, also known as Pierre Pruvost, is located well to the west of the Danakil depression at the foot of the regional Ethiopian scarp, between two large horsts of uplifted basement blocks.

name: Alayta
summary: The massive Alayta shield volcano covers an area of 2700 km2 in the western Danakil depression SW of Lake Afrera.

name: Dabbahu
summary: Dabbahu (also known as Boina, Boyna, or Moina) is a Pleistocene-to-Holocene volcanic massif forming an axial range of the Afar depression SSW of the Alayta massif.

name: Dabbayra
summary: Dabbayra, the westernmost volcano of the Afar depression, was constructed along an offshoot of the Ethiopian escarpment, SW of the Teru plain.

name: Manda Hararo
summary: As the southernmost axial range of western Afar, the Manda Hararo complex is located in the Kalo plain, SSE of Dabbahu volcano.

name: Groppo
summary: Groppo was identified by IAVCEI (1973) as a small alkali rhyolitic stratovolcano located in the western Afar near the Ethiopian escarpment, NE of Dessye.

name: Kurub
summary: The small Holocene shield volcano, also known as Kurub Koma, Kurub Koba, or Curub, lies in the Saha Plain, SE of the Manda Hararo complex in the South Danakil region.

name: Manda-Inakir
summary: Manda-Inakir consists of a series of NW-trending fissure vents and pyroclastic cones along the Ethiopia-Djibouti border.

name: Mousa Alli
summary: The Mousa Alli volcanic complex is a large Holocene stratovolcano constructed along the border between Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti.

name: Gufa
summary: The Gufa volcanic field, located along the Eritrea-Djibouti border, consists of a group of basaltic scoria cones and lava flows, aligned E-W, NE of the large Mousa Alli stratovolcano.

name: Assab Volcanic Field
summary: The Assab volcanic field near the Red Sea coast in southern Eritrea forms a spectacular range of basaltic cinder cones and associated lava flows.

name: Ardoukoba
summary: The Ardoukôba (Asal) Rift in Djibouti, trending NW from the Red Sea, contains a broad area of youthful fissure vents between Lake Asal and the Ghoubbat al Kharab gulf.

name: Manda Gargori
summary: The Manda Gargori rift, located north of the town of Aisa Aita NE of Borawli volcano and SE of Kurub volcano, is the youngest rift segment in the Afar depression and is only one third the width of the adjacent Manda Hararo-Goba'ad rift system to the west.

name: Dama Ali
summary: Dama Ali is a broad 25-km-wide shield volcano that rises above the NW shore of Lake Abbe in eastern Ethiopia.

name: Gabillema
summary: Gabillema is a rhyolitic stratovolcano along the axis of the Addado graben.

name: Yangudi
summary: Yangudi volcano, lying in the Addado graben of the northern Main Ethiopian Rift, is a complex rhyolitic stratovolcano with an elliptical summit caldera.

name: Ayelu
summary: Ayelu is a vegetated rhyolitic stratovolcano, located south of the Asbahri plain in the southern Afar region.

name: Adwa
summary: Adwa (also known as Aabida, Amoissa, or Dabita), is a broad stratovolcano in the southern Afar area immediately east of the younger vegetated Ayelu volcano.

name: Hertali
summary: Hertali is a basaltic fissure vent that fed lava flows at the S end of the Awash plain, about 50 km NNE of Dofen volcano.

name: Liado Hayk
summary: The Liado Hayk (Liado Lake) volcanic field consists of a dozen closely spaced maars and cinder cones with associated lava fields in the Awash plain NE of Dofen volcano.

name: Dofen
summary: The Dofen shield volcano rises 450 m above the Awash plain in the northern Main Ethiopian Rift.

name: Fentale
summary: Fentale is a volcanic complex at the N end of the Main Ethiopian Rift that includes a main stratovolcano and caldera with various subsidiary features.

name: Beru
summary: An area of Holocene basaltic lava flows is located along the Main Ethiopian Rift at Beru, between Fentale and Kone (Gariboldi) volcanoes.

name: Kone
summary: The Kone volcanic complex (also known as Gariboldi) is composed of a series of silicic calderas and young basaltic cinder cones and lava flows about 30 km SW of Fentale volcano in the Main Ethiopian Rift.

name: Boset
summary: The Boset volcanic complex includes the Boset-Gudda (Great Boset) and Boset-Bericha (Little Boset) composite volcanoes rising above the floor of the Ethiopian Rift valley.

name: Bishoftu Volcanic Field
summary: The Bishoftu volcanic field, also known as Debre Zeit, consists of an area of fissure-fed Holocene lava flows, cinder cones, tuff rings, and  maars.

name: Melkassa
summary: The Melkassa (or Sodore) volcanic field is an extensive 15 x 25 km group of about 30 Pleistocene and Holocene pyroclastic cones and lava flows that covers the floor of the E side of the Ethiopian Rift Valley, around the town of Melkassa, between the Boset….

name: Gedemsa
summary: The Gedemsa caldera covers 7 x 9 km along the Main Ethiopian Rift E of Lake Koka and SW of Wonji Sugar Estate Farm.

name: Bora-Bericha-Tullu Moye
summary: The Bora-Bericha-Tullu Moye (BBTM) volcanic complex includes three main silicic edifices and at least 11 smaller cones within the Main Ethiopian Rift.

name: East Ziway
summary: A large area of basaltic cinder cones and lava flows lies within about 5 km of the SE shore of Lake Ziway, and also forms islands along its E shore.

name: Butajiri-Silti Field
summary: The Butajiri-Silti volcanic field consists of a large group of basaltic cinder cones, maars, and lava flows in an 80-km-long, NE-SW-trending area near the western margin of the Ethiopian Rift.

name: Aluto
summary: Aluto, between lakes Zway and Langano (Mirrga), is a stratovolcano with multiple vents aligned along NNE-SSW and E-W fissures along a narrow graben between the two lakes.

name: Shala
summary: The Shala (also known as O'a) caldera along the central Main Ethiopian Rift forms the eastern portion of the 15 x 25 km Lake Shala.

name: Corbetti
summary: Corbetti is is one of the largest calderas (15.6 x 10.9 km) within the Main Ethiopian Rift (MER).

name: Bilate River Field
summary: The Bilate River basin west of Lake Awasa contains a group of lake-filled maars and tuff rings of Pleistocene and probable Holocene age (WoldeGabriel 1987, pers.

name: Northern Lake Abaya Volcanic Field
summary: The Northern Lake Abaya volcanic field consists primarily of small Quaternary cones and basaltic lava flows between Doguna volcano to the north, Chericha to the E, Lake Abaya to the south, and the Hobitcha caldera to the west.

name: Korath Range
summary: The Korath Range is an isolated group of about 20 tuff cones and lava flows in southern Ethiopia that were erupted along the Turkana Rift, which extends north from Kenya.

name: Mega Volcanic Field
summary: The Mega Volcanic Field in southern Ethiopia is present on both sides of the 100-km-long NW-SE Mega escarpment, and covers about 1,400 km2.

name: Lake Turkana North Island
summary: The 2-km-wide North Island in Lake Turkana is the northernmost and smallest of three volcanic islands in the lake.

name: Lake Turkana Central Island
summary: Central Island in the middle of Lake Turkana, also known as Crocodile Island, is composed of more than a dozen craters and cones, three of which are filled by small lakes.

name: Lake Turkana South Island
summary: The southernmost and largest of the three volcanic islands in Lake Turkana, South Island (sometimes referred to as Hohnel Island), contains numerous tuff cones.

name: Marsabit
summary: Marsabit is a massive basaltic shield volcano located 170 km E off the center of the East African Rift.

name: Barrier, The
summary: The Barrier volcanic complex separates Lake Turkana from the broad Suguta Trough to the S, the site of a former lake.

name: Namarunu
summary: The largely Pliocene Namarunu trachytic shield volcano is topped by cones and lava flows of upper Pleistocene and Holocene age.

name: Segererua Plateau
summary: A large number of late-Pleistocene to Holocene basaltic cones, lava flows, and maars occur along a roughly 50-km-long NE-SW trend on the Segererua and Rusarus Plateaus and areas to the SW.

name: Emuruangogolak
summary: The broad Emuruangogolak shield volcano is situated at a narrow constriction in the Gregory Rift and almost completely straddles it.

name: Silali
summary: The 30-km-wide Silali trachytic shield volcano, the largest Quaternary volcano in the northern Gregory Rift, completely straddles the East African Rift.

name: Paka
summary: The dominantly Pleistocene Paka shield volcano in the Gregory Rift contains a small 1.5-km-wide summit caldera.

name: Korosi
summary: The trachytic Korosi shield volcano lies at the N end of Lake Baringo.

name: Ol Kokwe
summary: The elongated Ol Kokwe Island in the center of Lake Baringo SW of Korosi volcano consists of young basaltic scoria cones that cap a trachytic shield volcano.

name: Nyambeni Hills
summary: The broad NE-SW-trending Nyambeni shield volcano is capped by numerous phonolitic lava domes, basaltic cones, and lava flows of late-Pleistocene to Holocene age (Hackman et al., 1989).

name: Menengai
summary: The massive Menengai shield volcano occupies the floor of the East African Rift.

name: Homa Mountain
summary: Homa Mountain is a large carbonatitic complex with a flat-topped summit that forms a broad peninsula on the E shore of Lake Victoria.

name: Elmenteita Badlands
summary: The Elmenteita Badlands, located between Lake Elmenteita (N) and Eburru volcano (S), is an area of pyroclastic cones and lava flows of varying ages.

name: Eburru, Ol Doinyo
summary: Eburru volcano is elongated E-W perpendicular to the Gregory Rift NW of Lake Naivasha.

name: Olkaria
summary: The Olkaria volcanic complex, located immediately S of Lake Naivasha and W of Longonot volcano, comprises up to 80 individual alkali rhyolite centers.

name: Longonot
summary: The trachytic Longonot stratovolcano SE of Lake Naivasha in the Gregory Rift valley contains a 8 x 12 km caldera.

name: Suswa
summary: The phonolitic-to-trachytic Suswa volcano in the Kenyan Rift, ~50 km WNW of Nairobi, is notable for its 8 x 12 km caldera.

name: Lengai, Ol Doinyo
summary: The symmetrical Ol Doinyo Lengai is the only volcano known to have erupted carbonatite tephras and lavas in historical time.

name: Chyulu Hills
summary: The 100-km-long NW-SE-trending Chyulu Hills volcanic field is located 150 km E of the Kenya Rift.

name: Meru
summary: Meru has a conical profile when viewed from the west, but there is a 4-km-wide collapse crater to the E.

name: Ngozi
summary: Ngozi caldera is the most prominent volcanic feature of the Poroto Ridge, a transverse structure at the northern end of the Karonga basin.

name: Rungwe
summary: Rungwe volcano, the largest in the Karonga basin NW of Lake Malawi (Lake Nyasa), is cut by a 4-km-wide caldera that is breached to the WSW.

name: Kyejo
summary: Late-stage activity of the Kyejo (Kieyo) trachytic stratovolcano, NW of Lake Malawi (Lake Nyassa), consisted of the formation of numerous maars and cinder cones.

name: Fort Portal Volcanic Field
summary: The carbonatite lavas and tuffs of the Fort Portal Volcanic Field in Uganda, NE of Mount Ruwenzori between Lake Albert and Lake Edward, consists of a group of tuff cones and maars covering an area of about 145 km2.

name: Ndali-Kasenda Volcanic Field
summary: The Ndali-Kasenda Volcanic Field (also known as Kwatya) is located in the Western Rift Valley, N of the equator and E of the Ruwenzori Mountains about halfway between Lake Edward and Lake Albert.

name: Nyamulagira
summary: Africa's most active volcano, Nyamulagira (also known as Nyamuragira), is a massive high-potassium basaltic shield about 25 km N of Lake Kivu and 13 km NNW of the steep-sided Nyiragongo volcano.

name: Nyiragongo
summary: The Nyiragongo stratovolcano contained a lava lake in its deep summit crater that was active for half a century before draining catastrophically through its outer flanks in 1977.

name: Karisimbi
summary: Karisimbi is a complex basanitic-to-trachytic volcano with a symmetrical sharp-peaked summit.

name: Mugogo
summary: The small Mugogo cone was built during a 1957 eruption.

name: Basile, Pico
summary: Pico Basilé is the largest and highest of three basaltic shield volcanoes forming Bioko Island.

name: Cameroon
summary: The massive steep-sided Mount Cameroon rises above the coast of west Cameroon, overlooking the Bight of Biafra, part of the Gulf of Guinea.

name: Tombel Graben
summary: Young cinder cones and maars are abundant in the low-lying Tombel Graben (also referred to as the Tombel Plain) between Mount Cameroon and Mount Manengouba (within 4°58'N, 9°51'E and 4°33'N, 9°35'E).

name: Oku Volcanic Field
summary: Numerous maars and basaltic cinder cones lie on or near the deeply dissected rhyolitic and trachytic Mount Oku massif along the Cameroon volcanic line.

name: Todra Volcanic Field
summary: The Todra Volcanic Field covers about 1,000 km2 in the Tuareg shield in the southern Aïr region of Niger.

name: Tahalra Volcanic Field
summary: The large E-W elongated Tahalra volcanic field covers an area of about 1,800 km2 in the Hoggar Province of southern Algeria.

name: Atakor Volcanic Field
summary: The massive Atakor volcanic field is the largest in the Hoggar (or Ahaggar) volcanic province of southern Algeria and covers an area of 2,150 km2.

name: Manzaz Volcanic Field
summary: The Manzaz volcanic field, north of the Atakor volcanic field in the Hoggar (Ahaggar) volcanic province of Algeria, consists of a large number of scoria cones and associated lava flows.

name: Toh, Tarso
summary: The Tarso Tôh Pleistocene-to-Holocene volcanic field in the NW part of the arid Tibesti Range of Chad contains 150 scoria cones and two maars.

name: Tousside, Tarso
summary: Tarso Toussidé, a broad volcanic massif at the western end of the Tibesti Range, is capped by the Toussidé stratovolcano, constructed at the western end of the 14-km-wide ignimbritic Pleistocene Yirrigue caldera.

name: Voon, Tarso
summary: The broad summit of Tarso Voon volcano, located in the west-central part of the Tibesti Range, is truncated by a shallow 14 x 18 km wide caldera.

name: Koussi, Emi
summary: The large Emi Koussi volcano at the SE end of the Tibesti Range, a 60 x 80 km massif constructed over a basement of Cretaceous and Paleozoic sandstones, forms the highest summit of the Sahara.

name: Marra, Jebel
summary: The most prominent feature of the vast Jebel Marra volcanic field, located in the Darfur province of western Sudan, is the youthful Deriba caldera.

name: Kutum Volcanic Field
summary: The basaltic Kutum volcanic field, in the northern Darfur area of western Sudan, is located SW of the larger Meidob volcanic field.

name: Meidob Volcanic Field
summary: The alkaline Meidob volcanic field in western Sudan, at the NE end of the Darfur volcanic province, covers an area of 5,000 km2 with nearly 700 Pliocene-to-Holocene vents.

name: Bayuda Volcanic Field
summary: The Bayuda volcanic field is located in the Bayuda Desert of NE Sudan, south of the major Abu Hamed bend of the Nile River about 300 km N of Khartoum.

name: Ash Shaam, Harrat
summary: The massive Harrat Ash Shaam volcanic province, which extends from Syria through Jordan and into northern Saudi Arabia, contains many smaller volcanic fields.

name: Lunayyir, Harrat
summary: Harrat Lunayyir is a basaltic volcanic field in NW Saudi Arabia, east of the Red Sea port of Umm Lajj.

name: Ithnayn, Harrat
summary: The 4000 km2 Harrat Ithnayn volcanic field contains scattered shield volcanoes and scoria cones.

name: Khaybar, Harrat
summary: Harrat Khaybar, one of Saudi Arabia's largest volcanic fields, covers an area of more than 14,000 km2 N of Madinah (Medina).

name: Rahat, Harrat
summary: Harrat Rahat, Saudi Arabia's largest lava field, covers 20,000 km2 and extends for 300 km S of Madinah (Medina).

name: Kishb, Harrat
summary: The 5,900 km3 Harrat Kishb volcanic field, located E of a N-S-trending line of volcanic fields in central Saudi Arabia, is comprised of basaltic scoria cones, tuff rings and maars, and phonolitic lava domes and flows.

name: Birk, Harrat al
summary: The Harrat al Birk volcanic field, also known as Harrat Hayil or Hubhub al Sheikh, is the only Saudi Arabian volcanic field that lies directly along the Red Sea coast.

name: Yar, Jabal
summary: Jabal Yar, the southernmost young volcanic field in Saudi Arabia, is a small olivine basaltic field along the Red Sea coast at the SW tip of Saudi Arabia.

name: Arhab, Harra of
summary: The Quaternary Harra of Arhab in Yemen, north of the capital city of Sana'a, consists of a 1,500 km2 basaltic plateau capped by a few small stratovolcanoes and about 60 scoria cones, two of which have erupted in historical time.

name: Haylan, Jabal
summary: The Jabal Haylan area contains a 75-km-long chain of tuff cones and associated olivine basaltic lava flows in eastern Yemen.

name: Dhamar, Harras of
summary: The lava fields surrounding the town of Dhamar are part of a volcanic field extending 80 km E that includes several stratovolcanoes and many youthful volcanic cones.

name: Sawad, Harra Es-
summary: The Harra es-Sawâd (or Shuqra) volcanic field in southern Yemen extends for nearly 100 km along the Gulf of Aden, east of the city of Shuqra (Shaqra).

name: Balhaf-Bir Ali Volcanic Field
summary: The Balhaf-Bir Ali Volcanic Field along the Gulf of Aden in southern Yemen contains cinder cones associated with vesicular lava flows and scoria cones.

name: Bir Borhut
summary: Near the villages of Hleime and Al Ghayl, along the Wadi Hadhramout valley about 45 km from the coast of Yemen, is what appears to be a pyroclastic volcanic cone and extensive dark lava flows.

name: Damavand
summary: The Damavand stratovolcano is located 70 km NE of Iran's capital city of Tehran and 70 km S of the Caspian Sea.

name: Grille, La
summary: La Grille is a basaltic shield volcano at the N end of Grand Comore Island (Ngazidja).

name: Mayotte
summary: Mayotte, located in the Mozambique Channel between the northern tip of Madagascar and the eastern coast of Africa, consists two main volcanic islands, Grande Terre and Petite Terre, and roughly twenty islets within a barrier-reef lagoon complex (Zinke et….

name: Karthala
summary: The southernmost and largest of the two shield volcanoes forming Grand Comore Island (also known as Ngazidja Island), Karthala has two overlapping 3-4 km summit calderas generated by repeated collapse.

name: Fournaise, Piton de la
summary: Piton de la Fournaise is a massive basaltic shield volcano on the French island of Réunion in the western Indian Ocean.

name: Fani Maore
summary: Activity that began in May 2018 consisted of seismicity and ground deformation occurring offshore E of Mayotte Island (Lemoine et al., 2019).

name: Boomerang Seamount
summary: Boomerang Seamount, an active submarine volcano 18 km NE of Amsterdam Island, was first discovered during a bathymetric survey in 1996.

name: Amsterdam Island
summary: The elliptical 7 x 10 km Amsterdam Island is the northernmost subaerial volcano on the Antarctic Plate.

name: St. Paul
summary: The uninhabited triangular island of St.

name: Heard
summary: Heard Island on the Kerguelen Plateau in the southern Indian Ocean consists primarily of the emergent portion of two volcanic structures.

name: McDonald Islands
summary: The McDonald Islands are located on the Kerguelen Plateau about 75 km W of Heard Island.

name: Kerguelen Islands
summary: The Kerguelen Islands are composed primarily of Tertiary flood basalts and a complex of plutonic rocks.

name: Est, Ile de l'
summary: Ile de l'Est, the easternmost island in the Crozet archipelago, is a glacially eroded basaltic stratovolcano.

name: Possession, Ile de la
summary: Île de la Possession, located immediately W of Ile de l'Est in the Crozet archipelago, consists of a stratovolcano intruded by ring and cone dikes and modified by block faulting, marine erosion, and uplift.

name: Cochons, Ile aux
summary: The 8 x 10 km Ile aux Cochons, at the W end of the Crozet Islands, is a single stratovolcano with a small summit caldera and more than 60 scoria cones.

name: Prince Edward Island
summary: Uninhabited 5 x 10-km-wide Prince Edward Island lies opposite Marion Island at the N end of a submarine plateau on the Antarctic Plate immediately S of the SW Indian Ocean Ridge.

name: Marion Island
summary: Marion Island lies at the SW end of a submarine plateau immediately south of the SW Indian Ocean Ridge, opposite Prince Edward Island.

name: Auckland Volcanic Field
summary: The 600 km2 Auckland Volcanic Field, at the south end of the Northland Peninsula, is overlain by New Zealand's largest city, Auckland / Tamaki Makaurau.

name: Tuhua/Mayor Island
summary: The 4-km-wide Tuhua/Mayor Island, offshore of North Island in the Bay of Plenty, is the emergent portion of a 15-km-wide peralkaline shield volcano constructed between about 120,000 and 35,000 years ago.

name: Taranaki
summary: The nearly symmetrical, steep-sided cone of Taranaki (previously known as Egmont), is a large andesitic stratovolcano on the west coast of central North Island.

name: Whakaari/White Island
summary: The uninhabited Whakaari/White Island is the 2 x 2.4 km emergent summit of a 16 x 18 km submarine volcano in the Bay of Plenty about 50 km offshore of North Island.

name: Okataina
summary: The massive, dominantly rhyolitic Okataina Volcanic Centre (OVC) is surrounded by extensive ignimbrite and pyroclastic sheets produced during multiple caldera-forming eruptions.

name: Taupo
summary: Taupo, the most active rhyolitic volcano of the Taupo volcanic zone, is a large, roughly 35-km-wide caldera with poorly defined margins.

name: Tongariro
summary: Tongariro is a large volcanic massif, located immediately NE of Ruapehu volcano, that is composed of more than a dozen composite cones constructed over a period of 275,000 years.

name: Ruapehu
summary: Ruapehu, one of New Zealand's most active volcanoes, is a complex stratovolcano constructed during at least four cone-building episodes dating back to about 200,000 years ago.

name: Clark
summary: The submarine Clark stratovolcano lies near the southern end of the Southern Kermadec arc.

name: Tangaroa
summary: Tangaroa submarine volcano in the southern Kermadec arc rises to within 600 m of the ocean surface.

name: Rumble V
summary: Rumble V was discovered in 1992 at the southernmost end of the Rumble seamounts on the southern Kermadec Ridge, 17 km ESE of Rumble IV.

name: Rumble IV
summary: The submarine Rumble IV volcano was thought to have been active from April to December 1966, based on hydrophone signals (Kibblewhite, 1967), but later evidence indicated that the hydrophone array had been damaged and the signals originated from Rumble III….

name: Rumble III
summary: Rumble III seamount, the largest of the Rumbles group of submarine volcanoes along the South Kermadec Ridge, rises 2,300 m from the seafloor to within about 200 m of the surface.

name: Rumble II West
summary: Rumble II West, about 12 km NW of Rumble II East, rises 1,800 m from the ocean floor to within 1,200 m of the surface.

name: Healy
summary: Healy submarine volcano lies along the South Kermadec Ridge and consists of an elongated edifice with a 3 x 4 km wide caldera at the NE end whose rim reaches to 1,150 m below sea level.

name: Brothers
summary: The submarine Brothers volcano, located NE of the Healy submarine volcano, contains an oval-shaped summit caldera 3-3.5 km elongated NW-SE.

name: Wright
summary: Two volcanic cones, initially known informally as Volcano W and later named Wright, were discovered during a New Zealand-American submarine vent mapping expedition to the Kermadec arc in 2004.

name: Havre Seamount
summary: Havre Seamount has a caldera capping a 1-km-high edifice.

name: Curtis Island
summary: Curtis and nearby Cheeseman Islands are the emergent portions of a submarine volcano along the Kermadec Ridge.

name: Macauley
summary: Macauley Island is a rim remnant of a large submarine caldera centered 8 km to the NW.

name: Giggenbach
summary: Giggenbach, named after volcano gas geochemist Werner Giggenbach, is a basaltic-to-dacitic submarine volcano about 30 km NW of Macauley volcano.

name: Raoul Island
summary: Anvil-shaped Raoul Island is the largest and northernmost of the Kermadec Islands.

name: Monowai
summary: Monowai, also known as Orion seamount, is a basaltic stratovolcano that rises from a depth of about 1,500 to within 100 m of the ocean surface about halfway between the Kermadec and Tonga island groups, at the southern end of the Tonga Ridge.

name: Kermadec Arc at 24.8°S
summary: A large submarine volcano in the Northern Kermadec Arc, ~120 km N of Monowai, is known informally as Volcano 19 from a research cruise designation.

name: Tofua Arc at 21.3°S
summary: During a submarine eruption in 1907 pyroclastic material was ejected to 100 m above the ocean surface, and pumice rafts were produced.

name: Tofua Arc at 21.1°S
summary: A large submarine volcano rises to within 65 m of the ocean surface west of Tongatapu Island.

name: Tofua Arc at 20.9°S
summary: An unnamed submarine volcano is located along the Tofua Volcanic Arc 35 km NW of the Niu Aunofo lighthouse on Tongatapu Island.

name: Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai
summary: The small andesitic islands of Hunga Tonga and Hunga Ha'apai are part of the western and northern remnants of the rim (~6 km diameter) of a largely submarine caldera located about 30 km SSE of Falcon Island.

name: Fonuafo'ou
summary: The ephemeral Fonuafo'ou island in the central part of the Tonga Islands is also known as Falcon Island, named after the British vessel H.M.S.

name: Tofua
summary: The low, forested Tofua Island in the central part of the Tonga Islands group is the emergent summit of a large stratovolcano that was seen in eruption by Captain Cook in 1774.

name: Kao
summary: The symmetrical Kao rises steeply from the ocean about 6 km N of Tofua Island in Tonga.

name: Lateiki
summary: Lateiki, previously known as Metis Shoal, is a submarine volcano midway between the islands of Kao and Late that has produced a series of ephemeral islands since the first confirmed activity in the mid-19th century.

name: Home Reef
summary: Home Reef, a submarine volcano midway between Metis Shoal and Late Island in the central Tonga islands, was first reported active in the mid-19th century, when an ephemeral island formed.

name: Late
summary: The 6-km-wide circular island of Late, along the Tofua volcanic arc about 55 km WSW of Vavau, contains a 400-m-wide, 150-m-deep summit crater with an ephemeral lake.

name: Tofua Arc at 18.3°S
summary: A submarine volcano along the Tofua Volcanic Arc ~45 km NW of Vava'u Island was first observed in September 2001, ~35 km S of Fonualei and 60 km NE of Late volcano.

name: Fonualei
summary: The small island of Fonualei (~2 km diameter) contains a fumarolically active crater breached to the SE with a fresh lava flow extending to the sea and forming a rugged shoreline.

name: Tafahi
summary: The small 1.2 x 2.8 km island of Tafahi is a conical stratovolcano about 7 km N of the island of Niuatoputapu in the northern Tonga Islands.

name: Curacoa
summary: A submarine volcano south of Curacoa Reef at the northern end of the Tofua volcanic arc was first observed in eruption in 1973.

name: Niuafo'ou
summary: Niuafo'ou ("Tin Can Island") is a low 8-km-wide island that forms the summit of a largely submerged basaltic shield volcano in the north central Lau Basin about 170 km W of the northern end of the Tofua volcanic arc.

name: Dugong
summary: This volcano was discovered during an Australian research cruise in 2008.

name: Lobster
summary: Active hydrothermal venting was noted when this volcano was first discovered in 2008 by an Australian research expedition.

name: Tafu-Maka
summary: Two submarine volcanoes, Tafu and Maka, lie along a NE-SW-trending ridge segment in the southern part of the NE Lau Spreading Center (NELSC).

name: West Mata
summary: West Mata, a submarine volcano rising to within 1,174 m of the ocean surface, is located in the northeastern Lau Basin at the northern end of the Tofua arc, about 200 km SW of Samoa and north of the Curacoa submarine volcano.

name: Niuatahi
summary: Niuatahi is a nearly circular caldera ~15 km in diameter, with a floor at a depth of about 2 km (Arculus, 2012).

name: Vailulu'u
summary: Vailulu'u, a massive basaltic seamount discovered in 1975, rises 4,200 m from the sea floor to a depth of 590 m.

name: Ta'u
summary: The 10-km-wide Ta'u Island, located at the E end of the Samoan islands, is ringed by sea cliffs.

name: Ofu-Olosega
summary: The two triangle-shaped islands of Ofu and Olosega in eastern Samoa, with a combined length of 6 km, are separated by a narrow strait.

name: Tutuila
summary: The elongated, extensively eroded Tutuila Island in the center of the Samoan Islands consists of five Pliocene-to-Pleistocene volcanoes constructed along two or three rifts trending SSW-NNE.

name: Malumalu
summary: The Malumalu seamount (also called Southeast Bank) is about 50 km SW of Ta'u Island and 90 km SSE of Tutuila in the Samoan Islands.

name: Upolu
summary: The massive, basaltic shield volcano forming 75-km-long Upolu Island in Samoa is elongated in an E-W direction and was constructed during two periods of extensive eruptions during the Pliocene and Pleistocene.

name: Savaii
summary: Savai'i, the largest and highest of the Samoan islands, consists of a massive basaltic shield volcano constructed along a WNW-ESE-trending rift zone that splits into two rifts on the east side of the 75-km-long, oval-shaped island.

name: Taveuni
summary: Taveuni, the third largest of the Fiji islands, is known as the "Garden Island" due to its rich volcanic soils.

name: Nabukelevu
summary: The andesitic-to-dacitic Nabukelevu lava-dome complex occupies the SW end of Kadavu Island at the S end of the Fiji archipelago.

name: St. Andrew Strait
summary: The St.

name: Central Bismarck Sea
summary: SOFAR signals resembling those produced at known submarine eruptions were recorded in January 1972 in the central Bismarck Sea (Johnson et al., 1981).

name: Blup Blup
summary: The 2 x 3.5 km forested island of Blup Blup contains lava flows with well-defined flow fronts.

name: Kadovar
summary: The 2-km-wide island of Kadovar is the emergent summit of a Bismarck Sea stratovolcano of Holocene age.

name: Bam
summary: The 1.6 x 2.4 km island of Bam is the summit of a mostly submerged volcano in the Schouten Islands off the coast of New Guinea, ~40 km NNE of the mouth of the Sepik River.

name: Manam
summary: The 10-km-wide island of Manam, lying 13 km off the northern coast of mainland Papua New Guinea, is one of the country's most active volcanoes.

name: Karkar
summary: Karkar is a 19 x 25 km forest-covered island that is truncated by two nested summit calderas.

name: Hankow Reef
summary: Oral tradition suggests the possible existence of a now-submerged volcano off the coast of Papua New Guinea.

name: Long Island
summary: The broad profile of Long Island is dominated by two steep-sided stratovolcanoes, Mount Reaumur in the north and Cerisy Peak in the south.

name: Umboi
summary: Umboi Island, 50 km in its longest dimension, is the largest of the volcanic islands off the N coast of New Guinea.

name: Ritter Island
summary: Prior to 1888, Ritter Island was a steep-sided, nearly circular island about 780 m high between Umboi and Sakar Islands.

name: Sakar
summary: Sakar is an incised stratovolcano with a summit crater lake.

name: Langila
summary: Langila, one of the most active volcanoes of New Britain, consists of a group of four small overlapping composite basaltic-andesitic cones on the lower E flank of the extinct Talawe volcano in the Cape Gloucester area of NW New Britain.

name: Dakataua
summary: The 10.5 x 13.5 km Dakataua caldera anchors the northern tip of the Willaumez Peninsula of New Britain.

name: Bola
summary: Bola volcano (also known as Wangore) is a symmetrical stratovolcano located immediately SW of Dakataua caldera on the Willaumez Peninsula.

name: Garua Harbour
summary: The Garua (Talasea) Harbour volcanic field consists of a group of lava domes and ash cones of possible Holocene age.

name: Krummel-Garbuna-Welcker
summary: The basaltic-to-dacitic Krummel-Garbuna-Welcker Volcanic Complex consists of three volcanic peaks located along a 7-km N-S line above a shield-like foundation at the southern end of the Willaumez Peninsula.

name: Lolo
summary: Lolo is a nearly symmetrical andesitic stratovolcano, ~3.5 km in diameter, located N of Witori volcano along the N coast of New Britain near Cape Hoskins.

name: Witori
summary: The active Pago cone has grown within the Witori caldera (5.5 x 7.5 km) on the northern coast of central New Britain contains the active Pago cone.

name: Sulu Range
summary: The Sulu Range consists of a cluster of partially overlapping small stratovolcanoes and lava domes in north-central New Britain off Bangula Bay.

name: Hargy
summary: This little-known volcano is one of several major calderas on the island of New Britain.

name: Bamus
summary: Symmetrical Bamus volcano, also referred to locally as the South Son, is located SW of Ulawun volcano, known as the Father.

name: Ulawun
summary: The symmetrical basaltic-to-andesitic Ulawun stratovolcano is the highest volcano of the Bismarck arc, and one of Papua New Guinea's most frequently active.

name: Lolobau
summary: Lolobau volcano has grown over the W rim of a 6-km-wide caldera which formed about 12,000 years ago.

name: Rabaul
summary: The low-lying Rabaul caldera on the tip of the Gazelle Peninsula at the NE end of New Britain forms a broad sheltered harbor utilized by what was the island's largest city prior to a major eruption in 1994.

name: Tavui
summary: The mostly submarine Tavui caldera lies off the NE tip of the Gazelle Peninsula north of Rabaul caldera.

name: Lamington
summary: Lamington is an andesitic stratovolcano with a 1.3-km-wide breached summit crater containing a lava dome that rises above the coastal plain of the Papuan Peninsula of New Guinea north of the Owen Stanley Range.

name: Hydrographers Range
summary: The Hydrographers Range is a forested, deeply dissected andesitic volcanic massif extending from the eastern margin of Mount Lamington north to the coast of eastern Papua New Guinea.

name: Managlase Plateau
summary: Thirty small volcanic centers of late-Pleistocene to Holocene age are located in SE Papua New Guinea on the Managlase Plateau, south of the Hydrographers Range and SW of the Dyke Ackland Bay.

name: Victory
summary: The dominantly andesitic Mount Victory stratovolcano, forming part of Cape Nelson on the NE coast of Papua New Guinea, is covered by rainforest.

name: Sessagara Hills
summary: The small low-lying andesitic Sessagara Hills volcanic field is located near the mouth of the Uiaka River, south of Collingwood Bay and NE of the Goropu Mountains on the Papuan Peninsula of New Guinea.

name: Goodenough
summary: Goodenough is a roughly circular volcanic island that is the westernmost of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands off the NE tip of Papua New Guinea.

name: Iamalele
summary: Multiple volcanic features and active thermal areas are located on the SW part of Fergusson Island, in the center of the D'Entrecasteaux island group.

name: Dawson Strait Group
summary: The Dawson Straits, located between eastern Fergusson and western Normanby Islands in the D'Entrecasteaux island group, contains a volcanic field with several centers that define a possible partly submerged caldera.

name: Balbi
summary: The complex andesitic Balbi stratovolcano on Bougainville Island includes a large number of coalesced cones and lava domes.

name: Billy Mitchell
summary: Billy Mitchell, a small pyroclastic shield immediately NE of Bagana volcano, has produced some of the largest Holocene eruptions in Papua New Guinea.

name: Bagana
summary: Bagana volcano, in a remote portion of central Bougainville Island, is frequently active.

name: Takuan Group
summary: The Takuan volcano group in southern Bougainville Island consists of three closely spaced, NW-SE-trending andesitic-dacitic stratovolcanoes.

name: Loloru
summary: Loloru, the SE-most volcano on Bougainville Island, is the source of a broad ignimbrite apron that covers much of the southern part of the island.

name: Simbo
summary: Simbo is a small island in the western Solomons with three truncated andesitic volcanic centers.

name: Kana Keoki
summary: Bathymetry and petrologic evidence indicated the presence of an active dacitic submarine volcano SW of Rendova Island (Taylor, 1987).

name: Coleman Seamount
summary: The research vessel "Moana Wave" (University of Hawaii) discovered a young submarine volcano SE of Kana Keoki seamount during a November 1985 to January 1986 cruise.

name: Kavachi
summary: Named for a sea-god of the Gatokae and Vangunu peoples, Kavachi is located in the Solomon Islands south of Vangunu Island.

name: New Georgia at 8.9°S
summary: An unnamed seamount was mapped during a 1979 cruise about 9 km NE of Kavachi (Okugrin, 1985), near the SE end of the New Georgia Islands at about 8.9°S.

name: Savo
summary: The 6 x 7 km island of Savo, off the NE coast of Guadalcanal Island, consists of a forested andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano with a shallow, elliptical 1 x 1.5 km summit crater.

name: Tinakula
summary: The small 3.5-km-wide island of Tinakula is the exposed summit of a massive stratovolcano at the NW end of the Santa Cruz islands.

name: Motlav
summary: The elongated island of Motlav, also referred to as Mota Lava, is comprised of at least five Pleistocene basaltic stratovolcanoes capped by two well-preserved late-Pleistocene to Holocene pyroclastic cones, Tuntog and Vetnam.

name: Suretamatai
summary: Suretamatai volcano (also known as Soritimeat) forms much of Vanua Lava Island, one of the largest of Vanuatu's Banks Islands.

name: Gaua
summary: The roughly 20-km-diameter Gaua Island, also known as Santa Maria, consists of a basaltic-to-andesitic stratovolcano with an 6 x 9 km summit caldera.

name: Ambae
summary: The island of Ambae, also known as Aoba, is a massive 2,500 km3 basaltic shield that is the most voluminous volcano of the New Hebrides archipelago.

name: Ambrym
summary: Ambrym is a large basaltic volcano with a 12-km-wide caldera formed during a major Plinian eruption with dacitic pyroclastic flows about 1,900 years ago.

name: Lopevi
summary: The small 7-km-wide conical island of Lopevi, known locally as Vanei Vollohulu, is one of Vanuatu's most active volcanoes.

name: East Epi
summary: The submarine East Epi group of basaltic and dacitic cones are located within a possible 10-km-diameter caldera off the NE coast of southern Epi Island in Vanuatu.

name: Kuwae
summary: The largely submarine Kuwae caldera occupies the area between Epi and Tongoa islands.

name: Nguna-Emau
summary: The islands of Nguna, Pele, and Emau (or Emao), north of Efaté Island (also known as Vate), have been variously mapped as Pleistocene and Pleistocene to Holocene.

name: Traitor's Head
summary: The Traitor's Head peninsula north of Cook Bay on eastern Erromango Island is comprised of three Holocene volcanic cones that are the youngest on the 50-km-long island.

name: Yasur
summary: Yasur has exhibited essentially continuous Strombolian and Vulcanian activity at least since Captain Cook observed ash eruptions in 1774.

name: Gemini-Oscostar
summary: The submarine Gemini-Oscostar volcanic field lies near the southern end of the Vanuatu (or New Hebrides) Volcanic Arc, ~100 km S of Aneityum Island.

name: Matthew Island
summary: Matthew Island is composed of two low andesitic-to-dacitic cones separated by a narrow isthmus.

name: Hunter Island
summary: Hunter Island, the SE-most volcano of the New Hebrides arc, is a 1-km-wide island consisting of a composite andesitic-to-dacitic cone topped by explosion craters and a lava dome.

name: Newer Volcanics Province
summary: The voluminous Newer Volcanics Province covers a broad 15,000 km2 area of SE Australia with nearly 400 small shield volcanoes and explosive vents of Tertiary-to-Holocene age.

name: McBride Volcanic Province
summary: An area of around 5,500 km2 is covered by the broad lava plains and cones of the McBride Volcanic Province.

name: Barren Island
summary: Barren Island, a possession of India in the Andaman Sea about 135 km NE of Port Blair in the Andaman Islands, is the only historically active volcano along the N-S volcanic arc extending between Sumatra and Burma (Myanmar).

name: Peuet Sague
summary: Peuet Sague is a large volcanic complex in NW Sumatra.

name: Telong, Bur ni
summary: The conical Bur ni Telong volcano was constructed at the southern base of the massive Bur ni Geureudong volcanic complex, one of the largest in northern Sumatra.

name: Singkut
summary: The Quaternary Singkut caldera is about 7 x 4 km with the S half of the rim topographically distinct.

name: Sinabung
summary: Gunung Sinabung is a Pleistocene-to-Holocene stratovolcano with many lava flows on its flanks.

name: Sorikmarapi
summary: Sorikmarapi is a forested stratovolcano with a 600-m-wide summit crater containing a lake and substantial sulfur deposits.

name: Malintang
summary: The broad forested Malintang andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano has an irregular summit crater with a 900 x 1,500 m lake.

name: Talakmau
summary: The Talakmau (also known as Talamau) volcano rises above the western coastal plain of Sumatra about 70 km NW of Marapi.

name: Marapi
summary: Gunung Marapi, not to be confused with the better-known Merapi volcano on Java, is Sumatra's most active volcano.

name: Tandikat-Singgalang
summary: This volcanic complex is dominated by the Singgalang stratovolcano and the smaller Tandikat edifice ~4.5 km SSW.

name: Talang
summary: Talang is part of a large volcanic edifice just NW of Dibawah Lake.

name: Kerinci
summary: Gunung Kerinci in central Sumatra forms Indonesia's highest volcano and is one of the most active in Sumatra.

name: Sumbing
summary: Smaller than its prominent namesake on Java, Sumatra's Sumbing volcano has a complicated summit region containing several crater remnants and a 180-m-long crater lake.

name: Kaba
summary: The Kaba volcanic massif is ~8 km long, elongated WSW-ENE, with a summit area that includes multiple large craters.

name: Dempo
summary: Dempo is a stratovolcano that rises above the Pasumah Plain of SE Sumatra.

name: Patah
summary: Patah is a heavily forested, dissected Quaternary volcano SE of Dempo volcano.

name: Ranau
summary: Ranau is an 8 x 13 km Pleistocene caldera partially filled by the crescent-shaped Lake Ranau.

name: Suoh
summary: The 8 x 16 km Suoh (or Suwoh) depression appears to have a dominantly tectonic origin, but contains a smaller complex of overlapping calderas oriented NNE-SSW.

name: Krakatau
summary: The renowned Krakatau (frequently misnamed as Krakatoa) volcano lies in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra.

name: Pulosari
summary: The basaltic-to-andesitic Pulosari stratovolcano at the western end of Java lies south of the 15-km-wide Pleistocene Danau caldera.

name: Karang
summary: Gunung Karang volcano in westernmost Java was constructed SE of the 15-km-wide Pleistocene Danau caldera.

name: Perbakti-Gagak
summary: The Perbakti-Gagak volcanic complex, also known as Kiaraberes-Gagak, is a cluster of deeply eroded stratovolcanoes situated immediately SW of Salak volcano.

name: Salak
summary: The forested Salak volcano was constructed at the NE end of an eroded volcanic range.

name: Gede-Pangrango
summary: The two peaks of the Gede-Pangrango volcanic complex overlook the major cities of Cianjur, Sukabumi, and Bogor, situated to the E, S, and NW, respectively.

name: Patuha
summary: The forested andesitic Gunung Patuha rises SW of the plain of Bandung in western Java.

name: Tangkuban Parahu
summary: Gunung Tangkuban Parahu is a broad stratovolcano overlooking Indonesia's former capital city of Bandung.

name: Papandayan
summary: Papandayan is a complex stratovolcano at the S end of a curved volcanic massif with Kendang volcano ~9 km away at the N end, Gunung Puntang ~3.5 km NNE, and Gunung Jaya ~6 km NNE.

name: Guntur
summary: Guntur is a complex of several overlapping stratovolcanoes about 10 km NW of the city of Garut in western Java.

name: Tampomas
summary: Gunung Tampomas is an andesitic stratovolcano overlooking the northern coastal plain of western Java about halfway between Tangkubanparahu and Cereme volcanoes.

name: Galunggung
summary: The forested slopes of Galunggung in western Java SE of Bandung are cut by a 2-km-wide collapse scarp open towards the ESE.

name: Talagabodas
summary: The Gunung Talagabodas stratovolcano lies immediately north of the more well-known Galunggung volcano.

name: Ciremai
summary: The symmetrical Ciremai stratovolcano is located closer to the northern coast than other central Java volcanoes.

name: Slamet
summary: Slamet is one of Java's most active volcanoes.

name: Dieng Volcanic Complex
summary: The Dieng plateau in the highlands of central Java is renowned both for the variety of its volcanic scenery and as a sacred area housing Java's oldest Hindu temples, dating back to the 9th century CE.

name: Sundoro
summary: Gunung Sundoro, in central Java, is located between the Dieng complex to the NW and Sumbing volcano to the SE.

name: Sumbing
summary: Gunung Sumbing is a stratovolcano that is the SE-most edifice of a chain of volcanoes in central Java that includes Sundoro and the Dieng Complex.

name: Merbabu
summary: Gunung Merbabu is a massive forested volcano north of Merapi in central Java.

name: Merapi
summary: Merapi, one of Indonesia's most active volcanoes, lies in one of the world's most densely populated areas and dominates the landscape immediately north of the major city of Yogyakarta.

name: Lawu
summary: The Lawu volcanic complex includes a deeply eroded volcano to the south joined to a younger edifice to the north considered by van Bemmelen (1949b) to be probably Holocene.

name: Kelud
summary: The relatively inconspicuous Kelud stratovolcano contains a summit crater lake that has been the source of some of Indonesia's most deadly eruptions.

name: Kawi-Butak
summary: The broad Kawi-Butak volcanic massif lies immediately E of Kelut volcano and S of Arjuno-Welirang volcano.

name: Arjuno-Welirang
summary: The Arjuno and Welirang volcanoes anchor the SE and NW ends, respectively, of a 6-km-long line of volcanic cones and craters.

name: Penanggungan
summary: Gunung Penanggungan, one of Java's most revered mountains, is a small stratovolcano immediately north of the Arjuno-Welirang massif.

name: Semeru
summary: Semeru, the highest volcano on Java, and one of its most active, lies at the southern end of a volcanic massif extending north to the Tengger caldera.

name: Tengger Caldera
summary: The 16-km-wide Tengger caldera is located at the northern end of a volcanic massif extending from Semeru volcano.

name: Lamongan
summary: Lamongan, a small stratovolcano located between the massive Tengger and Iyang-Argapura volcanic complexes, is surrounded by numerous maars and cinder cones.

name: Iyang-Argapura
summary: The massive Iyang-Argapura volcanic complex dominates the landscape between Raung and Lamongan volcanoes in eastern Java.

name: Raung
summary: Raung, one of Java's most active volcanoes, is a massive stratovolcano in easternmost Java that was constructed SW of the rim of Ijen caldera.

name: Ijen
summary: The Ijen volcano complex at the eastern end of Java consists of a group of small stratovolcanoes constructed within the 20-km-wide Ijen (Kendeng) caldera.

name: Baluran
summary: The small andesitic Baluran, dwarfed by its neighbor Ijen volcano to the SW, occupies the very NE tip of Java.

name: Buyan-Bratan
summary: The most obvious feature of the Buyan-Bratan volcanic complex in north-central Bali is the 11 x 6 km wide Bratan caldera (also known as Catur or Tjatur caldera), which contains three caldera lakes.

name: Batur
summary: The historically active Batur is located at the center of two concentric calderas NW of Agung volcano.

name: Agung
summary: Symmetrical Agung stratovolcano, Bali's highest and most sacred mountain, towers over the eastern end of the island.

name: Rinjani
summary: Rinjani volcano on the island of Lombok rises to 3726 m, second in height among Indonesian volcanoes only to Sumatra's Kerinci volcano.

name: Tambora
summary: The massive Tambora stratovolcano forms the entire 60-km-wide Sanggar Peninsula on northern Sumbawa Island.

name: Sangeang Api
summary: Sangeang Api volcano, one of the most active in the Lesser Sunda Islands, forms a small 13-km-wide island off the NE coast of Sumbawa Island.

name: Sano, Wai
summary: The Wai Sano composite volcano at the western end of Flores Island includes a 2.5 x 3.5 km elliptical caldera in the NW part of a larger 9-10 km edifice.

name: Ranakah
summary: The Anak Ranakah (Child of Ranakah) lava dome was formed in 1987 in an area without previous recorded eruptions at the base of the large older lava dome of Gunung Ranakah.

name: Inierie
summary: The symmetrical Gunung Inierie stratovolcano in south-central Flores overlooks the Sawu Sea, and is the highest volcano on the island.

name: Inielika
summary: Inielika is a broad, low volcano in central Flores Island that was constructed within the Lobobutu caldera.

name: Ebulobo
summary: Ebulobo, also referred to as Amburombu or Keo Peak, is a steep-sided symmetrical stratovolcano in central Flores Island.

name: Iya
summary: Gunung Iya is the southernmost of a group of three volcanoes comprising a small peninsula south of the city of Ende on central Flores Island.

name: Kelimutu
summary: Kelimutu is a small, but well-known, Indonesian compound volcano in central Flores Island with three summit crater lakes of varying colors.

name: Paluweh
summary: Paluweh, also known as Rokatenda, forms the 8-km-wide island of Palu'e north of the volcanic arc that cuts across Flores Island.

name: Egon
summary: Gunung Egon, also known as Namang, sits within the narrow section of eastern Flores Island.

name: Lewotobi
summary: The Lewotobi edifice in eastern Flores Island is composed of the two adjacent Lewotobi Laki-laki and Lewotobi Perempuan stratovolcanoes (the "husband and wife").

name: Iliboleng
summary: Iliboleng stratovolcano was constructed at the SE end of Adonara Island across a narrow strait from Lomblen Island.

name: Lewotolok
summary: The Lewotolok (or Lewotolo) stratovolcano occupies the eastern end of an elongated peninsula extending north into the Flores Sea, connected to Lembata (formerly Lomblen) Island by a narrow isthmus.

name: Ililabalekan
summary: Ililabalekan volcano is situated on a prominent peninsula in SW Lembata (formerly Lomblen) Island.

name: Iliwerung
summary: Constructed on the southern rim of the Lerek caldera, Iliwerung forms a prominent south-facing peninsula on Lembata (formerly Lomblen) Island.

name: Tara, Batu
summary: The small isolated island of Batu Tara in the Flores Sea ~50 km N of Lembata (fomerly Lomblen) Island and the main volcanic arc.

name: Sirung
summary: Sirung is located at the NE end of a volcanic massif with multiple centers that extends 14 km NE from the southern end of Pantar Island.

name: Wurlali
summary: The andesitic Wurlali stratovolcano was constructed at the northern end of a 5-km-wide caldera on the eastern side of Damar Island in the Banda Sea.

name: Teon
summary: Teon, an elongated andesitic island volcano in the southwestern Banda arc, is also known as Serawerna, the name of its active crater.

name: Nila
summary: The 5 x 6 km Nila Island in the Banda Sea is comprised of a low-rimmed caldera breached at sea level on the south and east, with a youthful forested cone.

name: Serua
summary: The 2 x 4 km island of Serua is the emergent summit of a volcano rising 3,600 m above the Banda Sea floor.

name: Manuk
summary: The small steep-sided island of Manuk is the easternmost volcano in the Banda volcanic arc.

name: Banda Api
summary: The 3-km-wide island of Banda Api is the northern-most volcano in the Banda arc and has a long period of recorded observation because of its key location in the Portuguese and Dutch spice trade.

name: Colo
summary: Colo volcano forms the isolated small island of Una Una in the middle of the Gulf of Tomini in northern Sulawesi.

name: Ambang
summary: The compound Ambang volcano is the westernmost of the active volcanoes on the northern arm of Sulawesi.

name: Soputan
summary: The Soputan stratovolcano on the southern rim of the Quaternary Tondano caldera on the northern arm of Sulawesi Island is one of Sulawesi's most active volcanoes.

name: Lokon-Empung
summary: The Lokong-Empung volcanic complex, rising above the plain of Tondano in North Sulawesi, includes four peaks and an active crater.

name: Mahawu
summary: The elongated Mahawu volcano immediately east of Lokon-Empung volcano is the northernmost of a series of young volcanoes along a SSW-NNE line near the margin of the Quaternary Tondano caldera.

name: Klabat
summary: Klabat is a symmetrical stratovolcano near the tip of the northern arm of Sulawesi Island, east of the city of Manado.

name: Tangkoko-Duasudara
summary: The eastern peninsula at the far NE end of Sulawesi near the city of Bitung is occupied by a volcanic complex consisting of two major edifices within a nature reserve.

name: Ruang
summary: Ruang volcano is the southernmost volcano in the Sangihe Island arc, north of Sulawesi Island; it is not the better known Raung volcano on Java.

name: Karangetang
summary: Karangetang (Api Siau) volcano lies at the northern end of the island of Siau, about 125 km NNE of the NE-most point of Sulawesi.

name: Banua Wuhu
summary: The submarine Banua Wuhu volcanic cone lies ~600 m off the western coast of Mahengatang Island, the emergent summit of a large submarine edifice, in the Sangihe Islands.

name: Awu
summary: The massive Gunung Awu stratovolcano occupies the northern end of Great Sangihe Island, the largest of the Sangihe arc.

name: Tarakan
summary: Two cinder cones between Galela Bay and Lake Galela on norther Halmahera, NE of Dukono volcano, were mapped by Supriatna (1980) as basaltic and Holocene.

name: Dukono
summary: The Dukono complex in northern Halmahera is on an edifice with a broad, low profile containing multiple peaks and overlapping craters.

name: Tobaru
summary: Gunung Tobaru, also known as Lolodai, is located in northern Halmahera WSW of Dukono and NNE of Ibu.

name: Ibu
summary: The truncated summit of Gunung Ibu stratovolcano along the NW coast of Halmahera Island has large nested summit craters.

name: Gamkonora
summary: The shifting of eruption centers on Gamkonora, the highest peak of Halmahera, has produced an elongated series of summit craters along a N-S trending rift.

name: Todoko-Ranu
summary: Todoko-Ranu is a large volcanic complex south of Gamkonora in North Maluku, Halmahera, that includes two calderas.

name: Jailolo
summary: The Jailolo volcanic complex forms a peninsula west of Jailolo Bay on the western coast of Halmahera Island.

name: Hiri
summary: Hiri is a 3-km-wide forested island immediately north of Gamalama on Ternate Island, and is the northernmost of a chain of volcanic islands off the western coast of Halmahera.

name: Gamalama
summary: Gamalama is a near-conical stratovolcano that comprises the entire island of Ternate off the western coast of Halmahera, and is one of Indonesia's most active volcanoes.

name: Kie Matubu
summary: The conical Kie Matubu volcano on the south end of Tidore Island is the highest peak of the North Maluku island chain west of Halmahera.

name: Mare
summary: The small volcanic island of Mare, immediately south of Tidore, was mapped as Holocene in age by Apandi and Sudana (1980).

name: Moti
summary: The 5-km-wide island of Moti, also known as Motir, is part of a chain of volcanic islands off the western coast of Halmahera.

name: Kie Besi
summary: Kie Besi volcano, forming the 10-km-wide Makian island off the west coast of Halmahera, has been the source of infrequent, but strong eruptions that have devastated villages on the island.

name: Melebingoy
summary: Mélébingóy (previously known as Parker) is a low, vegetated stratovolcano overlooking Sarangani Bay near the southern tip of Mindanao Island.

name: Matutum
summary: The symmetrical Matutum stratovolcano overlooks the  city of General Santos in southern Mindanao, NW of Sarangani Bay, Philippines.

name: Leonard Range
summary: An andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano complex in the Leonard Range is truncated by a 4 x 5 km caldera partially filled by Lake Leonard.

name: Makaturing
summary: Mount Makaturing is the central edifice in the Butig Mountains S of Lake Lanao in central Mindanao that includes a complex of volcanic cones and craters stretching 10 km E and 15 km WSW.

name: Ragang
summary: The large Ragang stratovolcano, also called Piapayungan, is SE of Lake Lanao in central Mindanao.

name: Musuan
summary: Musuan, also known as Calayo, is an isolated, low grass-covered andesitic-to-dacitic lava dome and tuff cone that rises above flat farmland in the province of Bukidnon in central Mindanao.

name: Camiguin
summary: The 20-km-long Camiguin Island just off the coast of north-central Mindanao Island consists of four overlapping stratovolcanoes overlying older buried edifices.

name: Kanlaon
summary: Kanlaon volcano (also spelled Canlaon) forms the highest point on the Philippine island of Negros.

name: Cabalían
summary: Mount Cabalían, at the SE tip of Leyte Island, is dissected by steep radial ridges that are moderately to thickly vegetated.

name: Biliran
summary: The volcanic island of Biliran, located across the narrow Biliran Strait from the northern tip of Leyte Island, contains many prominent andesitic lava domes, the highest of which is 1301 m Surio.

name: Bulusan
summary: Luzon's southernmost volcano, Bulusan, was constructed along the rim of the 11-km-diameter dacitic-to-rhyolitic Irosin caldera, which was formed about 36,000 years ago.

name: Mayon
summary: Symmetrical Mayon, which rises above the Albay Gulf NW of Legazpi City, is the most active volcano of the Philippines.

name: Iriga
summary: Mount Iriga (locally known as Mt Asog) is a small andesitic stratovolcano that rises immediately W of Lake Buhi which has satellitic cinder cones of basaltic composition.

name: Isarog
summary: The broad isthmus between Lagonoy Gulf and San Miguel Bay in SE Luzon is occupied by Mount Isarog.

name: Banahaw
summary: Banahaw (also known as Banahao), the highest of a group of volcanoes south and east of Manila, is flanked by San Cristobal (7 km W) and Banahaw de Lucban on the NE.

name: San Pablo Volcanic Field
summary: The San Pablo Volcanic Field, (also known as the Laguna Volcanic Field) lies at the southern end of Laguna de Bay, the largest lake on Luzon Island.

name: Taal
summary: Taal is one of the most active volcanoes in the Philippines and has produced some powerful eruptions.

name: Pinatubo
summary: Prior to 1991 Pinatubo volcano was a relatively unknown, heavily forested lava dome complex located 100 km NW of Manila with no records of historical eruptions.

name: Cagua
summary: The Mount Cagua stratovolcano lies at the NE tip of Luzon.

name: Camiguin de Babuyanes
summary: Forested Mount Camiguin occupies the SW tip of 22-km-long Camiguin Island in the Babuyan archipelago, north of Luzon Island.

name: Didicas
summary: Didicas, 22 km NE of Camiguin Island in the Babuyanes Islands north of Luzon, was a submarine volcano prior to 1952, when a permanent island was formed.

name: Babuyan Claro
summary: Multiple Quaternary volcanic centers occupy Babuyan de Claro Island north of Luzon.

name: Iraya
summary: The morphologically youthful Iraya stratovolcano is the northernmost active volcano in the Philippines.

name: Hainan Volcanic Field
summary: The Hainan volcanic field consists of Quaternary lava flows that extend over about 4,100 km2 of northern Hainan Island (also known as Qiong).

name: Ly Son Group
summary: The Lý Son (formerly known as Cù-Lao Ré) volcanic group consists of four subaerial and nine submarine cones about 150 km off the coast of central Vietnam.

name: Cendres, Ile des
summary: The Ile des Cendres group of submarine volcanoes off the SE coast of Vietnam includes two submarine cones that built ephemeral islands during an eruption in 1923 and two submarine lava cones of uncertain age.

name: Popa
summary: Mount Popa, in central Burma (Myanmar), is a large, steep-sided composite cone that rises above a surrounding lava plateau.

name: Tengchong
summary: The Tengchong volcanic field, located in southern China near the border with Burma (Myanmar), was active during five periods ranging from the early Pliocene to the Holocene.

name: Kueishantao
summary: Kueishantao Island, the southernmost of five small volcanic islands off the NE coast of Taiwan, is also known as Guieshan Island and "Turtle Mountain Island" due to its profile as seen from some points on Taiwan.

name: Tatun Volcanic Group
summary: The Tatun (Datun) group consists predominately of a series of andesitic lava domes in the northernmost part of Taiwan.

name: Submarine Volcano NNE of Iriomotejima
summary: The southernmost Ryukyu Islands volcano is a shallow submarine volcano 20 km NNE of Iriomotejima island and 35 km WSW of the northern tip of the island of Ishigakishima in an area with an estimated depth of 200-300 m.

name: Io-Torishima
summary: The 1 x 2.7 km island of Io-Torishima, located north of the largest island of the Ryukyus, Okinawa, is composed of two andesitic volcanoes.

name: Yokoatejima
summary: Yokoatejima is a small, 3.5-km-long, dumbbell-shaped island NW of Amami Oshima Island at the SW end of the Tokara island chain.

name: Akusekijima
summary: Akusekijima is a small stratovolcano in the southern Ryukyu Islands.

name: Suwanosejima
summary: The 8-km-long island of Suwanosejima in the northern Ryukyu Islands consists of an andesitic stratovolcano with two active summit craters.

name: Nakanoshima
summary: The 9 x 5 km island of Nakanoshima is surrounded by coral reefs.

name: Kuchinoshima
summary: Kuchinoshima, lying in the northern Ryukyu Islands between the volcanic islands of Nakanoshima and Kuchinoerabujima, consists of two andesitic stratovolcanoes and a NW-SE-trending chain of lava domes.

name: Kuchinoerabujima
summary: A group of young stratovolcanoes forms the eastern end of the irregularly shaped island of Kuchinoerabujima in the northern Ryukyu Islands, 15 km W of Yakushima.

name: Kikai
summary: Multiple eruption centers have exhibited recent activity at Kikai, a mostly submerged, 19-km-wide caldera near the northern end of the Ryukyu Islands south of Kyushu.

name: Ata
summary: The submerged 15 x 25 km Ata caldera under Kagoshima Bay is one of several large calderas in southern Kyushu and the source of major pyroclastic flows associated with its formation more than 40,000 years ago.

name: Aira
summary: The Aira caldera in the northern half of Kagoshima Bay contains the post-caldera Sakurajima volcano, one of Japan's most active.

name: Yonemaru-Sumiyoshiike
summary: Yonemaru and Sumiyoshiike are basaltic maars formed in coastal lowland deposits north of the Aira caldera, on the SW and SE flanks of the small Pleistocene Aojiki cone.

name: Kirishimayama
summary: Kirishimayama is a large group of more than 20 Quaternary volcanoes located north of Kagoshima Bay.

name: Fukue
summary: A group of small olivine basaltic shield volcanoes and cinder cones lies at the eastern end of Fukuejima in the Goto Islands off the western coast of Kyushu.

name: Unzendake
summary: The massive Unzendake volcanic complex comprises much of the Shimabara Peninsula east of the city of Nagasaki.

name: Asosan
summary: The 24-km-wide Asosan caldera was formed during four major explosive eruptions from 300,000 to 90,000 years ago.

name: Kujusan
summary: Kujusan is a complex of stratovolcanoes and lava domes lying NE of Aso caldera in north-central Kyushu.

name: Yufu-Tsurumi
summary: A group of lava domes rises above the hot spring resort city of Beppu on Japan's Inland Sea, possibly within an ancient breached caldera.

name: Abu
summary: The dominantly Pleistocene Abu volcano group, located along northern coast near the SW end of Honshu, consists of basaltic-to-dacitic lava flows, small shield volcanoes (some with associated cinder cones), and lava domes.

name: Sanbesan
summary: Sanbesan stratovolcano, near the northern coast of SW Honshu, has a summit cut by a small caldera about 1 km in diameter.

name: Izu-Tobu
summary: The Izu-Tobu volcano group (Higashi-Izu volcano group) is scattered over a broad, plateau-like area of more than 400 km2 on the E side of the Izu Peninsula.

name: Hakoneyama
summary: Hakoneyama volcano is truncated by two overlapping calderas, the largest of which is 10 x 11 km wide.

name: Fujisan
summary: The conical form of Fujisan, Japan's highest and most noted volcano, belies its complex origin.

name: Yokodake
summary: Yokodake lava dome, capped by eight small craters, has been active into the Holocene.

name: Ontakesan
summary: The massive Ontakesan stratovolcano, the second highest volcano in Japan, lies at the southern end of the Northern Japan Alps.

name: Hakusan
summary: Hakusan is a complex andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano near the western coast of central Honshu.

name: Norikuradake
summary: Norikuradake volcano consists of an elongated group of small andesitic stratovolcanoes and craters arranged along a N-S line above a ridge crest in the southern part of the Northern Japan Alps.

name: Akandanayama
summary: Akandanayama is located NW of Abo Pass in south-central Honshu.

name: Yakedake
summary: Yakedake rises above the popular resort of Kamikochi in the Northern Japan Alps.

name: Midagahara
summary: Midagahara volcano is a dissected andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano on a plateau surrounded by high peaks of the North Japan Alps.

name: Niigata-Yakeyama
summary: Niigata-Yakeyama, one of several Japanese volcanoes named Yakeyama ("Burning Mountain"), is an andesitic-to-dacitic lava dome in Niigata prefecture in west-central Honshu, about 20 km from the coast.

name: Myokosan
summary: Myokosan is a steep-sided basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano north of Nagano City that overlooks Lake Nojiri below its SE flank.

name: Asamayama
summary: Asamayama, Honshu's most active volcano, overlooks the resort town of Karuizawa, 140 km NW of Tokyo.

name: Kusatsu-Shiranesan
summary: The Kusatsu-Shiranesan complex, located immediately north of Asama volcano, consists of a series of overlapping pyroclastic cones and three crater lakes.

name: Shiga
summary: The Shiga volcanic complex immediately north of Kusatsu-Shirane volcano consists of a group of small andesitic shield volcanoes and pyroclastic cones.

name: Harunasan
summary: Harunasan volcano is truncated by a small summit caldera containing the symmetrical post-caldera pyroclastic cone of Haruna-Fuji.

name: Akagisan
summary: The broad, low dominantly andesitic Akagisan volcano rises above the northern end of the Kanto Plain.

name: Hiuchigatake
summary: Hiuchigatake volcano lies in Nikko National Park and erupted the 8 km3 Hiuchigatake-Nanairi tephra and pyroclastic flow deposit about 170,00-160,000 years ago.

name: Nikko-Shiranesan
summary: Nikko-Shiranesan is a relatively small, 2578-m-high andesitic volcano consisting of a group of four lava domes resting on a shield volcano that rises to the NW of scenic Lake Chuzenji in Nikko National Park.

name: Nantaisan
summary: Nantaisan stratovolcano rises above the north shore of Lake Chuzenji in Nikko National Park, and forms a backdrop to the temple complex there.

name: Omanago Group
summary: The Omanago volcano group consists of a series of five closely spaced lava domes that were constructed north and NW of Nantai volcano in Nikko National Park.

name: Takaharayama
summary: Takaharayama is a small stratovolcano with lava domes located SW of Nasudake volcano and NNW of Utsunomiya city in central Honshu.

name: Nasudake
summary: The Nasudake volcanic group consists of a N-S-trending cluster of stratovolcanoes and lava domes at the north end of the Kanto Plain.

name: Numazawa
summary: Numazawa is a small, 2-km-wide dominantly dacitic-to-rhyolitic caldera constructed within an older Pliocene caldera.

name: Bandaisan
summary: One of Japan's most noted volcanoes, Bandaisan rises above the north shore of Lake Inawashiro.

name: Adatarayama
summary: The broad forested massif of Adatarayama volcano is located E of Bandai volcano, about 15 km SW of Fukushima city.

name: Azumayama
summary: The Azumayama volcanic group consists of a cluster of stratovolcanoes, shield volcanoes, lava domes, and pyroclastic cones.

name: Zaozan [Zaosan]
summary: The Zaozan (or Zaosan) volcano group consists of a complex cluster of stratovolcanoes in north-central Honshu about 40 km W of Sendai Bay.

name: Hijiori
summary: Hijiori caldera is a small, inconspicuous caldera located NE of the Pleistocene Gassan stratovolcano.

name: Naruko
summary: Naruko is a poorly defined, 5.5 x 7 km caldera NW of the city of Sendai.

name: Kurikomayama
summary: The summit of Kurikomayama volcano is cut by a 4-km-wide caldera breached to the north that is partially filled by the Tsurugi-dake central cone, once mined for sulfur.

name: Chokaisan
