summary: Massive Chokaisan volcano is composed of two overlapping stratovolcanoes with a conical profile that inspired the local names of Akita-Fuji or Dewa-Fuji.

name: Akita-Komagatake
summary: Two calderas partially filled by basaltic cones cut the summit of Akita-Komagatake volcano.

name: Iwatesan
summary: Viewed from the east, Iwatesan volcano has a symmetrical profile that invites comparison with Fuji, but on the west an older cone is visible containing an oval-shaped, 1.8 x 3 km caldera.

name: Hachimantai
summary: Hachimantai was constructed from widely scattered vents during the Pleistocene and is capped with andesitic lavas from vents in the center of the complex.

name: Akita-Yakeyama
summary: One of several Japanese volcanoes named Yakeyama ("Burning Mountain"), Akita-Yakeyama is the most recently active of a group of coalescing edifices in NW Honshu immediately west of Hachimantai volcano.

name: Megata
summary: Megata, a group of three small maars along the tip of the Oga Peninsula in NW Honshu, has been active during the Holocene (Ishikawa et al., 1957).

name: Iwakisan
summary: Iwakisan volcano, symmetrical on all but its western flanks, has been called the Fujisan of the Tsugaru district.

name: Towada
summary: The lake-filled, 11-km-wide, Towada caldera in northern Honshu formed during as many as six major explosive eruptions over a 40,000-year period ending about 13,000 years ago.

name: Hakkodasan
summary: The basaltic-to-rhyolitic Hakkodasan volcano includes at least 17 stratovolcanoes and lava domes south of Mutsu Bay at the northern end of Honshu.

name: Osorezan
summary: Osorezan, on the Shimokita Peninsula in northernmost Honshu, contains a 5-km-wide caldera partly occupied by a shallow lake that drains through the N caldera wall.

name: Izu-Oshima
summary: Izu-Oshima volcano in Sagami Bay, east of the Izu Peninsula, is the northernmost of the Izu Islands.

name: Toshima
summary: The small 2 x 2.4 km island of Toshima is located in the northern Izu Islands south of Izu-Oshima Island about 20 km W of the main volcanic front.

name: Niijima
summary: The elongated island of Niijima, SSW of Oshima, is 11 km long and only 2.5 km wide.

name: Kozushima
summary: A cluster of rhyolitic lava domes and associated pyroclastic deposits form the 4 x 6 km island of Kozushima in the northern Izu Islands.

name: Miyakejima
summary: The circular, 8-km-wide island of Miyakejima forms a low-angle stratovolcano that rises about 1,100 m from the sea floor in the northern Izu Islands about 200 km SSW of Tokyo.

name: Mikurajima
summary: Mikurajima is a small steep-sided island located between the more well-known Miyakejima and Hachijojima volcanoes.

name: Kurose Hole
summary: Kurose Hole, between Mikura and Hachijo-jima islands, is a nearly circular submarine caldera 5-7 km in diameter with a 600-760 m deep floor.

name: Hachijojima
summary: Hachijojima, in the central Izu Islands about 300 km S of Tokyo, consists of two small Quaternary dominantly basaltic stratovolcanoes forming an elongated NW-SE-trending island.

name: Aogashima
summary: The small 2.5 x 3.5 km dominantly basaltic island of Aogashima is surrounded by steep cliffs and contains a small 1.7 x 1.5-km-wide caldera.

name: Kita-Bayonnaise
summary: The large submarine Kita-Bayonnaise (North Bayonnaise) submarine caldera, also known as Myojin Knoll, lies between the Aogashima and Myojinsho (also called Beyonesu Rocks) calderas abotu 300 km SSE of the Izu Peninsula.

name: Myojinsho
summary: Beyonesu Rocks are part of the barely exposed rim of the largely submarine Myojinsho caldera.

name: Sumisujima
summary: Sumisujima (also known as Smith Rocks) is a steep-sided basaltic pinnacle that forms part of the outer southern flank of a 8-9 km submarine caldera that truncates a 20-km-wide seamount.

name: Izu-Torishima
summary: The circular, 2.7-km-wide island of Izu-Torishima in the southern Izu Islands is capped by an unvegetated summit cone formed during an eruption in 1939.

name: Sofugan
summary: Sofugan is a steep-sided pinnacle that rises 99 m above the sea surface south of Torishima volcano.

name: Suiyo Seamount
summary: Suiyo, one of the Shichiyo Seamounts, named for the seven days of the week, lies south of Sofugan volcano.

name: Mokuyo Seamount
summary: Mokuyo is one of the Shichiyo Seamounts, named for the seven days of the week.

name: Doyo Seamount
summary: Doyo is the southernmost of the Shichiyo Seamounts, named for the seven days of the week.

name: Nishinoshima
summary: The small island of Nishinoshima was enlarged when several new islands coalesced during an eruption in 1973-74.

name: Kaikata Seamount
summary: Kaikata Seamount is a basaltic-to-dacitic submarine volcano located north of Kaitoku Seamount.

name: Kaitoku Seamount
summary: Submarine eruption have been observed during March 1984 and August 2022-January 2023 from Kaitoku Seamount (Kaitoku Kaizan), a three-peaked submarine volcano 80 km NNW of Kita-Ioto.

name: Kita-Ioto
summary: No historical eruptions have occurred from the deeply eroded Kita-Ioto stratovolcano, which forms a steep-sided basaltic cone rising about 800 m above the sea.

name: Ioto
summary: Ioto, in the Volcano Islands of Japan, lies within a 9-km-wide submarine caldera.

name: Kita-Fukutokutai
summary: Kita-Fukutokutai is a submarine volcano halfway between the Ioto and Minami-Ioto islands.

name: Fukutoku-Oka-no-Ba
summary: Fukutoku-Oka-no-ba is a submarine volcano located 5 km NE of the island of Minami-Ioto.

name: Minami-Hiyoshi
summary: Periodic water discoloration and water-spouting have been reported over the Minami-Hiyoshi submarine volcano since 1975, when detonation sounds and an explosion were also reported.

name: Nikko
summary: Nikko submarine volcano is a massive seamount that rises from nearly 3 km depth to within 392 m of the ocean surface near the N end of the Mariana Volcanic Arc.

name: Fukujin
summary: Fukujin seamount in the Mariana Volcanic Arc has risen on occasion to just beneath the ocean surface.

name: Kasuga 1
summary: Kasuga 1, the northernmost of three seamounts in the the Kasuga seamount chain SE of Fukujin, rises from a depth of 3,000 m to within about 600 m of the ocean surface.

name: Kasuga 2
summary: Kasuga 2, also referred to as Minami Kasuga (South Kasuga), is the central of three volcanoes forming the Kasuga seamount chain, which trends SSW from the volcanic front of the Izu-Marianas arc.

name: NW Eifuku
summary: NW Eifuku is a small submarine volcano that exhibits vigorous thermal activity.

name: Daikoku
summary: The conical summit of Daikoku seamount lies along an E-W ridge SE of Eifuku and rises to within 323 m of the sea surface.

name: Farallon de Pajaros
summary: The small 2-km-wide island of Farallon de Pajaros (also known as Uracas) is the northernmost and most active volcano of the Mariana Islands.

name: Ahyi
summary: Ahyi seamount is a large conical submarine volcano ~18 km SE of the island of Farallon de Pajaros in the northern Marianas.

name: Supply Reef
summary: Supply Reef is a conical submarine volcano in the northern Mariana Islands that rises to within 8 m of the surface.

name: Maug Islands
summary: The three small elongated Maug Islands, the largest ~2.3 km long, represent the rim of a 2.5-km-wide caldera on a submarine edifice more than 20 km in diameter.

name: Asuncion
summary: A single large asymmetrical stratovolcano forms 3-km-wide Asuncion Island.

name: Agrigan
summary: The highest of the Marianas arc volcanoes, Agrigan contains a 500-m-deep, flat-floored caldera.

name: Pagan
summary: Pagan Island, the largest and one of the most active of the Mariana Islands volcanoes, consists of two stratovolcanoes connected by a narrow isthmus.

name: Alamagan
summary: Alamagan is the emergent summit of a large stratovolcano in the central Mariana Islands with a roughly 350-m-deep summit crater east of the center of the island.

name: Guguan
summary: The island of Guguan, ~2.8 km in diameter, is composed of an eroded volcano on the south, a caldera with a post-caldera cone, and a northern volcano.

name: Zealandia Bank
summary: Zealandia Bank consists of two pinnacles about 1 km apart rising from a submerged bank to near the ocean surface between Guguan and Sarigan Islands.

name: Sarigan
summary: Sarigan volcano forms an irregular 3-km-long island consisting of a low truncated cone with a 750-m-wide summit crater that contains a small ash cone.

name: South Sarigan Seamount
summary: South Sarigan seamount, rising to within about 184 m of the ocean surface 12 km S of Sarigan Island, was the site of a short explosive submarine eruption in May 2010 that produced a plume of ash and steam to 12 km altitude.

name: Anatahan
summary: The elongate, 9-km-long island of Anatahan in the central Mariana Islands consists of a large stratovolcano with a 2.3 x 5 km compound summit caldera.

name: East Diamante
summary: The dacitic East Diamante submarine volcano contains an elongated NE-SW-trending caldera with a pronounced rim on the NE side.

name: Ruby
summary: Ruby is a basaltic submarine volcano that rises to within about 200 m of the ocean surface near the southern end of the Mariana arc NW of Saipan.

name: Esmeralda Bank
summary: Esmeralda Bank is a massive submarine volcano with three cones oriented N-S over about 15 km.

name: NW Rota-1
summary: A submarine volcano detected during a 2003 NOAA bathymetric survey of the Mariana Island arc was found to be hydrothermally active and named NW Rota-1.

name: Forecast Seamount
summary: Forecast Seamount lies about 70 km W of the southern tip of Guam and about 19 km NW of Seamount X.

name: Seamount X
summary: Hydrothermal activity was detected during a 2003 NOAA expedition at a submarine volcano about 70 km WSW of Guam.

name: Mariana Back-Arc Segment at 15.5°N
summary: The Mariana back-arc spreading segment centered at 15.5°N is part of a line of recently surveyed segments with anomalous hydrothermal plumes.

name: Oshima-Oshima
summary: Oshima-Oshima, a 10 km2 island about 105 km W offshore from the SW tip of Hokkaido, is the emergent summit of two coalescing basaltic-to-andesitic stratovolcanoes.

name: Esan
summary: Esan is a small volcanic complex of seven overlapping andesitic-to-dacitic lava domes on the eastern tip of the Oshima Peninsula across the Tsugaru Strait from Honshu.

name: Hokkaido-Komagatake
summary: Much of the truncated Hokkaido-Komagatake andesitic volcano on the Oshima Peninsula of southern Hokkaido is Pleistocene in age.

name: Toya
summary: Usuzan, one of Hokkaido's most well-known volcanoes, is a small stratovolcano located astride the southern topographic rim of the 110,000-year-old Toya caldera.

name: Niseko
summary: The Niseko volcano group in SW Hokkaido contains a cluster of andesitic stratovolcanoes and lava domes that extends 25 km E-W and 15 km N-S.

name: Yoteizan
summary: Yoteizan is a symmetrical andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano with a Fuji-like profile the forms a prominent landmark NW of Toya caldera.

name: Kuttara
summary: The Kuttara volcanic group consists of a series of small stratovolcanoes, lava domes, pyroclastic cones, and a caldera near the Pacific coast SE of Toya caldera and SW of Shikotsu caldera.

name: Shikotsu
summary: The 13 x 15 km Shikotsu caldera, largely filled by the waters of Lake Shikotsu, was formed during one of Hokkaido's largest Quaternary eruptions about 31-34,000 years ago.

name: Rishirizan
summary: Rishirizan is a highly dissected andesitic stratovolcano that forms a 20-km-wide island west of the northern tip of Hokkaido.

name: Tokachidake
summary: Tokachidake volcano consists of a group of dominantly andesitic stratovolcanoes and lava domes arranged on a NE-SW line above a plateau of welded Pleistocene tuffs in central Hokkaido.

name: Taisetsuzan
summary: The Taisetsuzan volcano group lies at the northern end of the Taisetsu-Tokachi graben in central Hokkaido.

name: Maruyama
summary: The Nipesotsu-Maruyama volcano group, located west of Nukabira Lake about 20 km E of Tokachidake volcano, is composed of a number of overlapping andesitic-to-rhyolitic stratovolcanoes and lava domes constructed along a NW-SE trend.

name: Akan
summary: Akan is a 13 x 24 km caldera located immediately SW of Kussharo caldera in eastern Hokkaido.

name: Kussharo
summary: The 20 x 26 km Kussharo caldera (also spelled Kutcharo or Kuccharo), is the largest of a cluster of calderas in NE Hokkaido.

name: Mashu
summary: Mashu is a 6-km-wide Holocene caldera that truncates a stratovolcano constructed on the ESE rim of the large Kussharo caldera.

name: Rausudake
summary: Rausudake is an andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano with summit lava domes on the Shiretoko Peninsula in NE Hokkaido.

name: Tenchozan
summary: Phreatic eruptions at Tenchozan occurred approximately 1,900 years ago.

name: Shiretoko-Iozan
summary: Shiretoko-Iozan, one of many Japanese "sulfur mountains," is noted for the extrusion of molten sulfur during eruptions in 1889 and 1936.

name: Tomariyama [Golovnin]
summary: Tomariyama, also known as Golovnin, forms the southern end of Kunashir Island, across the Nemuro Strait from Hokkaido.

name: Raususan [Mendeleev]
summary: Raususan, also known as Mendeleev, is a low compound stratovolcano located in the southern part of Kunashir Island.

name: Ruruidake [Smirnov]
summary: Ruruidake is a late-Pleistocene andesitic-to-dacitic volcanic complex on the NW tip of Kunashir Island in the southern Kuriles, NW of Chachadake [Tiatia} volcano.

name: Chachadake [Tiatia]
summary: The symmetrical Chachadake, also known as Tiatia, is on the SE side of northern Kunashir Island in the southern Kuriles.

name: Berutarubesan [Berutarube]
summary: The Berutarubesan andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano forms the SW tip of Iturup Island in the southern Kuriles.

name: Etorofu-Atosanupuri [Atosanupuri]
summary: The conical Etorofu-Atosanupuri stratovolcano forms a prominent peninsula joined to the SW side of Iturup (Etorofu) Island by a low isthmus only 30 m high.

name: Hitokappu Volcano Group [Bogatyr Ridge]
summary: The Hitokappu Volcano Group [Bogatyr Ridge] on Iturup Island in the southern Kuriles consists of a cluster of late-Pleistocene to Holocene cones and craters extending ~14 km NE-SW.

name: Etorofu-Yakeyama [Grozny Group]
summary: The Etorofu-Yakeyama (Ivan Grozny) complex is located in the center of Iturup Island.

name: Odamoisan [Tebenkov]
summary: Odamoisan (also known as Tebenkov), lies in the center of Iturup Island along the E coast.

name: Sashiusudake [Baransky]
summary: The Sashiusudake (also known as Baransky) volcanic complex along the Pacific coast in the central part of Iturup Island consists of an eroded Pleistocene volcano that is capped by a Holocene stratovolcano.

name: Chirippusan [Chirip]
summary: Chirippusan (also simply Chirip) volcano is on the Chirip Peninsula, which extends N into the Sea of Okhotsk from central Iturup Island.

name: Moyorodake [Medvezhia]
summary: The Moyorodake volcanic complex (also known as Medvezhia) occupies the NE end of Iturup (Etorofu) Island.

name: Ivao Group
summary: The Ivao group of cones along the Krishtofovich Ridge of SW Urup Island contains several well-preserved cones of Holocene age.

name: Kolokol Group
summary: A group of Holocene volcanoes in central Urup Island is named after its most prominent volcano, Kolokol.

name: Kuril Arc at 46.3°N
summary: A shallow flat-topped edifice ~8 km in diameter, with depths from 0-50 m, is located in the Urup Strait ~15 km S of the Chernyye Brat'ya (Black Brothers) islands and ~20 km ENE of Urup Island in the Kuril Islands.

name: Chirpoi
summary: Chirpoi, a small island lying between the larger islands of Simushir and Urup, contains a half dozen volcanic edifices constructed within an 8-9 km wide, partially submerged caldera.

name: Milna
summary: Milna (or Mil'na) is the southernmost volcano on Simushir Island in the central Kuriles, and includes the Goriaschaia Sopka lava dome on the NW flank.

name: Zavaritzki Caldera
summary: The Zavaritzki volcano on Simushir Island in the central Kuril Islands contains three nested calderas 10, 8, and 3 km in diameter.

name: Prevo Peak
summary: Symmetrical Prevo Peak, also known as Simushiru-Fuji for its resemblance to Japan's noted volcano, is capped by a 500 x 600 m summit crater.

name: Uratman
summary: The northernmost volcano on Simushir Island, Uratman consists of a 7.5-km-wide Pleistocene caldera with walls that rise 450 m above a 250-m-deep caldera bay.

name: Ketoi
summary: The circular 10-km-wide Ketoi island, which rises across the 19-km-wide Diana Strait from Simushir Island, hosts of one of the most complex volcanic structures of the Kuril Islands.

name: Ushishur
summary: The subaerial portion of Ushishur volcano in the central Kuriles is exposed in two small islands, the southern containing the summit caldera and the northern a portion of the volcano's flanks.

name: Srednii
summary: Remnants of the Srednii submarine volcano form a hazardous obstruction in the strait between Rasshua and Ushishur Islands.

name: Rasshua
summary: The elongated 6 x 13 km island of Rasshua in the central Kuriles contains three overlapping central cones within a 6 km caldera whose eastern margin is beyond the shoreline.

name: Sarychev Peak
summary: Sarychev Peak, one of the most active volcanoes of the Kuril Islands, occupies the NW end of Matua Island in the central Kuriles.

name: Raikoke
summary: A low truncated volcano forms the small barren Raikoke Island, which lies 16 km across the Golovnin Strait from Matua Island in the central Kuriles.

name: Chirinkotan
summary: The small, mostly unvegetated 3-km-wide island of Chirinkotan occupies the far end of an E-W volcanic chain that extends nearly 50 km W of the central part of the main Kuril Islands arc.

name: Ekarma
summary: The small 5 x 7.5 km island of Ekarma lies 8.5 km N of Shiashkotan Island along an E-W-trending volcanic chain extending westward from the central part of the main Kuril Island arc.

name: Sinarka
summary: Sinarka volcano, occupying the northern end of Shiashkotan Island in the central Kuriles, has a complex structure.

name: Kharimkotan
summary: The 8 x 12 km island of Kharimkotan (also spelled Harimkotan) in the northern Kuriles consists of a stratovolcano cut by two breached depressions on the east and NW sides.

name: Tao-Rusyr Caldera
summary: The southern half of Onekotan Island in the northern Kuril Islands contains the 7.5-km-wide Tao-Rusyr caldera, which is mostly filled by Kal'tsevoe lake.

name: Nemo Peak
summary: Nemo Peak volcano at the northern end of Onekotan Island in the northern Kuriles is truncated by two preglacial nested calderas, the largest of which is 10 km in diameter and extends to the northern coast.

name: Shirinki
summary: The 3-km-diameter island of Shirinki is located west of the main Kuril Island arc and ~20 km WSW of Fuss Peak on Paramushir Island.

name: Fuss Peak
summary: Fuss Peak forms a peninsula that lies across a low isthmus on the SW coast of Paramushir Island in the northern Kuriles.

name: Karpinsky Group
summary: The Karpinsky Group on southern Paramushir Island in the Kuril Islands consists of three Holocene andesitic volcanic centers at the southern end of the Karpinsky Ridge.

name: Chikurachki
summary: Chikurachki, the highest volcano on Paramushir Island in the northern Kuriles, is a relatively small cone constructed on a high Pleistocene edifice.

name: Vernadsky Ridge
summary: The Vernadsky Ridge on northern Paramushir island in the northern Kuriles is a large massif with over 40 volcanic centers in three volcano groups each ~7-8 km apart.

name: Ebeko
summary: The flat-topped summit of the central cone of Ebeko volcano, one of the most active in the Kuril Islands, occupies the northern end of Paramushir Island.

name: Alaid
summary: The highest and northernmost volcano of the Kuril Islands, Alaid is a symmetrical stratovolcano when viewed from the north, but has a 1.5-km-wide summit crater that is breached open to the south.

name: Kambalny
summary: The southernmost major stratovolcano on the Kamchatka peninsula, Kambalny has a summit crater that is breached to the SE.

name: Koshelev
summary: Koshelev is at the southern end of the Kamchatka Peninsula, SW of the Pauzhetka volcano-tectonic depression and NW of Kambalny volcano.

name: Yavinsky
summary: Yavinsky is an early to mid-Pleistocene basaltic volcano that forms an arcuate ridge (Yavinsky Khrebet) along the SW coast of Kamchatka, overlooking the town of Ozernovsky and the mouth of the Ozernaya River.

name: Diky Greben
summary: Diky Greben is a lava-dome complex that formed in the center of the 20 x 25 km Pauzhetka caldera, which also contains the Kurile Lake caldera to the east.

name: Kurile Lake
summary: Kurile Lake caldera lies within the eastern part of the massive Pauzhetka caldera, but is considered as a separate volcanic system here.

name: Iliinsky
summary: The conical Iliinsky volcano (also spelled Ilyinsky), rising dramatically to 1555 m above the NE shore of Kurile Lake, was constructed beginning about 7600 radiocarbon years ago at the NE margin of Kurile Lake caldera.

name: Zheltovsky
summary: Zheltovsky volcano was constructed during the last 8000 years within a 4 x 5 km caldera truncating an earlier Pleistocene edifice.

name: Ksudach
summary: Ksudach is unique among Kamchatka volcanoes in its morphology and geologic history.

name: Olkoviy-Ozernoy Volcanic Field
summary: A large group of Quaternary basaltic pyroclastic cones and associated lava flows (Masurenkov, 1980) fills a topographic low W and NW of Ksudach and Khodutka volcanoes.

name: Khodutka
summary: Khodutka stratovolcano was formed during the late-Pleistocene to early Holocene, partially covering the older Priemysh stratovolcano on the NW flank.

name: Asacha
summary: The Asacha group is a complex massif of Pleistocene-to-Holocene volcanoes located within a distinctly fault-bounded crustal block WSW of Mutnovsky volcano.

name: Visokiy
summary: The basaltic Visokiy cone is the largest and central feature of a 10-km-long line of basaltic cinder cones between Asacha to the SW and Gorely to the NE.

name: Mutnovsky
summary: Massive Mutnovsky, one of the most active volcanoes of southern Kamchatka, is formed of four coalescing stratovolcanoes of predominantly basaltic composition.

name: Gorely
summary: Gorely volcano consists of five small overlapping stratovolcanoes constructed along a WNW-ESE line within a large 9 x 13 km caldera.

name: Opala
summary: The steep-sided conical Opala stratovolcano was constructed during the late-Pleistocene to Holocene at the northern end of the 12 x 14 km, 40,000-year-old Opala caldera.

name: Tolmachev Dol
summary: Tolmachev Dol (Tomachev Plateau) is broad volcanic highland NE of Opala volcano that includes numerous late-Pleistocene and Holocene cinder cones and associated lava flows.

name: Vilyuchinsky
summary: Vilyuchinsky, or Vilyuchik, is a steep-sided Pleistocene-to-Holocene stratovolcano south of Avachinsky Bay.

name: Barkhatnaya Sopka
summary: The Barkhatnaya Sopka group of Pleistocene andesitic-to-rhyolitic lava domes and Holocene basaltic pyroclastic cones is located along the Paratunka River about 30 km NNW of Gorely volcano.

name: Koryaksky
summary: The large symmetrical Koryaksky stratovolcano is the most prominent landmark of the NW-trending Avachinskaya volcano group, which towers above Kamchatka's largest city, Petropavlovsk.

name: Avachinsky
summary: Avachinsky, one of Kamchatka's most active volcanoes, rises above Petropavlovsk, Kamchatka's largest city.

name: Dzenzursky
summary: Dzenzursky is a strongly eroded stratovolcano of Pleistocene age that lies along a ridge extending NW from Zhupanovsky volcano.

name: Zhupanovsky
summary: The Zhupanovsky volcanic massif consists of four overlapping stratovolcanoes along a WNW-trending ridge.

name: Veer
summary: Cinder cones along the Levaya Avacha River about 60 km N of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskiy erupted lavas over young river terraces.

name: Kostakan
summary: A group of basaltic cinder cones lies south of Bakening volcano, west of the Srednaya Avacha (Middle Avacha) river valley.

name: Bakening
summary: Bakening (also known as Bakenin) lies well west of the eastern volcanic range of Kamchatka, at the head of the Srednyaya Avacha River, about 100 km NNW of Petropavlovsk.

name: Zavaritsky
summary: Zavaritsky volcano consists of a complex of six cinder cones trending NW-SE, and an explosion crater located near the headwaters of the Levaya Avacha River west of the main Eastern Kamchatka volcanic arc.

name: Akademia Nauk
summary: The lake-filled Akademia Nauk caldera is one of three volcanoes constructed within the mid-Pleistocene, 15-km-wide Polovinka caldera.

name: Karymsky
summary: Karymsky, the most active volcano of  Kamchatka's eastern volcanic zone, is a symmetrical stratovolcano constructed within a 5-km-wide caldera that formed during the early Holocene.

name: Maly Semyachik
summary: Maly Semyachik is a compound stratovolcano located in a 10-km-wide caldera within the 15 x 20 km mid-Pleistocene Stena-Soboliny caldera.

name: Bolshoi Semiachik
summary: The Bolshoi Semiachik volcanic complex was constructed within a 10-km-wide caldera whose rim is exposed only on the west.

name: Taunshits
summary: Taunshits volcano, located west of the massive Uzon caldera, is an andesitic stratovolcano that was constructed beginning about 39,000 years before present (BP) on top of a large Pleistocene tuya pedestal.

name: Uzon
summary: The Uzon and Geysernaya calderas, containing Kamchatka's largest geothermal area, form a 7 x 18 km depression that originated during multiple mid-Pleistocene eruptions.

name: Kikhpinych
summary: Kikhpinych, the youngest stratovolcano of the Eastern Volcanic Zone of Kamchatka, contains three summits constructed along a roughly E-W line above the eroded Pleistocene Pik volcano, NE of the Uzon caldera.

name: Krasheninnikov
summary: The late Pleistocene to Holocene Krasheninnikov volcano is comprised of two overlapping stratovolcanoes within a 9 x 10 km Pleistocene caldera.

name: Kronotsky
summary: The symmetrical Kronotsky stratovolcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula lies between the Pacific Ocean and Lake Kronotsky.

name: Gamchen
summary: Gamchen is a complex volcano composed of four stratovolcanoes, one of which is of Holocene age.

name: Komarov
summary: Komarov volcano is a complex structure along the Gamchen ridge.

name: Vysoky
summary: Visoky, at the northern end of a chain of small volcanoes trending NNW from Gamchen volcano, is a small Holocene stratovolcano with a youthful-looking summit crater constructed over the east flank of the Pleistocene Bogdanovich shield volcano.

name: Kizimen
summary: Kizimen is an isolated, conical stratovolcano that is morphologically similar to St.

name: Tolbachik
summary: The massive Tolbachik volcano is located at the southern end of the Kliuchevskaya volcano group.

name: Udina
summary: The Udina volcanic massif consists of two conical stratovolcanoes constructed along a WNW-ESE line at the south end of the Kliuchevskaya volcanic group, SE of Tolbachik volcano.

name: Zimina
summary: The eroded stratovolcanoes of Ostraya and Ovalnaya Zimina form a ridge north of the Udina complex at the SE end of the Kliuchevskaya volcano group.

name: Bezymianny
summary: The modern Bezymianny, much smaller than its massive neighbors Kamen and Kliuchevskoi on the Kamchatka Peninsula, was formed about 4,700 years ago over a late-Pleistocene lava-dome complex and an edifice built about 11,000-7,000 years ago.

name: Kamen
summary: The steep-sided Kamen stratovolcano lies at the center of a N-S chain of volcanoes, flanked by Bezymianny and Kliuchevskoi.

name: Klyuchevskoy
summary: Klyuchevskoy is the highest and most active volcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula.

name: Ushkovsky
summary: The Ushkovsky (formerly known as Plosky) complex is a large compound volcanic massif located at the NW end of the Kliuchevskaya volcano group.

name: Sheveluch
summary: The high, isolated massif of Sheveluch volcano (also spelled Shiveluch) rises above the lowlands NNE of the Kliuchevskaya volcano group.

name: Piip
summary: Dredged rocks from the summits of volcanic cones rising from 2,500 m depth to within a few hundred meters of the surface yielded dacitic lavas and pumice apparently of Holocene age (Fedotov et al., 1989; Seliverstov et al., 1986).

name: Khangar
summary: Khangar volcano, also spelled Hangar, is the southernmost volcano of the Sredinny Range, which stretches N-S across western Kamchaktka.

name: Cherpuk Group
summary: Severny Cherpuk (South Cherpuk) and Yuzhny Cherpuk (North Cherpuk) are two cinder cones SW of Ichinsky volcano that comprise the largest monogenetic volcanoes of the Sredinny Range.

name: Ichinsky
summary: Ichinsky, by far the highest peak in the Sredinny Range, is a massive, 450 km3 edifice.

name: Bolshoi-Kekuknaysky
summary: Bolshoi (Bolshoy) and Kekuknaysky are two large, partially overlapping basaltic shield volcanoes located NW and NNW, respectively, of Uksichan volcano.

name: Alney-Chashakondzha
summary: The glacier-capped Alney-Chashakondzha complex, one of the largest volcanoes of the Sredinny Range, consists of two large mostly Pleistocene andesitic stratovolcanoes constructed on a large Pliocene shield volcano.

name: Shisheika
summary: The andesitic Shisheika lava dome lies far to the west of the crest of the Sredinny Range, near the mouth of the Shishei River.

name: Terpuk
summary: Terpuk is a small basaltic shield volcano west of the crest of the Sredinny Range, south of Leutongey volcano, and NW of Kebeney volcano.

name: Sedanka Lava Field
summary: The Sedanka lava field (Sedanka Dol) is located immediately west of the Sredinny Range axis and is formed by dominantly mafic lavas from small strato- and shield-like volcanoes, along with more than 100 cinder and lava cones of the late….

name: Gorny Institute
summary: Gorny Institute volcano lies at the NE end of chain of small late-Quaternary volcanoes extending NE from Kebeney volcano in the central Sredinny Range.

name: Kinenin
summary: Kinenin maar lies at the eastern foot of the Sredinny Range, about 80 km NNW of Sheveluch volcano.

name: Bliznetsy
summary: The Bliznetsy ("Twins") lava flows occupy a low-lying area east of the Sredinny Range and north of the Eastern Volcanic Zone volcanoes.

name: Titila
summary: Titila is a small basaltic shield volcano NW of Lake Glubokoye, west of the crest of the central Sredinny Range.

name: Elovsky
summary: This cluster of overlapping small basaltic shield volcanoes is located east of the crest of the Sredinny Range, NE of Shishel and SE of Alngey volcanoes.

name: Nylgimelkin
summary: The basaltic Nylgimelkin (also known as Atlasov) shield volcano and the topographically higher but smaller shield of Novagrablenova are dwarfed by their neighbor, the glacier-clad Pleistocene Khuvkhoitun, the highest Quaternary volcano of the northern….

name: Spokoiny
summary: The dacitic-to-rhyolitic Spokoiny stratovolcano lies immediately south of Ostry volcano and NE of Iktunup volcano in the northern Sredinny Range.

name: Ostry
summary: Conical Ostry volcano (also known as Ostraya) is a late-Quaternary stratovolcano on the western side of the major NE-trending graben along the axis of the northern Sredinny Range.

name: Severny
summary: Severny is a late Quaternary shield volcano located at the NW end of a major NE-trending graben along the crest of the northern Sredinny Range.

name: Udokan Plateau
summary: The Udokan Plateau volcanic field occupies a broad area about 400 km ENE of the northern tip of Lake Baikal.

name: Jombolok
summary: A group of small basaltic cinder cones in the East Sayan region of central Asia, about 200 km WNW of the SW tip of Lake Baikal, produced the Jombolok lava field.

name: Taryatu-Chulutu
summary: The Taryatu-Chulutu volcanic field lies in north-central Mongolia about 250 km W of Ulaanbaatar.

name: Khoid Naiman Nuur
summary: A cone, designated here as Khoid Naiman Nuur ("North Eight Lakes"), is located in the upper reaches of a river valley ~25 km SW from the Orkhan (or Tsutgalan) waterfall, just N of the Khuisiin Naiman Nuur ("Eight Lakes of the Navel") area.

name: Ashikule Volcanic Field
summary: The Ashikule Volcanic Field contains 10 Pliocene to Holocene pyroclastic cones at the western end of the Kunlun Mountains.

name: Honggeertu
summary: The Honggeertu volcanic field is located in Nei Mongol Province, NW of Beijing.

name: Arxan-Chaihe
summary: The Arxan-Chaihe Volcanic Field, in the central Da Hinggan Mountains of Inner Mongolia in NE China, contains at least 27 volcanic features.

name: Keluo Group
summary: The Keluo volcanic field in NE China is located near the Russian border, S of the Heilongjiang (Black Dragon) River.

name: Wudalianchi
summary: The Wudalianchi volcanic field, named for a string of five scenic lava-dammed lakes, consists of 14 cinder cones capping a 500 km2 shield-like lava plateau in NE China.

name: Jingpohu
summary: Jingpohu is a Pliocene-to-Holocene volcanic field in the Jingpo Lake area of Heilongjiang Province, NE China.

name: Longgang Group
summary: The Longgang volcanic field covers 1,700 km2 in the Jilin Province of NE China.

name: Changbaishan
summary: Massive Changbaishan stratovolcano (also known as Baitoushan and by the Korean names of Baegdu, Paektu, or P'aektu-san), is located along the China/Korea border.

name: Ulleungdo
summary: Ulleungdo, also known as Ulreungdo, is a 10-km-wide island about 100 km E of the central Korean Peninsula.

name: Halla
summary: The massive Halla shield volcano forms much of the 40 x 80 km Cheju (Jeju) Island, which lies 90 km S of the Korean Peninsula.

name: Buldir
summary: The westernmost volcanic center of the 2500-km-long Aleutian arc, the island includes the older Buldir volcano in the center and the younger East Cape volcano to the NE.

name: Kiska
summary: Conical Kiska volcano is the westernmost historically active volcano of the 2500-km-long Aleutian arc.

name: Segula
summary: The 6 x 7 km island of Segula east of Kiska volcano consists of a conical stratovolcano cut by a prominent NNW-SSE-trending fissure that extends to sea level at both ends of the island.

name: Davidof
summary: A cluster of small islands between Segula and Little Sitkin in the western Aleutians, the largest of which is Davidof, are remnants of a stratovolcano that collapsed during the late Tertiary, forming a 2.7-km-wide caldera.

name: Little Sitkin
summary: Diamond-shaped Little Sitkin Island is bounded by steep cliffs on the east, north, and NE sides.

name: Semisopochnoi
summary: Semisopochnoi, the largest subaerial volcano of the western Aleutians, is 20 km wide at sea level and contains an 8-km-wide caldera.

name: Gareloi
summary: The 8 x 10 km Gareloi Island, the northernmost volcano of the Delarof Group at the western end of the Andreanof Islands, consists of a stratovolcano with two summits and a prominent SE-trending fissure.

name: Tanaga
summary: Tanaga volcano, the second largest volcanic center of the central Aleutians, is the central and highest of three youthful stratovolcanoes oriented along a roughly E-W line at the NW tip of Tanaga Island.

name: Takawangha
summary: Takawangha is a youthful volcano with an ice-filled caldera on northern Tanaga Island, near the western end of the Andreanof Islands.

name: Bobrof
summary: The geology and timing of volcanism on this small uninhabited 3 x 4 km island, located in the Andreanof islands 50 km west of Adak and 15 km west of Kanaga volcano, are unknown (Coats, 1956).

name: Kanaga
summary: Symmetrical Kanaga stratovolcano is situated within the Kanaton caldera at the northern tip of Kanaga Island.

name: Moffett
summary: Rising above Adak, the largest town of the Aleutians, Mount Moffett is a modest-sized, eroded stratovolcano with several flank lava domes.

name: Great Sitkin
summary: The Great Sitkin volcano forms much of the northern side of Great Sitkin Island.

name: Kasatochi
summary: Located at the northern end of a shallow submarine ridge trending perpendicular to the Aleutian arc, Kasatochi is small 2.7 x 3.3 km island volcano with a 750-m-wide summit crater lake.

name: Koniuji
summary: The very small, 1 x 1.5 km Koniuji Island, between Atka and Kasatochi volcanoes, is the emergent top of a mostly submarine volcano.

name: Atka Volcanic Complex
summary: The Atka Volcanic Complex consists of a central shield and Pleistocene caldera and four notable volcanic cones.

name: Seguam
summary: The 11.5 x 24 km island of Seguam, between Amlia and Amukta Islands in the central Aleutians, contains two calderas with Holocene post-caldera cones.

name: Amukta
summary: The symmetrical Amukta stratovolcano lies in the central Aleutians SW of Chagulak Island and is the westernmost of the Islands of the Four Mountains group.

name: Chagulak
summary: The 3-km-diameter island of Chagulak is the exposed summit of a stratovolcano in the Islands of the Four Mountains group of the Aleutians.

name: Yunaska
summary: The elongated 9 x 23 km Yunaska in the Islands of the Four Mountains group of the Aleutian Islands is comprised of two distinct volcanic centers.

name: Herbert
summary: The 10-km-wide Herbert Island, the SW-most of the Islands of the Four Mountains group, lies across a strait SW of Mount Cleveland.

name: Carlisle
summary: Carlisle Island is a steep-sided, conical stratovolcano across the Carlisle Pass strait from Mount Cleveland.

name: Cleveland
summary: The symmetrical Mount Cleveland stratovolcano is situated at the western end of the uninhabited Chuginadak Island.

name: Tana
summary: The Tana volcanic complex forming the eastern half of the Chuginadak Island, opposite the conical Cleveland stratovolcano, is composed of two prominent E-W-trending volcanoes.

name: Uliaga
summary: The small 3-km-wide island of Uliaga, located at the NE end of the Islands of the Four Mountains archipelago immediately NW of Kagamil Island, is an eroded stratovolcano.

name: Kagamil
summary: Kagamil Island lies near the NE end of the Islands of the Four Mountains archipelago in the central Aleutians, between Chuginadak and Uliaga Islands.

name: Vsevidof
summary: The symmetrical Vsevidof stratovolcano, near the SW end of Umnak Island, contains a 1.2-km-wide, ice-filled summit crater that is breached by glaciers on the E and N sides.

name: Recheschnoi
summary: The heavily glaciated Recheschnoi stratovolcano is located ENE of a roughly 900-m-high saddle across from Vsevidof volcano.

name: Okmok
summary: The basaltic Okmok shield volcano forms the NE end of Umnak Island in the Aleutian Islands.

name: Bogoslof
summary: Bogoslof is the emergent summit of a submarine volcano that lies 40 km N of the main Aleutian arc.

name: Makushin
summary: The ice-covered Makushin volcano on northern Unalaska Island is capped by a 2.5 km caldera.

name: Akutan
summary: Akutan contains a 2-km-wide caldera with a large cinder cone in the NE part of the caldera that has been the source of frequent explosive eruptions and occasional lava effusion that covers the caldera floor.

name: Westdahl
summary: Westdahl is a broad glacier-covered volcano occupying the SW end of Unimak Island.

name: Fisher
summary: The Fisher caldera, on western Unimak Island NE of Westdahl volcano, is 11 x 18 km elongated in a NE direction It formed around 9,400 years ago, accompanied by emission of large-volume pyroclastic flows that reached the Bering Sea and the Pacific Ocean.

name: Shishaldin
summary: The symmetrical glacier-covered Shishaldin in the Aleutian Islands is the westernmost of three large stratovolcanoes in the eastern half of Unimak Island.

name: Roundtop
summary: The flat-topped, glacier-covered Roundtop is the easternmost and lowest of an E-W-trending line of volcanoes on eastern Unimak Island, 13 km SW of the village of False Pass.

name: Amak
summary: Amak, the easternmost of the Aleutian Islands, is a small island stratovolcano that lies north of the main Aleutian volcanic front, about 50 km NW of Frosty volcano on the western tip of the Alaska Peninsula.

name: Frosty
summary: Frosty Peak, the youngest of two large volcanic structures of the Cold Bay Volcanic Center, is the westernmost Holocene volcano on the Alaska Peninsula, SW of the village of Cold Bay.

name: Dutton
summary: The Mount Dutton volcanic center east of Cold Bay near the tip of the Alaska Peninsula consists of a glacier-covered central lava dome complex.

name: Emmons Lake Volcanic Center
summary: The Emmons Lake Volcanic Center, located north of Volcano Bay and SW of Pavlof volcano, includes the Emmons and Hague stratovolcanoes within the Emmons Lake caldera.

name: Pavlof
summary: The most active volcano of the Aleutian arc, Pavlof is a Holocene stratovolcano that was constructed along a line of vents extending NE from the Emmons Lake caldera.

name: Pavlof Sister
summary: Located near the western end of the Alaska Peninsula at the end of a chain of volcanoes trending NE from Emmons Lake caldera, the symmetrical Pavlof Sister stratovolcano is somewhat more eroded than Pavlof volcano to the SW.

name: Dana
summary: Mount Dana is a small calc-alkaline volcano NE of Canoe Bay inlet at the head of Pavlof Bay consisting of an apron of volcaniclastic debris surrounding a central dome complex.

name: Stepovak Bay Group
summary: The Stepovak Bay Group is a chain of four cones, extending over a distance of 18 km, just SW of Kupreanof volcano.

name: Kupreanof
summary: Kupreanof is the largest and NE-most of a group of five relatively closely spaced Quaternary volcanic centers opposite Stepovak Bay.

name: Veniaminof
summary: Veniaminof, on the Alaska Peninsula, is truncated by a steep-walled, 8 x 11 km, glacier-filled caldera that formed around 3,700 years ago.

name: Black Peak
summary: The highly eroded stratovolcano and lava dome complex of Black Peak was constructed within an ice-free mid-Holocene caldera with two small caldera lakes on the N and E sides.

name: Aniakchak
summary: One of the most dramatic calderas of the Aleutian arc, the 10-km-wide Aniakchak caldera formed around 3,400 years ago during a voluminous eruption in which pyroclastic flows traveled more than 50 km N to the Bering Sea and also reached the Pacific Ocean to….

name: Yantarni
summary: Yantarni is a small andesitic stratovolcano located between Aniakchak caldera and Chiginadak volcanoes that was not discovered until 1979.

name: Chiginagak
summary: The symmetrical, glaciated Chiginagak stratovolcano locatedon the Alaska Peninsula ~15 km NW of Chiginagak Bay contains a small summit crater, which is breached to the south, and one or more summit lava domes.

name: Kialagvik
summary: Kialagvik is a small, poorly known glacier-mantled stratovolcano NE of Chiginagak volcano with a Holocene central lava dome and associated pyroclastic-flow deposits (Riehle, in Wood and Kienle 1990).

name: Ugashik-Peulik
summary: The Ugashik-Peulik volcanic complex lies south of Becharof Lake and east of Upper Ugashik Lake.

name: Ukinrek Maars
summary: Ukinrek Maars are two explosion craters that were created in an area without previous volcanic activity during a 10-day phreatomagmatic eruption March-April 1977.

name: Alaska Peninsula Arc at 155.4°W
summary: A small unnamed lava dome and an associated lava flow about 30 km E of Becharof Lake and 8 km NW of Alinchak Bay are not significantly modified by glacial erosion.

name: Martin
summary: The mostly ice-covered Mount Martin stratovolcano lies at the SW end of the Katmai volcano cluster in Katmai National Park.

name: Mageik
summary: Mount Mageik is a broad ice-capped stratovolcano at the head of the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes across Katmai Pass from Trident volcano.

name: Trident
summary: The Trident stratovolcano cluster was named for the three prominent peaks that were the most visible features at the summit prior to 1953.

name: Katmai
summary: Katmai was initially considered to be the source of the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes ash flow in 1912.

name: Novarupta
summary: Novarupta, the least topographically prominent volcano in the Katmai area, was formed during a major eruption in 1912.

name: Griggs
summary: The summit of Mount Griggs towers above Knife Creek on the NE side of the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes.

name: Snowy Mountain
summary: Snowy Mountain, located 15 km NE of Mount Katmai, is the SW-most of a chain of closely spaced volcanoes extending NE along the crest of the Alaska Range.

name: Denison
summary: Mount Denison lies near the head of the Serpent Tongue, Hook, and Hallo glaciers NE of Snowy volcano.

name: Steller
summary: Mount Steller is part of a chain of closely spaced volcanic peaks oriented NE-SW in Katmai National Park and lies between Mount Denision and Kukak volcanoes.

name: Kukak
summary: The almost completely ice-covered Kukak volcano lies west of Hallo Bay near the end of a glacier-covered range extending NE from Mount Katmai.

name: Kaguyak
summary: The 2.5-km-wide Kaguyak caldera in the NE part of Katmai National Park is filled by a lake more than 180 m deep whose surface lies 550 m below the caldera rim.

name: Fourpeaked
summary: Poorly known Fourpeaked volcano in NE Katmai National Park consists of isolated outcrops surrounded by the Fourpeaked Glacier, which descends eastward almost to the Shelikof Strait.

name: Douglas
summary: Glacier-covered, dissected Mount Douglas stratovolcano is located at the N end of the Alaska Peninsula south of Kamishak Bay, and is the NE-most in Katmai National Park.

name: Augustine
summary: Augustine volcano, rising above Kamishak Bay in the southern Cook Inlet about 290 km SW of Anchorage, is the most active volcano of the eastern Aleutian arc.

name: Iliamna
summary: Iliamna is a prominent glacier-covered stratovolcano in Lake Clark National Park on the western side of Cook Inlet, about 225 km SW of Anchorage.

name: Redoubt
summary: Redoubt is a glacier-covered stratovolcano with a breached summit crater in Lake Clark National Park about 170 km SW of Anchorage.

name: Spurr
summary: Mount Spurr is the closest volcano to Anchorage, Alaska (130 km W) and just NE of Chakachamna Lake.

name: Hayes
summary: Hayes volcano, located in a remote and rugged part of the Alaska Range NW of Anchorage and N of Mount Gerdine, was not discovered until 1975.

name: St. Paul Island
summary: The largest of the Pribilof Islands, St.

name: Ingakslugwat Hills
summary: The Ingakslugwat Hills consist of at least 32 small cinder cones and eight larger craters covering more than 500 km2 in the Yukon-Kuskokwin delta area of SW Alaska.

name: St. Michael
summary: The St.

name: Imuruk Lake
summary: The Oligocene-to-Holocene Imuruk monogenetic volcanic field in the central Seward Peninsula north of the Bendeleben Mountains contains around 75 small basaltic vents surrounded by voluminous lava flows.

name: Buzzard Creek
summary: Two Holocene tuff rings form craters 300 and 66 m wide near the headwaters of Buzzard Creek at the northern foot of the central Alaska Range NE of the town of Healy along the Parks Highway.

name: Wrangell
summary: Mount Wrangell is one of the world's largest continental-margin volcanoes, with a diameter of 30 km at 2,000 m elevation.

name: Churchill
summary: The Bona-Churchill massif in the St.

name: Edgecumbe
summary: The Edgecumbe volcanic field covers about 260 km2 of Kruzov Island west of Sitka in SE Alaska.

name: Duncan Canal
summary: Basaltic flows in the Duncan Canal area of the central SE Alaska panhandle are both subaerial and submarine.

name: Tlevak Strait-Suemez Island
summary: Scattered flat-lying lava flows with pahoehoe surfaces occur near Tlevak Strait and on the SW end of Suemez Island near the southern end of the SE Alaska panhandle.

name: Behm Canal-Rudyerd Bay
summary: Numerous basaltic cinder cones and lava flows occur in the panhandle of SE Alaska on both sides of Behm Canal, which divides Revillagigedo Island from the mainland.

name: Fort Selkirk
summary: The Fort Selkirk volcanic field near the junction of the Yukon and Pelly rivers in central Yukon is the northernmost Holocene volcanic field in Canada.

name: Alligator Lake
summary: A group of basaltic cones and lava flows (the Miles Canyon basalts) in south-central Yukon near the capital city of Whitehorse was considered to be of Pleistocene age (Wheeler, 1961).

name: Atlin Volcanic Field
summary: The Surprise Lake volcanic field in the Atlin volcanic district is a group of late-Pleistocene to Holocene cinder cones on the Teslin Plateau in NW-most British Columbia, between Atlin Lake on the W and Surprise Lake on the E.

name: Tuya Volcanic Field
summary: A broad region with numerous formerly subglacial volcanic cones known as tuyas forms the Tuya Volcanic Field near Tuya Lake and a broad area to the N.

name: Heart Peaks
summary: The late-Cenozoic Heart Peaks shield volcano, located NW of Level Mountain in NW British Columbia, is capped by rhyolitic lava domes.

name: Level Mountain
summary: Level Mountain is the most voluminous eruptive center of the Stikine volcanic belt in NW British Columbia.

name: Edziza
summary: The composite felsic stratovolcano Mount Edziza and associated satellitic lava domes and pyroclastic cones were constructed over the past 7.5 million years during five magmatic cycles beginning with eruption of alkali basalts and ending with felsic and….

name: Spectrum Range
summary: The Spectrum Range, named for its extensive colorful solfataric alteration, is one of four large composite volcanoes that make up the Mount Edziza-Spectrum Range volcanic complex, in which a predominately rhyolitic lava dome complex overlies a basal….

name: Hoodoo Mountain
summary: Hoodoo Mountain is a flat-topped Pleistocene-to-Holocene volcano in the Boundary Ranges of NW British Columbia near the Alaska border that is composed of both subglacial and subaerial volcanic products.

name: Iskut-Unuk River Cones
summary: Eight small basaltic centers at the southern end of the Stikine volcanic belt near the Alaska border comprise the Iskut-Unuk River Cones group.

name: Tseax River Cone
summary: The basaltic Tseax River cinder cones (Aiyansh volcano) at the southern end of the Stikine volcanic belt have been the site of some of the youngest volcanic eruptions in Canada.

name: Crow Lagoon
summary: Thick deposits of Holocene basaltic tephra originating from an unknown volcanic center have been found near Crow Lagoon, ~40 km N of Prince Rupert near the southern tip of the SE Alaskan panhandle.

name: Milbanke Sound Group
summary: Swindle, Lake, and Lady Douglas Islands in the Milbanke Sound area of the Fiord Ranges in west-central British Columbia contain cinder cones of Holocene age.

name: Nazko
summary: Nazko Cone, the easternmost and youngest volcano of the Anahim Volcanic Belt in the Chilcotin-Nechako Plateau, central British Columbia, rests on glacial till.

name: Wells Gray-Clearwater
summary: The Wells Gray-Clearwater volcanic field in the Quesnel Highland of east-central British Columbia contains basaltic cones and lava flows of early Pleistocene to Holocene age.

name: Silverthrone
summary: The Silverthrone volcanic complex lies near the coast in SW British Columbia, 55 km N of Kingcome Inlet and 60 km NW of Knight Inlet.

name: Bridge River Cones
summary: The Bridge River Cones volcanic field consists of a group of small basaltic and trachybasaltic eruptive centers at the extreme northern end of the Garibaldi volcanic belt in SW British Columbia.

name: Meager
summary: Mount Meager volcanic complex, of Pliocene-to-Holocene age, forms a dissected andesitic-to-rhyodacitic stratovolcano with multiple eroded summit lava domes and volcanic necks.

name: Garibaldi Lake
summary: A group of nine small andesitic stratovolcanoes and basaltic andesite vents in the scenic Garibaldi Lake area immediately north of Mount Garibaldi was formed during the late Pleistocene and early Holocene.

name: Garibaldi
summary: Mount Garibaldi at the head of Howe Sound north of Vancouver is a Pleistocene dacitic stratovolcano capped by a lava dome complex.

name: Cayley Volcanic Field
summary: The Cayley volcanic field is a deeply dissected basaltic andesite to rhyodacitic complex that covers a broad area between the Cheakamus and Squamish river valleys in the central Garibaldi volcanic belt.

name: Baker
summary: Mount Baker, the northernmost of Washington's volcanoes, is a glacier-clad andesitic stratovolcano constructed above the E flank of the eroded mid-Pleistocene Black Buttes volcano and SW of the early Pleistocene 4.5 x 8 km rhyodacitic Kulshan caldera.

name: Glacier Peak
summary: Glacier Peak, the most isolated of the Cascade volcanoes, rises above the rugged forested terrain of the Glacier Peak Wilderness Area in the North Cascades.

name: Rainier
summary: Mount Rainier is a heavily glaciated andesitic volcano in the Puget Sound region.

name: Adams
summary: The andesitic-dacitic Mount Adams stratovolcano is second in volume only to Mount Shasta in the Cascade Range.

name: St. Helens
summary: Prior to 1980, Mount St.

name: West Crater
summary: West Crater, a small andesitic lava dome with associated lava flows, is part of a Quaternary volcanic field in southern Washington consisting primarily of small basaltic and basaltic andesite cinder cones and shield volcanoes, oriented along a NW-SE zone….

name: Indian Heaven
summary: The Pleistocene-to-Holocene Indian Heaven volcanic field, located midway between St.

name: Hood
summary: Mount Hood, Oregon's highest peak, forms a prominent backdrop to the city of Portland.

name: Jefferson
summary: Mount Jefferson, Oregon's second highest peak, is a deeply eroded stratovolcano.

name: Blue Lake Crater
summary: Blue Lake Crater is a series of at least three overlapping explosion craters along a NE trend slightly east of the crest of the Cascade Range in the state of Oregon.

name: Sand Mountain Field
summary: The Sand Mountain volcanic field consists of 23 basaltic and basaltic andesite cinder cones along a N-S line immediately west of the Cascade crest NW of Mount Washington.

name: Belknap
summary: The Belknap Crater area near McKenzie Pass in Oregon, north of the Three Sisters volcanoes, was the source of one of the largest concentrations of youthful volcanism in the Cascade Range.

name: Three Sisters
summary: The north-south-trending Three Sisters volcano group dominates the landscape of the Central Oregon Cascades.

name: Bachelor
summary: This volcanic system extends from Mount Bachelor on the N to Lookout Mountain about 20 km S, with a chain of scoria cones and small shield volcanoes between and additional volcanic features to the E.

name: Davis Lake
summary: The Davis Lake area contains three andesitic Holocene cinder cones and associated fresh-looking lava flows along a N-S line at the base of a group of Pleistocene basaltic andesite shield volcanoes east of the crest of the Cascade Range, south of the Mount….

name: Newberry
summary: Newberry volcano, situated east of the Cascade Range, covers an area of about 1,600 km2.

name: Devils Garden
summary: The Devils Garden lava field, the NW-most of a group of three youthful-looking basaltic lava fields SE of Newberry volcano, east of the Cascade Range, contains 117 km2 of overlapping pahoehoe lava flows erupted from fissure vents at the NE part of the field.

name: Cinnamon Butte
summary: Cinnamon Butte, Thirsty Point, and Kelsay Point are forested cinder cones along a WNW-ESE line immediately west of the Cascade crest and NE of Diamond Lake.

name: Crater Lake
summary: The spectacular 8 x 10 km Crater Lake caldera in the southern Cascades of Oregon formed about 7,700 years ago as a result of the collapse of a complex of overlapping shield and stratovolcanoes known as Mount Mazama.

name: Diamond Craters
summary: Diamond Craters volcanic field consists of a 70 km2 area of basaltic lava flows along with numerous cinder cones and maars located between the SE Oregon town of Burns and Steens Mountain.

name: Jordan Craters
summary: Jordan Craters volcanic field consists of well-preserved basaltic lava flows and scoria cones that are the youngest and northernmost of a group of three Quaternary lava fields covering an area of 250 km2 in SE Oregon.

name: Shasta
summary: The most voluminous of the Cascade volcanoes, northern California's Mount Shasta is a massive compound stratovolcano composed of at least four main edifices constructed over a period of at least 590,000 years.

name: Medicine Lake
summary: Medicine Lake is a large Pleistocene-to-Holocene, basaltic-to-rhyolitic shield volcano east of the main axis of the Cascade Range.

name: Lassen Volcanic Center
summary: The Lassen Volcanic Center consists of the andesitic Brokeoff stratovolcano SW of Lassen Peak, a dacitic lava dome field, peripheral small andesitic shield volcanoes, and large lava flows, primarily on the Central Plateau NE of Lassen Peak.

name: Clear Lake Volcanic Field
summary: The late-Pliocene to early Holocene Clear Lake Volcanic Field in the northern Coast Ranges contains lava dome complexes, cinder cones, and maars of basaltic-to-rhyolitic composition.

name: Mono Lake Volcanic Field
summary: The Mono Lake volcanic field east of Yosemite National Park and north of the Mono Craters consists of vents within Mono Lake and on its north shore.

name: Mono-Inyo Craters
summary: The Mono-Inyo Craters chain, on the eastern side of the Sierra Nevada between Mono Lake and Long Valley caldera, form a sickle-shaped, 25-km-long group of 35 dominantly rhyolitic lava domes, lava flows, and tephra rings.

name: Mammoth Mountain
summary: Mammoth Mountain, a trachydacitic lava-dome complex, lies on the SW topographic rim of Long Valley caldera.

name: Ubehebe Craters
summary: The Ubehebe Craters (pronounced you-bee-HEE-bee) consist of an isolated group of overlapping maars formed during eruptions of alkali basalt along a fault cutting alluvial fan deposits on the flanks of Tin Mountain in Death Valley National Park.

name: Salton Buttes
summary: The Salton Buttes consist of five small rhyolitic lava domes extruded onto Quaternary sediments of the Colorado River delta at the SE margin of the Salton Sea.

name: Black Butte Crater Lava Field
summary: The Black Butte Crater lava field is the westernmost of the young lava fields of the Eastern Snake River Plain.

name: Craters of the Moon
summary: Craters of the Moon, the largest lava field of the Snake River Plain (SRP), covers about 1,600 km2 with more than 60 mapped lava flows erupted from eight fissure systems.

name: Wapi Lava Field
summary: The Wapi Lava Field, SE of the Craters of the Moon, covers about 325 km2, and consists of a low shield volcano formed during an eruption around 300 BCE that produced ~6 km3 of pahoehoe lava flows.

name: Hell's Half Acre
summary: Hell's Half Acre, the easternmost of the young basaltic lava fields of the Snake River Plain, covers an area of about 400 km2 SW of Idaho Falls.

name: Soda Lakes
summary: Two lake-filled maars, Soda Lake and Little Soda Lake, lie NW of the town of Fallon.

name: Markagunt Plateau
summary: The Markagunt Plateau volcanic field, covering 3,000 km2 east of Cedar Breaks National Monument in SW Utah, includes basaltic cinder cones, lava vents, and sparsely vegetated lava flows.

name: Black Rock Desert
summary: The Black Rock Desert volcanic field consists of a group of closely spaced small Pleistocene-to-Holocene volcanic fields in the Black Rock and Sevier deserts of south-central Utah, at the eastern margin of the Great Basin.

name: Carrizozo
summary: The massive Carrizozo lava flow, which traveled 75 km down the Tularosa Basin of south-central New Mexico, is one of Earth's longest known Holocene lava flows.

name: Zuni-Bandera
summary: The Zuni-Bandera volcanic field covers 2,460 km2 along the Jemez lineament west of the Rio Grande Rift.

name: Red Hill-Quemado
summary: The Red Hill-Quemado volcanic field in western New Mexico is across the border from the Springerville volcanic field in Arizona and contains more than 40 cinder cones and maars that were active from the late Miocene to early Holocene.

name: Dotsero
summary: A small maar and scoria cone complex at Dotsero is located near the junction of the Colorado and Eagle Rivers west of the Gore Range.

name: Uinkaret Field
summary: The Uinkaret volcanic field straddling the Grand Canyon contains cinder cones that have produced lava flows that repeatedly cascaded into the Grand Canyon, forming temporary lava dams up to 200 m high.

name: San Francisco Volcanic Field
summary: The vast San Francisco Volcanic Field in northern Arizona has more than 550 vents, the youngest of which is Sunset Crater, named for its brilliantly colored scoria deposits on the cone.

name: West Valley Segment
summary: The West Valley Segment is the northern-most part of the Juan de Fuca Ridge, intersecting the Sovanco Fracture Zone and offset from the Endeavour Segment to the south.

name: Endeavour Segment
summary: The Endeavour Segment (or Ridge) lies near the northern end of the Juan de Fuca Ridge, W of the coast of Washington and SW of Vancouver Island.

name: Cobb Segment
summary: The Cobb Segment is in the northern part of the Juan de Fuca Ridge, south of the Endeavour Ridge segment.

name: CoAxial Segment
summary: The CoAxial segment of the Juan de Fuca Ridge is about 435 km W of the Oregon coast, NE of Axial volcano.

name: Axial Seamount
summary: Axial Seamount rises 700 m above the mean level of the central Juan de Fuca Ridge crest about 480 km W of Cannon Beach, Oregon, to within about 1,400 m of the ocean surface.

name: Cleft Segment
summary: The Cleft Segment, the southernmost of the Juan de Fuca Ridge, lies immediately north of the Blanco Fracture Zone.

name: North Gorda Ridge Segment
summary: The northernmost of five segments of the Gorda Ridge lies immediately south of the Blanco Transform Fault that offsets the Gorda and Juan de Fuca oceanic spreading ridges.

name: Jackson Segment
summary: The Jackson Segment of the Gorda Ridge more than 200 km off the coast of Oregon lies immediately SSW of the North Gorda Ridge, the northermost of five segments forming the Gorda Ridge spreading center.

name: Escanaba Segment
summary: The linear, N-S-trending Escanaba Segment, the southernmost of the Gorda Ridge, lies immediately north of the Mendocino Francture Zone off the coast of northern California.

name: East Blanco Depression
summary: The East Blanco Depression (EBD) is a pull-apart basin within the western Blanco Transform Fault Zone, a right-lateral transform fault that links the Juan de Fuca Ridge and Gorda Ridge (Dziak et al., 1996).

name: Kama'ehuakanaloa
summary: The Kama’ehuakanaloa seamount, previously known as Loihi, lies about 35 km off the SE coast of the island of Hawaii.

name: Kilauea
summary: Kilauea overlaps the E flank of the massive Mauna Loa shield volcano in the island of Hawaii.

name: Mauna Loa
summary: Massive Mauna Loa is a basaltic shield volcano that rises almost 9 km from the ocean floor to form the world's largest Holocene volcano.

name: Mauna Kea
summary: Mauna Kea, Hawaii's highest volcano, reaches 4205 m, only 35 m above its neighbor, Mauna Loa.

name: Hualalai
summary: The basaltic Hualalai, at the western end of the island, is the third youngest shield volcano on Hawaii.

name: Haleakala
summary: The massive Haleakala shield volcano forms the eastern portion of the island of Maui.

name: Teahitia
summary: Teahitia is a submarine volcano in the Society Islands whose summit reaches to within ~1,700 m of the surface, 40 km NE of the SE tip of Tahiti Island.

name: Rocard
summary: Rocard is a small volcanic seamount about 60 km WNW of Mehetia and 28 km ESE of Teahitia seamount.

name: Moua Pihaa
summary: Moua Pihaa is a massive, steep-sided submarine volcano that rises to within 160 m of the ocean surface SW of Mehetia Island.

name: Mehetia
summary: The 1.5-km-wide, steep-sided island of Mehetia (known as Me'etia or Meket'ia in the Tahitian and Tuamotuan languages, respectively), the youngest and SE-most of the Society Islands, lacks a well-developed fringing coral reef.

name: Adams Seamount
summary: Adams Seamount was constructed above the Pitcairn hot spot in the central Pacific, about 90 km WSW of Pitcairn Island.

name: Macdonald
summary: Discovered by the detection of teleseismic waves in 1967, Macdonald seamount (also known as Tamarii seamount) rises from a depth of about 1,800 m to within 27 m of the ocean surface at the eastern end of the Austral Islands.

name: Northern EPR at 17°N
summary: This second-order segment of the northern East Pacific Rise, also called Segment RO2, lies between the Orozco and Rivera transform faults, south of the Rivera transform.

name: Northern EPR at 16°N
summary: This second-order segment of the northern East Pacific Rise, also called Segment RO3, lies between the Orozco and Rivera transform faults, immediately north of the Orozco transform.

name: Northern EPR at 10.7°N
summary: Divers in the submersible Alvin discovered an extremely fresh lava flow in an unexpected location at 10°44'N on the East Pacific Rise during an expedition in November 2003.

name: Northern EPR at 9.8°N
summary: A series of dives with the submersible Alvin in 1991 on the East Pacific Rise at about 9°50'N detected evidence for a very recent, possibly ongoing, eruption.

name: Galapagos Rift at 86°W
summary: The Galápagos Rift is an oceanic spreading ridge between the Cocos plate to the north and the Nazca plate to the south.

name: Southern EPR at 8°S
summary: A massive 15 +/- 4 km3 lava flow field covers about 220 km2 of the East Pacific Rise (EPR) axis crest at about 8°S.

name: Southern EPR at 17.5°S (Segment K)
summary: Lava flows from a very recent eruption were observed in 1994 along segment K of the southern East Pacific Rise.

name: Southern EPR at 18.2°S (Segment J)
summary: The axial crest of Segment J of the Southern East Pacific Rise consists of an asymmetrical shallow graben varying from 250 to 600 m wide with walls about 20 m high.

name: Southern EPR at 18.5°S (Segment I)
summary: The narrow axial crest of Segment I of the Southern East Pacific Rise in some places is less than 50 m wide.

name: Hollister Ridge
summary: Acoustic T-waves from a seismic swarm, possibly associated with magmatic activity, were recorded in 1991 from a location 130 km S of the Eltanin Fracture Zone (Bulletin of the Global Volcanism Network, 1991).

name: Udintsev Transform
summary: Acoustic signals (T-waves) from a seismic swarm were detected in 1990 from a source along the Udintsev fracture zone at about 143°W, along the segment that corresponds with the Pacific-Antarctic Ridge (Global Volcanism Network Bulletin, 1990).

name: Pinacate
summary: Pinacate is a roughly 55 x 60 km volcanic field in the Sonoran desert of NW México.

name: San Luis, Isla
summary: Isla San Luis is the largest of the seven Encantada islands at the NW end of the Guaymas lineament in the northern part of the Gulf of California.

name: Jaraguay Volcanic Field
summary: The Jaraguay Volcanic Field is the northernmost of a group of large young alkalic volcanic fields in Baja California.

name: San Borja Volcanic Field
summary: The San Borja (or El Rosarito) volcanic field, is located in central Baja California NE of the Vizcaino Peninsula.

name: Tortuga, Isla
summary: A youthful shield volcano forms Isla Tortuga, which lies in the Gulf of California, 40 km off the Baja coast.

name: Comondu-La Purisima
summary: The Comondú-La Purísima volcanic field, located in southern Baja California, west of the Sierra de la Giganta, dates back to the Miocene.

name: Barcena
summary: Volcán Bárcena, formed by eruptions during 1952-53, is the most prominent feature of the 4.5-km-long Isla San Benedicto, the NE-most of the Revillagigedo Islands, 350 km S of the tip of Baja California.

name: Socorro
summary: Socorro, the SE-most of the Revillagigedo Islands south of Baja California, is the summit of a massive, predominately submarine basaltic shield volcano capped by a largely buried, 4.5 x 3.8-km-wide summit caldera.

name: Durango Volcanic Field
summary: The broad Durango volcanic field covers 2,100 km2 at the NW corner of the Meseta Central near the eastern edge of the Sierra Madre Occidental of north-central México.

name: Sanganguey
summary: Volcán Sangangüey, the highest volcano of the NW-SE-trending Tepic-Zacoalco graben, is an eroded andesitic and dacitic stratovolcano that contains a prominent lava spine at its summit.

name: Ceboruco
summary: Volcán Ceboruco is the only volcano in the NW part of the Mexican Volcanic Belt with observed eruptions.

name: Mascota Volcanic Field
summary: A group of calc-alkaline andesitic and lamprophyre cinder cones and lava domes, along with associated lava flows, is located near the town of Mascota about 50 km E of Puerto Vallarta.

name: Colima
summary: The Colima complex is the most prominent volcanic center of the western Mexican Volcanic Belt.

name: Michoacan-Guanajuato
summary: The widespread Michoacán-Guanajuato volcanic field contains over 1,400 vents, including the historically active cinder cones of Parícutin and Jorullo, covering a 200 x 250 km wide area of Michoacán and Guanajuato states in west-central México.

name: Zitacuaro-Valle de Bravo
summary: The Zitácuaro-Valle de Bravo volcanic field in the central part of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt consists of a broad region of shield volcanoes, lava domes, and cinder cones surrounding the city of Heroica de Zitácuaro.

name: Jocotitlan
summary: The composite Jocotitlán volcano, which rises above the Toluca basin 60 km WNW of Mexico City, was constructed during the Pleistocene of andesitic-to-dacitic lava flows.

name: Toluca, Nevado de
summary: Nevado de Toluca, México's fourth highest peak, rises above the Toluca basin about 80 km W of Mexico City.

name: Chichinautzin
summary: The massive Chichinautzin volcanic field extends over an 88 km E-W area immediately south of Mexico City.

name: Iztaccihuatl
summary: Iztaccíhuatl (the "Woman in White") presents the profile of a sleeping woman as seen from the Valley of Mexico.

name: Popocatepetl
summary: Volcán Popocatépetl, whose name is the Aztec word for smoking mountain, rises 70 km SE of Mexico City to form North America's 2nd-highest volcano.

name: Malinche, La
summary: La Malinche is an eroded stratovolcano, cut by deep canyons, NE of the city of Puebla.

name: Serdan-Oriental Volcanic Field
summary: The Serdán-Oriental Volcanic Field, covering an area 35-40 km E-W and 60 km N-S, includes numerous late Pleistocene to Holocene rhyolitic lava domes, tuff cones, tuff rings, lava flows, and scoria cones.

name: Humeros, Los
summary: Los Humeros is the easternmost of a series of silicic volcanic centers with active geothermal systems located north of the axis of the Mexican Volcanic Belt.

name: Naolinco Volcanic Field
summary: The Naolinco Volcanic Field in the Sierra de Chiconquiaco range north of Jalapa (Xalapa), Veracruz, consists of a broad area of scattered Quaternary pyroclastic cones and associated dominantly basaltic lava flows.

name: Orizaba, Pico de
summary: Pico de Orizaba (Volcán Citlaltépetl), México's highest peak and North America's highest volcano, lies at the southern end of a volcanic chain extending north to Cofre de Perote volcano, east of the Serdan-Oriental Basin.

name: San Martin
summary: Volcán de San Martín, part of the Tuxtla Volcanic Field, is a broad alkaline shield volcano that rises above the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Chichon, El
summary: El Chichón is a small trachyandesitic tuff cone and lava dome complex in an isolated part of the Chiapas region in SE México.

name: Tacana
summary: Tacaná is a 4064-m-high composite stratovolcano that straddles the México/Guatemala border at the NW end of the Central American volcanic belt.

name: Tajumulco
summary: Tajumulco is Guatemala's highest peak and the highest volcano in Central America.

name: Santa Maria
summary: Symmetrical, forest-covered Santa María volcano is part of a chain of large stratovolcanoes that rise above the Pacific coastal plain of Guatemala.

name: Almolonga
summary: Volcán de Almolonga is an andesitic stratovolcano with a 3.3-km-wide late-Pleistocene central caldera that is located along the Zunil fault zone.

name: Atitlan
summary: Volcán Atitlán is one of several conical stratovolcanoes in the Guatemalan highlands.

name: Toliman
summary: Volcán Tolimán is a large andesitic stratovolcano that rises above the S shore of Lake Atitlán.

name: Acatenango
summary: Acatenango is ~15 km SW of the city of Antigua, Guatemala, and 3 km N of Fuego volcano.

name: Fuego
summary: Volcán Fuego, one of Central America's most active volcanoes, is also one of three large stratovolcanoes overlooking Guatemala's former capital, Antigua.

name: Agua
summary: The symmetrical, forested Volcán de Agua stratovolcano forms an impressive backdrop to the city of Antigua, Guatemala, opposite from the Fuego and Acatenango volcanoes.

name: Pacaya
summary: Eruptions from Pacaya are frequently visible from Guatemala City, the nation's capital.

name: Cuilapa-Barbarena
summary: The Cuilapa-Barbarena volcanic field contains approximately 70 Quaternary cinder cones, generally less than 100 m high.

name: Tecuamburro
summary: Tecuamburro is a small forested stratovolcano, or large lava-dome complex, about 50 km ESE of Guatemala City and 20 km S of the main volcanic chain.

name: Jumaytepeque
summary: Jumaytepeque is a small basaltic stratovolcano located NNE of the city of Cuilapa, north of the major NW-SE-trending Jalpatagua fault that cuts diagonally across SE Guatemala.

name: Moyuta
summary: Moyuta is the easternmost of a chain of large stratovolcanoes extending along the volcanic front of Guatemala.

name: Flores
summary: Volcán de Flores is one of the largest of a cluster of small stratovolcanoes located in SE Guatemala behind the volcanic front.

name: Tahual
summary: Deeply dissected Volcán Tahual rises ~700 m above plains S of the town of Monjas.

name: Santiago, Cerro
summary: A cluster of cinder cones and low shield volcanoes surrounds the city of Jutiapa in SE Guatemala.

name: Suchitan
summary: The summit of the andesitic-to-basaltic Volcán Suchitán stratovolcano, NE of the city of Jutiapa, is elongated N-S.

name: Chingo
summary: Volcán Chingo is a symmetrical stratovolcano that straddles the Guatemala/El Salvador border.

name: Ixtepeque
summary: Ixtepeque volcano, which takes its name from the Aztec word for obsidian, is perhaps the largest obsidian field in North America.

name: Singuil, Cerro
summary: The most prominent feature of a volcanic field in the interior valley of El Salvador near the Guatemalan border SE of Volcán Chingo is Cerro Singüil.

name: Apaneca Range
summary: The Apaneca Range (also known as the Cuyanausul Range) consists of a group of basaltic-to-andesitic Pleistocene and Holocene stratovolcanoes in western El Salvador between the Santa Ana complex and the Guatemala border.

name: Santa Ana
summary: Santa Ana (also known as Ilamatepec), is a massive, dominantly andesitic-to-trachyandesitic stratovolcano in El Salvador immediately W of Coatepeque Caldera.

name: Izalco
summary: Volcán de Izalco began growing in 1770 CE on the southern flank of Santa Ana volcano, eventually building a steep 650-m-high stratovolcano truncated by a 250-m-wide summit crater.

name: Coatepeque Caldera
summary: Coatepeque is a 6.5 x 11.5 km collapse caldera ~50 km W of San Salvador that is largely occupied by a lake with hot springs near the margins.

name: San Salvador
summary: The massive compound San Salvador volcano dominates the landscape W of El Salvador's capital city of San Salvador.

name: Cinotepeque, Cerro
summary: Cerro Cinotepeque is the largest and most prominent of a group of four pyroclastic cones mapped as Holocene by Weber and Weismann (1978) in low-lying areas on either side of the Río Lempa, ~40 km N of San Salvador.

name: Ilopango
summary: The 8 x 11 km Ilopango caldera, filled by one of El Salvador's largest lakes, has a scalloped 150-500 m high rim.

name: San Vicente
summary: San Vicente stratovolcano, also known as Chichontepec, is ~20 km SE of Lake Ilopango.

name: Taburete
summary: Taburete volcano rises above the Pacific coastal plain E of the Río Lempa at the SW end of a cluster of volcanoes between San Vincente and San Miguel volcanoes.

name: Tecapa
summary: Tecapa is a complex basaltic-to-andesitic stratovolcano at the NW end of a cluster of volcanoes E of the Río Lempa between San Vicente and San Miguel volcanoes.

name: Usulutan
summary: Usulután volcano anchors the SE end of a cluster of basaltic to basaltic andesite stratovolcanoes between San Vicente and San Miguel volcanoes.

name: Tigre, El
summary: Cerro el Tigre is the highest, NE-most, and oldest of the cluster of coalescing basaltic to basaltic andesite Quaternary volcanoes between the Río Lempa and San Miguel volcano.

name: Chinameca
summary: The small Chinameca stratovolcano (also known as El Pacayal) lies across a low saddle abotu 7 km NW of the large San Miguel volcano.

name: San Miguel
summary: The symmetrical cone of San Miguel, one of the most active volcanoes in El Salvador, rises from near sea level to form one of the country's most prominent landmarks.

name: Aramuaca, Laguna
summary: A solitary, 1-km-wide, lake-filled maar, Laguna Aramuaca, occupies a low-lying area about 10 km SE of the city of San Miguel.

name: Tigre, Isla del
summary: Isla del Tigre is a small, 5-km-wide island located across a narrow 2-km-wide strait S of Isla Zacate Grande in the Gulf of Fonseca.

name: Zacate Grande, Isla
summary: Zacate Grande volcano forms a low island 7 x 10 km wide across a narrow strait from the end of a peninsula surrounded on three sides by the Gulf of Fonseca and Chismuyo bay.

name: Yojoa, Lago
summary: The Lago Yojoa volcanic field consists a group of Pleistocene-to-Holocene scoria cones and collapse pits (Williams and McBirney, 1969).

name: Cosiguina
summary: Cosigüina (also spelled Cosegüina) is a low basaltic-to-andesitic composite volcano that is isolated from other eruptive centers in the Nicaraguan volcanic chain.

name: San Cristobal
summary: The San Cristóbal volcanic complex, consisting of five principal volcanic edifices, forms the NW end of the Marrabios Range.

name: Telica
summary: Telica, one of Nicaragua's most active volcanoes, has erupted frequently since the beginning of the Spanish era.

name: Negro, Cerro
summary: Nicaragua's youngest volcano, Cerro Negro, was created following an eruption that began in April 1850 about 2 km NW of the summit of Las Pilas volcano.

name: Las Pilas-El Hoyo Complex
summary: Las Pilas-El Hoyo volcanic complex, overlooking Cerro Negro volcano to the NW, includes a diverse cluster of cones within about a 3-km-diameter area.

name: Momotombo
summary: Momotombo is a young stratovolcano that rises prominently above the NW shore of Lake Managua, forming one of Nicaragua's most familiar landmarks.

name: Apoyeque
summary: The Apoyeque volcanic complex occupies the broad Chiltepe Peninsula, which extends into south-central Lake Managua.

name: Nejapa-Miraflores
summary: The Nejapa-Miraflores alignment (also known as Nejapa-Ticoma), ~10 km S of Apoyeque near the western margin of the Nicaraguan graben, cuts through the western part of the capital city of Managua and marks the right-lateral offset of the volcanic arc in….

name: Masaya
