summary: Masaya volcano in Nicaragua has erupted frequently since the time of the Spanish Conquistadors, when an active lava lake prompted attempts to extract the volcano's molten "gold" until it was found to be basalt rock upon cooling.

name: Granada
summary: The Granada lineament, also known as the La Joya alignment, is an arcuate fissure extending from about 2 km SE of the Apoyo caldera rim around to N of the city of Granada.

name: Mombacho
summary: Mombacho is an andesitic and basaltic stratovolcano on the shores of Lake Nicaragua south of the city of Granada that has undergone edifice collapse on several occasions.

name: Zapatera
summary: Zapatera is a small low shield volcano that forms a 7 x 10 km wide island on the western side of Lake Nicaragua just offshore from Mombacho volcano.

name: Concepcion
summary: Volcán Concepción is a symmetrical basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano that forms the NW half of the dumbbell-shaped island of Ometepe in Lake Nicaragua and is connected to neighboring Madera volcano by a narrow isthmus.

name: Orosi
summary: Orosí is one of a cluster of four eroded and vegetated cones in the Guanacaste Range at the NW corner of Costa Rica.

name: Rincon de la Vieja
summary: Rincón de la Vieja is a volcanic complex in the Guanacaste Range of NW Costa Rica.

name: Miravalles
summary: Miravalles is an andesitic stratovolcano that is one of five post-caldera cones along a NE-trending line within the broad 15 x 20 km Guayabo (Miravalles) caldera.

name: Tenorio
summary: The 225 km2 dominantly andesitic Tenorio volcanic massif anchors the SE end of the Guanacaste Range and consists of a cluster of densely forested NNW-SSE-trending volcanic cones.

name: Arenal
summary: Conical Volcán Arenal is the youngest stratovolcano in Costa Rica and one of its most active.

name: Platanar
summary: The Platanar volcanic center is the NW-most volcano in the Cordillera Central of Costa Rica.

name: Poas
summary: The broad vegetated edifice of Poás, one of the most active volcanoes of Costa Rica, contains three craters along a N-S line.

name: Barva
summary: One of three massive volcanoes close to the capital city of San José, Volcán Barva (Barba) is a complex volcano with multiple peaks and flank vents.

name: Irazu
summary: The massive Irazú volcano in Costa Rica, immediately E of the capital city of San José, covers an area of 500 km2 and is vegetated to within a few hundred meters of its broad summit crater complex.

name: Turrialba
summary: Turrialba, the easternmost of Costa Rica's Holocene volcanoes, is a large vegetated basaltic-to-dacitic stratovolcano located across a broad saddle NE of Irazú volcano overlooking the city of Cartago.

name: Baru
summary: The westernmost volcano in Panamá, Barú, is a complex dominantly andesitic stratovolcano in the Talamanca Range near the Costa Rica border.

name: Romeral
summary: The andesitic-to-dacitic Romeral stratovolcano lies at the northern end of the Ruiz-Tolima volcanic chain, NW of Cerro Bravo volcano, and east of the towns of Neira and Aranzazu.

name: Bravo, Cerro
summary: Cerro Bravo is a relatively low dominantly dacitic lava-dome complex north of Nevado del Ruiz that was constructed within the Pleistocene Quebrada Seca caldera.

name: Ruiz, Nevado del
summary: Nevado del Ruiz is a broad, glacier-covered volcano in central Colombia that covers more than 200 km2.

name: Santa Isabel
summary: Santa Isabel is a small andesitic shield volcano that is dwarfed by its neighbors to the NE (Nevado del Ruiz) and SE (Tolima).

name: Tolima, Nevado del
summary: The steep-sided, glacier-covered Nevado del Tolima volcano contrasts with the broad profile of Nevado del Ruiz to the north.

name: Machin
summary: The small Cerro Machín stratovolcano lies at the southern end of the Ruiz-Tolima massif about 20 km WNW of the city of Ibagué.

name: Huila, Nevado del
summary: Nevado del Huila, the highest peak in the Colombian Andes, is an elongated N-S-trending volcanic chain mantled by a glacier icecap.

name: Purace
summary: Puracé is an active andesitic volcano with a 600-m-diameter summit crater at the NW end of the Los Coconucos Volcanic Chain.

name: Sotara
summary: Volcán Sotará, also known as Cerro Azafatudo, is an  andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano about 25 km SSE of Popayán city in southern Colombia, SW of Puracé volcano.

name: Dona Juana
summary: The forested Doña Juana stratovolcano contains two calderas, breached to the NE and SW.

name: Galeras
summary: Galeras, a stratovolcano with a large breached caldera located immediately west of the city of Pasto, is one of Colombia's most frequently active volcanoes.

name: Azufral
summary: Azufral stratovolcano in southern Colombia, also known as Azufral de Túquerres, is truncated by a 2.5 x 3 km caldera containing a Holocene rhyodacitic lava-dome complex.

name: Cumbal
summary: Many youthful lava flows extend from the glacier-capped Cumbal volcano, the southernmost historically active volcano of Colombia.

name: Chiles-Cerro Negro
summary: The Chiles-Cerro Negro volcanic complex includes both the Pleistocene Chiles and the Cerro Negro de Mayasquer stratovolcanoes astride the Colombia-Ecuador border.

name: Soche
summary: Volcán el Soche, a small stratovolcano near the Colombia border, is the northernmost of a chain of Ecuadorian volcanoes east of the principal volcanic axis.

name: Chachimbiro
summary: The Chachimbiro volcanic complex lies about 25 km NW of the city of Ibarra.

name: Cuicocha
summary: The scenic lake-filled Cuicocha caldera is located at the southern foot of the sharp-peaked Pleistocene Cotacachi stratovolcano about 100 km N of Quito.

name: Imbabura
summary: Imbabura volcano rises to the north above scenic Laguna de San Pablo in the Interandean valley about 60 km N of Quito.

name: Mojanda
summary: Mojanda, one of the largest volcanoes of Ecuador's northern Interandean Depression, rises SW of the historic town of Otavalo.

name: Cayambe
summary: The massive compound andesitic-dacitic Cayambe stratovolcano is located on the western edge of the Cordillera Real, east of the Inter-Andean Valley.

name: Reventador
summary: Volcán El Reventador is the most frequently active of a chain of Ecuadorian volcanoes in the Cordillera Real, well east of the principal volcanic axis.

name: Pululahua
summary: Pululahua is a relatively low, forested volcano about 15 km N of Quito.

name: Guagua Pichincha
summary: Guagua Pichincha and the older Pleistocene Rucu Pichincha stratovolcanoes form a broad volcanic massif that rises immediately W of Ecuador's capital city, Quito.

name: Atacazo
summary: Atacazo, located about 25 km SW of Quito, consists of a large Pleistocene andesitic stratovolcanoes truncated by a late-Pleistocene to Holocene caldera.

name: Chacana
summary: Chacana is a massive, eroded caldera complex of Pliocene-Holocene age that forms one of the largest rhyolitic centers of the northern Andes.

name: Antisana
summary: Antisana is a massive, glacier-covered stratovolcano NE of Cotopaxi, along the western margin of the Eastern Cordillera, 50 km SE of Quito.

name: Aliso
summary: The Aliso volcanic complex lies at the eastern foot of the Ecuadorian Andes, east of Antisana volcano and SW of the town of Baeza.

name: Sumaco
summary: The forested Sumaco stratovolcano rises above the jungles of the western Amazon basin, east of Antisana volcano, and occupies an isolated position far to the east of the main Andes volcanic axis.

name: Iliniza
summary: The two glacier-covered peaks of Iliniza volcano are prominent landmarks west of the Interandean Valley.

name: Cotopaxi
summary: The symmetrical, glacier-covered, Cotopaxi stratovolcano is Ecuador's most well-known volcano and one of its most active.

name: Quilotoa
summary: Quilotoa is a truncated, dacitic cone in the Western Cordillera of Ecuador, 35 km WNW of the city of Latacunga, that contains a 3-km-wide caldera with steep-sided walls that rise 400 m above the surface of 240-m-deep caldera lake.

name: Chimborazo
summary: Glacier-clad Chimborazo, Ecuador's highest volcano, anchors the southern end of the country's "Avenue of Volcanoes" 30 km NW of the city of Riobamba.

name: Tungurahua
summary: Tungurahua, a steep-sided andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano that towers more than 3 km above its northern base, is one of Ecuador's most active volcanoes.

name: Licto
summary: The Licto group of scoria cones lies along the Río Chambo ~25 km SE of the city of Riobamba and just north of the town of Licto.

name: Sangay
summary: The isolated Sangay volcano, located east of the Andean crest, is the southernmost of Ecuador's volcanoes and its most active.

name: Fernandina
summary: Fernandina, the most active of Galápagos volcanoes and the one closest to the Galápagos mantle plume, is a basaltic shield volcano with a deep 5 x 6.5 km summit caldera.

name: Ecuador
summary: Volcán Ecuador straddles the equator at the NW end of Isabela Island.

name: Wolf
summary: Volcán Wolf, the highest volcano of the Galápagos Islands, straddles the equator at the north end of the archipelago's largest island, Isabela.

name: Darwin
summary: Volcán Darwin, named after the renowned naturalist, contains a symmetrical 5-km-wide, 200-m-deep summit caldera whose floor is nearly covered by youthful lava flows.

name: Alcedo
summary: Alcedo is one of the lowest and smallest of six shield volcanoes on Isabela Island.

name: Negra, Sierra
summary: The broad shield volcano of Sierra Negra at the southern end of Isabela Island contains a shallow 7 x 10.5 km caldera that is the largest in the Galápagos Islands.

name: Azul, Cerro
summary: Located at the SW tip of the J-shaped Isabela Island, Cerro Azul contains a steep-walled 4 x 5 km nested summit caldera complex that is one of the smallest diameter, but at 650 m one of the deepest in the Galápagos Islands.

name: Pinta
summary: The elongated island of Pinta is a shield volcano with numerous cones and lava flows originating from NNW-trending fissures.

name: Marchena
summary: The low shield volcano forming Marchena Island contains one of the largest calderas of the Galápagos Islands.

name: Genovesa
summary: The small, very low island of Genovesa is the top of a shield volcano.

name: Santiago
summary: The elongated shield volcano of Santiago Island, also known as San Salvador Island or James Island, has numerous scattered Holocene pyroclastic cones.

name: Santa Cruz
summary: The highlands of the broad Santa Cruz shield volcano rise to the N above the Charles Darwin Research Station at Academy Bay.

name: San Cristobal
summary: San Cristóbal Island consists of a densely vegetated western part and a lower, younger eastern part with many unvegetated lava flows.

name: Quimsachata-Oroscocha
summary: The Quimsachata-Oroscocha group consists of two late Pleistocene and Holocene monogenetic volcanoes at the foot of the Cordillera Oriental, far east of the main volcanic front.

name: Auquihuato, Cerro
summary: The Cerro Auquihuato cinder cone lies ~30 km NE of Sara Sara volcano.

name: Coropuna
summary: Nevado Coropuna is a massive ice-covered volcanic complex with multiple summit cones built over a 12 x 20 km area.

name: Andahua-Orcopampa
summary: The Andahua-Orcopampa volcanic field in the Andahua (or Andagua) valley area, 20 km ENE of Nevados de Coropuna, is a large 60 x 60 km scoria cone and lava field.

name: Huambo
summary: The monogenetic Huambo volcanic field lies SSE of the Andahua-Orcocampo volcanic field, west of Sabancaya volcano.

name: Sabancaya
summary: Sabancaya, located in the saddle NE of Ampato and SE of Hualca Hualca volcanoes, is the youngest of these volcanic centers and the only one to have erupted in historical time.

name: Misti, El
summary: El Misti is a symmetrical andesitic stratovolcano with nested summit craters immediately NE of the city of Arequipa, Peru.

name: Ubinas
summary: The truncated appearance of Ubinas, Perú's most active volcano, is a result of a 1.4-km-wide crater at the summit.

name: Huaynaputina
summary: Huaynaputina (whose name means "new volcano") was the source of the largest historical eruption of South America in 1600 CE.

name: Ticsani
summary: Ticsani is a dacitic lava dome complex in the Ichuna district of Peru, about 30 km SE of Huaynaputina volcano.

name: Tutupaca
summary: Tutupaca consists of two dissected volcanic edifices, of which the southern appears more youthful.

name: Yucamane
summary: Volcán Yucamane lies at the south end of a group of three volcanoes known as the Caliente-Yucamane Volcanic Complex; both it and Cerro Caliente to the north display evidence of postglacial lava flows, which overlie thick moraines.

name: Casiri, Nevados
summary: The Nevados Casiri compound volcano in Peru, also known as Paugarani, lies near the Chilean border ~25 km N of Tacora volcano.

name: Taapaca
summary: The Taapaca volcanic complex, lying W of the main Andean chain, rises NE of the small town of Putre, the principal settlement of the northern Chilean Altiplano.

name: Parinacota
summary: The symmetrical Volcán Parinacota is the southernmost and youngest of a pair of volcanoes forming the Nevados de Payachata group along the Chile-Bolivia border.

name: Guallatiri
summary: One of northern Chile's most active volcanoes, Volcán Guallatiri is a symmetrical ice-clad stratovolcano at the SW end of the Nevados de Quimsachata volcano group.

name: Isluga
summary: The broad Isluga volcano lies 7 km W of the Chile/Bolivia border at the W end of a group of volcanoes extending to Tata Sabaya volcano in Bolivia.

name: Tata Sabaya
summary: The symmetrical Tata Sabaya towers above the northern end of the Salar de Coipasa in the Altiplano of Bolivia.

name: Irruputuncu
summary: Irruputuncu is a small stratovolcano that straddles the Chile/Bolivia border.

name: Olca-Paruma
summary: A 15-km-long E-W ridge forming the border between Chile and Bolivia is comprised of several stratovolcanoes with Holocene lava flows.

name: Putana
summary: Volcán Putana, also known as Jorgencal or Machuca, is part of a large, roughly N-S-trending volcanic complex that covers an area of 600 km2.

name: Sairecabur
summary: This chain of andesitic-dacitic volcanoes along the Chile-Bolivia border contains at least 10 postglacial centers and stretches from Escalante volcano in the N to Sairecábur volcano in the S.

name: Licancabur
summary: The symmetrical steep-sided Licancabur stratovolcano was constructed primarily during the Holocene and contains a lake in its 400-m-wide summit crater.

name: Guayaques
summary: The Cerros de Guayaques group of N-S-trending rhyodacitic lava domes straddles the Chile-Bolivia border.

name: Purico Complex
summary: The Purico volcanic complex consists of two ignimbrite sheets, separated by a short erosional interval, that were erupted about 1.3 million years ago, along with several stratovolcanoes and lava domes that define a postulated 10 x 20 km ring fracture.

name: Colachi
summary: Colachi is a andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano that was constructed on an uplifted block of welded ignimbrites.

name: Acamarachi
summary: Acamarachi, a steep-sided andesitic-dacitic volcano, forms the highest peak in this part of the northern Andes.

name: Chiliques
summary: Volcán Chiliques is a structurally simple stratovolcano located immediately south of Laguna Lejía.

name: Lascar
summary: Láscar is the most active volcano of the northern Chilean Andes.

name: Cordon de Puntas Negras
summary: Two intersecting volcanic chains, the Cordón de Puntas Negras and Cordón Chalviri, trend roughly SE from Chiliques volcano to Volcán Puntas Negras stratovolcano and SW from there to Cerro Tuyajto, respectively.

name: Miniques
summary: Volcán Miñiques is a large basaltic andesite to dacitic volcanic complex S of Laguna Miscanti and Laguna Miñiques.

name: Tujle, Cerro
summary: The Cerro Tujle maar (also known as Cerro Tucle or Cerro Tugle) in the Cordón de Tujle has a 60-m-deep crater (de Silva and Francis, 1991).

name: Caichinque
summary: Caichinque is a relatively small Pleistocene-Holocene volcanic complex that forms a topographic high dividing Salar Capur from Salar Talar.

name: Tilocalar
summary: Two small eruptive vents that produced lava flows lie about 3 km apart in the Callejón de Tilocálar area.

name: Pular
summary: Cerro Pular on the NE end and Cerro Pajonales on the SW form a 12-km-long volcanic ridge NE of Socompa volcano that is mostly pre-Holocene, but may have experienced some more recent activity.

name: Negrillar, La
summary: The basaltic andesite La Negrillar cone and lava flow complex (also known as Aguas Perdidas) covers a roughly 50 km2 area along the SW margin of the Atacama basin about 35 km WNW of Socompa volcano between the small Sierra San Juan and Sierra Almeida ranges.

name: Socompa
summary: Straddling the Chile-Argentina border, Volcán Socompa is a massive dacitic stratovolcano that lies immediately north of the only railway line between the two countries.

name: Llullaillaco
summary: The world's highest historically active volcano, Llullaillaco sits astride the Chile-Argentina border.

name: Corrida de Cori Volcanic Field
summary: Cerro Escorial, a small andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano, has young-looking lava flows and a well-preserved crater.

name: Lastarria
summary: The NNW-trending edifice of 5706-m-high Lastarria volcano along the Chile-Argentina border contains five nested summit craters.

name: Cordon del Azufre
summary: Cordón del Azufre is a small volcanic complex straddling the Chile-Argentina border.

name: Bayo Gorbea, Cerro
summary: Cerro Bayo is a complex volcano of partial Holocene age located along the Chile-Argentina border.

name: Nevada, Sierra
summary: The Sierra Nevada volcanic complex, located in one of the most inaccessible parts of the Central Andes, covers an area of about 225 km2 astride the Chile-Argentina border.

name: Falso Azufre
summary: The Falso Azufre volcanic complex is a 15-km-long, E-W trending group of overlapping craters, lava domes, and composite cones extending from Chile into Argentina.

name: Incahuasi, Nevado de
summary: Nevado de Incahuasi is a complex volcanic massif that straddles the Chile-Argentina border ENE of Nevados Ojos del Salado volcano.

name: Ojos del Salado, Nevados
summary: The world's highest active volcano, Nevados Ojos del Salado, rises to 6,879 m along the Chile-Argentina border.

name: Solo, El
summary: El Solo is large stratovolcano composed of nine eruptive centers located west of Nevados del Ojos de Salado and SE of Tres Cruces volcano.

name: Aracar
summary: Aracar is a steep-sided stratovolcano with a youthful-looking summit crater 1-1.5 km in diameter that contains a small lake.

name: Central Andean Arc at 25.1°S
summary: An isolated basaltic andesite cinder cone was constructed on top of Miocene ignimbrites and lava flows between the Corrida de Cori range on the Chile/Argentina border and the Salar Río Grande in Argentina.

name: Condor, El
summary: The compound volcano of Cerro el Cóndor, one of the few large stratovolcanoes located wholly in Argentina, lies within a 2.5-km-wide caldera.

name: Peinado
summary: The symmetrical Cerro Peinado stratovolcano in Argentina is the source of well-preserved Holocene lava flows from summit and flank vents (de Silva and Francis, 1991).

name: Blanco, Cerro
summary: The Cerro Blanco volcanic complex contains the 5-km-diameter Cerro Blanco (or Robledo) caldera in NW Argentina, 80 km SW of the Cerro Galán caldera.

name: Tipas
summary: This massive volcanic complex is the world's third highest active volcano, but remains largely unknown.

name: Rapa Nui
summary: The triangular Rapa Nui (also known as Isla de Pascua, or Easter Island), is renowned for its dramatic megalithic statues of hand-carved basalt.

name: Tupungatito
summary: Tupungatito volcano, the northernmost historically active volcano of the central Chilean Andes, is located along the Chile-Argentina border about 90 km E of Santiago and immediately SW of the Pleistocene Tupungato volcano.

name: San Jose
summary: Volcán San José lies along the Chile-Argentina border at the southern end of a volcano group that includes the Pleistocene volcanoes of Marmolejo and Espíritu Santo.

name: Maipo
summary: Maipo, a conical stratovolcano that straddles the Chile-Argentina border SE of Santiago, partially fills the 16 x 20 km Pleistocene Diamante caldera, which formed about 450,000 years ago during an eruption that produced an about 350 km3 of rhyolitic….

name: Palomo
summary: Palomo is a small stratovolcano that is somewhat dissected by glaciers.

name: Atuel, Caldera del
summary: The 30 x 45 km Caldera del Atuel complex, ~30 km NW-SE and 45 km NE-SW, lies just east of the Argentina-Chile border and 18 km SSW of the rim of the Pleistocene Diamante caldera.

name: Risco Plateado
summary: The Risco Plateado volcanic complex lies about 10 km S of the Caldera del Atuel and consists of a stratovolcano cut by a 4-km-wide caldera.

name: Tinguiririca
summary: Tinguiririca is composed of at least seven Holocene scoria cones W of the Chile-Argentina border constructed along a NNE-SSW fissure over an eroded Pleistocene stratovolcano.

name: Planchon-Peteroa
summary: Planchón-Peteroa is an elongated complex volcano along the Chile-Argentina border with several overlapping calderas.

name: Infiernillo
summary: Infiernillo, a late-Pleistocene to Holocene basaltic andesite volcanic field along the Río Salado in Argentina lies about 70 km east of the crest of the Andes and NW of the town of Malargüe.

name: Calabozos
summary: The composite late-Pleistocene Calabozos caldera (14 x 26 km) produced major rhyodacitic-to-dacitic ashflow sheets of ~200-500 km3 each, collectively referred to as the Loma Seca Tuff, at 800,000, 300,000, and 150,000 years ago.

name: Descabezado Grande
summary: Volcán Descabezado Grande is a late-Pleistocene to Holocene andesitic-to-rhyodacitic stratovolcano with a 1.4-km-wide ice-filled summit crater.

name: Azul, Cerro
summary: The Cerro Azul stratovolcano is at the southern end of the Descabezado Grande-Cerro Azul eruptive system.

name: Maule, Laguna del
summary: The Laguna del Maule volcanic complex includes a 15 x 25 km caldera with a cluster of small stratovolcanoes, lava domes, and pyroclastic cones of Pleistocene-to-Holocene age.

name: San Pedro-Pellado
summary: The San Pedro-Pellado volcanic complex (also known as San Pedro-Tatara) has been active from the Pliocene to the Holocene.

name: Longavi, Nevado de
summary: The conical Nevado de Longaví is a late-Pleistocene to Holocene, dominantly andesitic stratovolcano constructed over a basement of Tertiary volcaniclastic and granitic rocks.

name: Blancas, Lomas
summary: Volcán Lomas Blancas is a small shield-like feature of late-Pleistocene to Holocene age (Moreno and Naranjo, 1991) located about 15 km SE of Nevado de Longaví.

name: Resago, Volcan
summary: Volcán Resago, in the Linares province of central Chile, is a cinder cone with a double crater.

name: Payun Matru
summary: The Payún Matrú volcanic field in Argentina includes a massive hawaiian-style shield volcano that lies 530 km from the oceanic trench.

name: Chillan, Nevados de
summary: The compound volcano of Nevados de Chillán is one of the most active of the Central Andes.

name: Tromen Volcanic Plateau
summary: Tromen is an Argentinian stratovolcano that is the primary structure in an elongated volcanic plateau or field that extends about 70 km from Tilhue in the S to Piujenta in the N, including the Boliviano caldera and Palao dome.

name: Antuco
summary: Antuco volcano, constructed NE of the Pleistocene Sierra Velluda stratovolcano, rises dramatically above the SW shore of Laguna de la Laja.

name: Copahue
summary: Volcán Copahue is an elongated composite cone constructed along the Chile-Argentina border within the 6.5 x 8.5 km wide Trapa-Trapa caldera that formed between 0.6 and 0.4 million years ago near the NW margin of the 20 x 15 km Pliocene Caviahue (Del Agrio)….

name: Callaqui
summary: The late-Pleistocene to Holocene Callaqui stratovolcano has a profile of an overturned canoe, due to its construction along an 11-km-long, SW-NE fissure above a 1.2-0.3 million year old Pleistocene edifice.

name: Tolhuaca
summary: Tolhuaca (or Tolguaca) is a late-Pleistocene to Holocene stratovolcano located immediately NW of Lonquimay volcano.

name: Lonquimay
summary: Lonquimay is a small, flat-topped, symmetrical stratovolcano of late-Pleistocene to dominantly Holocene age immediately SE of Tolguaca volcano.

name: Blanca, Laguna
summary: A group of cinder cones and associated lava flows SW of the town of Zapala at the southern end of the Loncopue graben form the Laguna Blanca volcanic field.

name: Llaima
summary: Llaima, one of Chile's largest and most active volcanoes, contains two main historically active craters, one at the summit and the other, Pichillaima, to the SE.

name: Sollipulli
summary: The 4-km-wide, glacier-filled Sollipulli caldera lies E of the Pleistocene Nevados de Sollipulli complex.

name: Caburgua-Huelemolle
summary: Four groups of basaltic cinder cones lie east of Lago Villarrica and NE of Villarrica volcano.

name: Villarrica
summary: The glacier-covered Villarrica stratovolcano, in the northern Lakes District of central Chile, is ~15 km south of the city of Pucon.

name: Quetrupillan
summary: The late-Pleistocene to Holocene Quetrupillán Volcanic Complex is at the center of a group of three volcanoes, with Villarrica and Lanin, trending transverse to the Andean chain.

name: Lanin
summary: Lanín is a large conical late-Pleistocene to Holocene stratovolcano along the Chile-Argentina border.

name: Huanquihue Group
summary: A group of young basaltic volcanoes lies in Argentina near the Chilean border, south of Lanín volcano.

name: Mocho-Choshuenco
summary: The compound Mocho-Choshuenco volcano is composed of two glacier-covered stratovolcanoes, located east of Lago Rinihué and SE of Lago Panguipulli and post-dating a 4-km-wide basaltic caldera.

name: Carran-Los Venados
summary: The Carrán-Los Venados volcano group includes about 50 basaltic to basaltic andesite scoria cones, maars, and a small stratovolcano that are broadly aligned along a 17-km-long ENE-WSW trend ESE of Lago Ranco.

name: Puyehue-Cordon Caulle
summary: The Puyehue-Cordón Caulle volcanic complex (PCCVC) is a large NW-SE-trending late-Pleistocene to Holocene basaltic-to-rhyolitic transverse volcanic chain SE of Lago Ranco.

name: Antillanca Volcanic Complex
summary: The Antillanca Volcanic Complex is a cluster of late-Pleistocene to Holocene basaltic-to-andesitic scoria cones, maars, and small stratovolcanoes covering an area of 380 km2 SE of Lago Puyehue and NE of Lago Rupanco.

name: Puntiagudo-Cordon Cenizos
summary: The Puntiagudo-Cordón Cenizos volcanic chain lies between Lago Rupanco and Lago Todos Los Santos in the Chilean lake district.

name: Osorno
summary: The symmetrical, glaciated, Osorno volcano towers above Todos los Santos and Llanquihué lakes.

name: Tronador
summary: The Tronador volcanic group straddles the Chile-Argentina border east of scenic Lake Todos los Santos.

name: Cayutue-La Vigueria
summary: The Cayutué-La Viguería volcanic field consists of about 20 basaltic maars and cinder cones of Holocene age along the N-S-trending Liquiñe-Ofqui fault zone.

name: Calbuco
summary: Calbuco is one of the most active volcanoes of the southern Chilean Andes, along with its neighbor, Osorno.

name: Yate
summary: Yate volcano is a late Pleistocene, glacially dissected basaltic andesite stratovolcano with Holocene flank vents.

name: Hornopiren
summary: Volcán Hornopirén, located SSW of Yate volcano, is a morphologically youthful basaltic andesite stratovolcano that is mostly forested.

name: Apagado
summary: Volcán Apagado, also known as Hualiaque, is located W of Hornopirén volcano and SW of Yate on the peninsula between the Gulf of Ancud and the Reloncaví estuary.

name: Crater Basalt Volcanic Field
summary: The Crater Basalt volcanic field in the northern Patagonia region of Argentina covers an area of about 700 km2.

name: Huequi
summary: Volcán Huequi is a small, glacier-free lava-dome complex in the center of the Huequi Peninsula in Ancud Bay.

name: Michinmahuida
summary: The glacier-covered basaltic-to-andesitic Volcán Michinmahuida, located west of Lago Reñihue, has a saddle-shaped summit with an elongated 3-km-wide caldera.

name: Chaiten
summary: Chaitén is a small caldera (~3 km in diameter) located 10 km NE of the town of Chaitén on the Gulf of Corcovado.

name: Yanteles
summary: Little-known glacier-covered Yanteles volcano in southern Chile is at the corner of a volcanic massif located 60 km S of the city of Chaiten, with higher eroded peaks about 5 km E and along a ridge extending 10 km SW.

name: Corcovado
summary: Little is known of this isolated volcano that was seen in eruption by Darwin in 1834, and an eruption was reported to have occurred in November 1835.

name: Melimoyu
summary: Melimoyu is a stratovolcano with an 8-km-wide, largely buried caldera located ~40 km NW of the town of Puyuhuapi.

name: Puyuhuapi
summary: A chain of dominantly basaltic cinder cones erupted along two NE-SW-trending fissures at the head of Puyuhuapi fjord comprise the Volcanes de Puyuhuapi.

name: Mentolat
summary: Volcán Mentolat is an ice-filled 6-km-wide caldera in the central part of Magdalena Island across the Puyuhuapi strait from Puerto Cisnes.

name: Cay
summary: Volcán Cay, located E of Macá volcano and NW of the town of Puerto Aisén, is a basaltic to dacitic stratovolcano.

name: Maca
summary: The glacier-covered, basaltic-to-dacitic Volcán Macá stratovolcano lies within a caldera and contains a summit lava dome.

name: Hudson, Cerro
summary: The ice-filled, 10-km-wide caldera of Cerro Hudson volcano was not recognized until its first 20th-century eruption in 1971.

name: Lautaro
summary: Lautaro is the northernmost volcano of the Austral Volcanic Zone (AVZ) in the southernmost Chilean Andes, and is the closest volcano to the Chile Triple Junction plate boundary.

name: Aguilera
summary: Aguilera, located west of Lake Argentina and NE of Peel Fjiord, is part of the Austral Volcanic Zone (AVZ) in the southernmost Chilean Andes.

name: Reclus
summary: Reclus, the source of several Patagonian Holocene tephra layers, was recognized to be an independent volcanic edifice in 1987.

name: Meullin
summary: The Meullín volcanic field consists of a chain of well-preserved cinder cones along the Lago Meullín, Lago Yulton, Río Cuervo, and Quitralco fault segments of the regional Liquine-Ofqui fault zone.

name: Burney, Monte
summary: Monte Burney, a large ice-covered volcano in the Patagonian region of Chile, lies about 200 km NW of the town of Punta Arenas.

name: Pali-Aike Volcanic Field
summary: The 3,000 km2 Pleistocene-to-Holocene Pali-Aike volcanic field straddles the Chile-Argentina border north of the Straits of Magellan, about 150 km NE of the town of Punta Arenas.

name: Fueguino
summary: A group of andesitic, columnar-jointed lava domes and pyroclastic cones up to 150 m high on Isla Cook mark the southernmost Holocene volcanoes of the Andes.

name: Saba
summary: Saba, the northernmost active volcano of the West Indies, is a 5-km-diameter island forming the upper half of a large stratovolcano that rises 1,500 m above the sea  floor.

name: Quill, The
summary: The Quill is a large dominantly andesitic stratovolcano that forms the SE end of St.

name: Liamuiga
summary: Mount Liamuiga volcano, comprising the NW end of St.

name: Nevis Peak
summary: The conical island of Nevis, lying across a narrow channel from St.

name: Soufriere Hills
summary: The complex, dominantly andesitic Soufrière Hills volcano occupies the southern half of the island of Montserrat.

name: Soufriere Guadeloupe
summary: La Soufrière de la Guadeloupe volcano occupies the southern end of Basse-Terre, the western half of the island of Guadeloupe.

name: Diables, Morne aux
summary: The lava dome complex of Morne aux Diables (Devils Peak) forms the northern tip of the island of Dominica.

name: Diablotins, Morne
summary: Morne Diablotins, in northern Dominica, is the largest and highest on the island.

name: Trois Pitons, Morne
summary: Two large lava-domes complexes, Morne Trois Pitons and Micotrin, rise NE of the capital city of Roseau in central Dominica.

name: Watt, Morne
summary: Morne Watt (Watt Mountain) volcano lies SE of the Trois Piton/Micotrin lava-dome complex in SE Dominica, E of the capital city of Roseau.

name: Plat Pays, Morne
summary: The Morne Plat Pays volcanic complex occupies the southern tip of the island of Dominica and has been active throughout the Holocene.

name: Pelee
summary: Montagne Pelée forms the northern end of the island of Martinique.

name: Qualibou
summary: The Qualibou caldera on the SW side of St.

name: Soufriere St. Vincent
summary: Soufrière St.

name: Kick 'em Jenny
summary: Kick 'em Jenny, an active submarine volcano 8 km off the N shore of Grenada, rises 1,300 m from the sea floor.

name: St. Catherine
summary: The island of Grenada is composed of five Pliocene-to-Pleistocene volcanic centers, the youngest and highest of which is Mount St.

name: Snaefellsjokull
summary: Ice-clad Snaefellsjökull volcano anchors the western tip of the isolated Snaefellsnes Peninsula in western Iceland.

name: Helgrindur
summary: Helgrindur (also known as Lysuhóll or Lysukard) is one of Iceland's smallest volcanic systems.

name: Ljosufjoll
summary: The Ljósufjöll volcanic system at the eastern end of the Snaefellsnes Peninsula is composed of a group of alkali olivine basaltic cinder cones and lava flows along short fissures on a roughly 90-km-long WNW-ESE line.

name: Reykjanes
summary: The Reykjanes volcanic system at the SW tip of the Reykjanes Peninsula, where the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rises above sea level, comprises a broad area of postglacial basaltic crater rows and small shield volcanoes.

name: Eldey
summary: The Eldey volcanic system is located on the northernmost part of the Reykjanes Ridge and is submarine with the exception of Eldey Island and the skerries (small rocky islands) Eldeyjardrangur, Geirfugladrangur, and Geirfuglasker.

name: Krysuvik-Trolladyngja
summary: The Krýsuvík-Trölladyngja volcanic system is described by the Catalogue of Icelandic Volcanoes as an approximately 50-km-long composite fissure swarm trending about N38°E, including a 30-km-long swarm of fissures, with no central volcano.

name: Fagradalsfjall
summary: Although the Fagradalsfjall fissure swarm has previously been considered a split or secondary swarm of the Krýsuvík–Trölladyngja volcanic system, as of September 2022 Icelandic volcanologists managing the Catalogue of Icelandic Volcanoes made the decision….

name: Brennisteinsfjoll
summary: The Brennisteinsfjöll volcanic system, located east of Kleifarvatn lake, consists of a series of NE-SW-trending crater rows and small shield volcanoes.

name: Hengill
summary: The Hengill volcanic system, cutting through Thingvallavatn lake, consists of a series of NE-SW-trending fissure vents, crater rows, and small shield volcanoes occupying a strongly faulted graben.

name: Hromundartindur
summary: Hrómundartindur is a small volcanic system located south of Thingvallavatn lake and immediately east of the Hengill volcanic system.

name: Grimsnes
summary: Grímsnes is a relatively small volcanic system located SE of Thingvallavatn lake.

name: Prestahnukur
summary: The Prestahnúkur volcanic system is located on the W side of the Langjökull icecap at the west margin of the Western Volcanic Zone, and overlaps with the Hengill volcanic system north of Lake Þingvallavatn.

name: Oddnyjarhnjukur-Langjokull
summary: The Oddnýjarhnjúkur-Langjökull system includes the Hveravellir central volcano at the northern end of this active volcanic zone that extends NE from the Reykjanes Peninsula.

name: Hofsjokull
summary: Hofsjökull volcano lies along an east-west-trending area connecting the two principal rift zones of Iceland.

name: Vestmannaeyjar
summary: The mostly submarine Vestmannaeyjar volcanic system is the southernmost and youngest volcanic center of the Eastern Volcanic Zone that cuts across E-central Iceland.

name: Eyjafjallajokull
summary: Eyjafjallajökull (also known as Eyjafjöll) is located west of Katla volcano.

name: Katla
summary: Katla volcano, located near the southern end of Iceland's eastern volcanic zone, is hidden beneath the Myrdalsjökull icecap.

name: Tindfjallajokull
summary: Tindfjallajökull is one of the oldest late-Quaternary volcanoes of the eastern volcanic zone of Iceland, and has produced rocks of basaltic-to-rhyolitic composition.

name: Torfajokull
summary: The Torfajökull central volcano, located north of Myrdalsjökull and south of Thorisvatn lake, is cut by a 12-km-wide caldera that formed during the Pleistocene.

name: Hekla
summary: One of Iceland's most prominent and active volcanoes, Hekla lies near the southern end of the eastern rift zone.

name: Grimsvotn
summary: Grímsvötn, Iceland's most frequently active volcano in recent history, lies largely beneath the vast Vatnajökull icecap.

name: Thordarhyrna
summary: The Þórðarhyrna central volcano has been moderately active during the Holocene, with the last eruption occurring in 1903 CE.

name: Bardarbunga
summary: The large central volcano of Bárðarbunga lies beneath the NW part of the Vatnajökull icecap, NW of Grímsvötn volcano, and contains a subglacial 700-m-deep caldera.

name: Tungnafellsjokull
summary: The Tungnafellsjökull central volcano, located immediately NW of the massive Vatnajökull icecap, contains two calderas.

name: Kverkfjoll
summary: Kverkfjöll is a large subglacial volcano at the NE end of the Vatnajökull icecap.

name: Askja
summary: Askja is a large basaltic central volcano that forms the Dyngjufjöll massif.

name: Fremrinamar
summary: The Fremrinámar volcanic system, N of Askja and SE of Myvatn lake, includes the central Ketildyngja shield volcano and the Sveinar fissure swarm that extends 130 km to the north coast of Iceland.

name: Krafla
summary: The Krafla volcanic system in the Northern Volcanic Zone (NVZ) of Iceland is about 100 km long, consisting of a fissure swarm and a central volcano with a 7 x 9 km caldera formed about 110,000 years ago that deposited a rhyolitic welded tuff.

name: Heidarspordar
summary: The Heiðarsporðar volcanic system in the Northern Volcanic Zone is about 22 km long, consisting of a fissure swarm and a central volcano.

name: Theistareykir
summary: The Holocene Theistareykir fissure system, including the basaltic Theistareykjarbunga shield volcano, extends from north of Myvatn lake to the coast of Iceland.

name: Tjornes Fracture Zone
summary: The offshore Tjörnes Fracture Zone is an oblique transform zone that separates the northern volcanic zone of Iceland from the Kolbeinsey Ridge, part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge north of Iceland.

name: Oraefajokull
summary: Öræfajökull, Iceland's highest peak, is a broad glacier-clad central volcano at the SE end of the Vatnajökull icecap.

name: Esjufjoll
summary: The subglacial Esjufjöll volcano at the SE part of the Vatnajökull icecap, north of Öraefajökull, consists of the Snaehetta central volcano and a large caldera.

name: Snaefell
summary: The timing of the most recent activity in the Snæfell volcanic system, NE of Vatnajökull, is unknown.

name: Kolbeinsey Ridge
summary: A submarine eruption was reported in 1372 CE near the Kolbeinsey Ridge NW of Grimsey Island.

name: Jan Mayen
summary: Remote Jan Mayen Island, located in the Norwegian Sea along the Jan Mayen Ridge about 650 km NE of Iceland, consists of two volcanic complexes separated by a narrow isthmus.

name: East Gakkel Ridge at 85°E
summary: During January-September 1999 global seismic networks detected an earthquake swarm along the East Gakkel Ridge (near 86°N, 85°E).

name: Pico Fracture Zone
summary: On 9 July 1865 the crew of a whaling ship observed a submarine eruption.

name: Flores
summary: Flores Island and Corvo Island to its north are located over 200 km W of the other Azores islands, west of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

name: Fayal
summary: The island of Fayal, also spelled Faial, is the nearest of the central Azorean islands to the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

name: Pico
summary: The conical Pico stratovolcano occupies the western end of Pico Island and is the highest volcano in the Azores.

name: Sao Jorge
summary: The dominantly basaltic São Jorge Island is 55 km long and 6.5 km wide.

name: Graciosa
summary: The SE end of Graciosa, the northernmost of the central Azorean islands, contains a 0.9 x 1.6 km caldera with active fumaroles.

name: Terceira
summary: Terceira Island contains multiple stratovolcanoes constructed along a prominent ESE-WNW fissure zone that cuts across the island.

name: Don Joao de Castro Bank
summary: Don Joao de Castro Bank is a large submarine volcano that rises to within 13 m of the ocean surface roughly halfway between Terceira and San Miguel Islands.

name: Sete Cidades
summary: Sete Cidades volcano at the western end of Sao Miguel Island contains a 5-km-wide summit caldera occupied by two caldera lakes.

name: Picos Fissural Volcanic System
summary: Nearly 200 scoria cones of the Picos volcanic system dot the narrow central zone of Sao Miguel Island between Sete Cidades and Agua de Pau volcanoes.

name: Agua de Pau
summary: The Agua de Pau stratovolcano in central Sao Miguel Island contains an outer 4 x 7 km caldera formed about 30,000-45,000 years ago and an inner 2.5 x 3 km caldera that was created about 15,000 years ago.

name: Furnas
summary: Furnas volcano lies at the eastern end of Sao Miguel Island, immediately west of the older Nordeste shield volcano and its Povoaçao caldera.

name: Monaco Bank
summary: Monaco Bank is a submarine volcano constructed along a NW-SE-trending fissure 20 km S of the western tip of Sao Miguel Island.

name: Madeira
summary: Madeira Island is the emergent top of a massive shield volcano that rises about 6 km from the floor of the Atlantic Ocean and forms the largest island of the 90-km-long Madeira Archipelago.

name: La Palma
summary: The 47-km-long wedge-shaped island of La Palma, the NW-most of the Canary Islands, is composed of two large volcanic centers.

name: Hierro
summary: The triangular island of Hierro is the SW-most and least studied of the Canary Islands.

name: Tenerife
summary: The large triangular island of Tenerife is composed of a complex of overlapping Miocene-to-Quaternary stratovolcanoes.

name: Gran Canaria
summary: The circular 60-km-wide island of Gran Canaria in the middle of the Canary archipelago includes three major volcanic structures, and has been modified by caldera collapse, gravitational edifice failure, and extensive erosion resulting in steep-walled….

name: Fuerteventura
summary: Pleistocene and Holocene cinder cones and lava flows cover large portions of elongated Fuerteventura Island at the SE end of the Canary Islands.

name: Lanzarote
summary: The 60-km-long island of Lanzarote at the NE end of the Canary Islands contains the largest concentration of youthful volcanism in the Canaries.

name: Fogo
summary: The island of Fogo consists of a single massive stratovolcano that is the most prominent of the Cape Verde Islands.

name: Brava
summary: Brava Island, 18 km W of Fogo, is the westernmost of the southern Cape Verde islands.

name: Romanche Fracture Zone
summary: Several reports of submarine disturbances of possible volcanic origin near the equator were noted by Neumann van Padang et al.

name: Ascension
summary: Ascensión Island, just west of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge ~2,250 km E of the eastern-most point of Brazil, is the 12-km-diameter emergent summit of a stratovolcano that rises ~3,000 m above the seafloor.

name: Walvis Ridge at 33°S
summary: Hydrophones in the North Atlantic Ocean recorded signals from an explosive eruption in the South Atlantic along the Walvis Ridge about 780 km NE of Tristan da Cunha Island (Haxel and Dziak, 2005).

name: Tristan da Cunha
summary: Tristan da Cunha is a 13-km-wide island volcano lying about 500 km E of the crest of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge just south of the latitudes of Buenos Aires and Cape Town.

name: Nightingale Island
summary: Nightingale Island, along with the adjacent smaller Middle (or Alex) and Stoltenhoff Islands and associated small islets, are the southernmost of the Tristan da Cunha island group.

name: Bouvet
summary: The solitary ice-covered shield volcano of Bouvet Island is located just off the Southwest Indian Ridge, east of the triple junction between the African, South American, and Antarctic plates.

name: Buckle Island
summary: Buckle Island is in the center of a 160-km-long chain of volcanic islands forming the Balleny Islands off the coast of Antarctica's Victoria Land.

name: Young Island
summary: Young Island is the northernmost and second largest of the Balleny Islands off the coast of Antarctica's Victoria Land.

name: Sturge Island
summary: Sturge is the largest and southernmost of the Balleny Islands, which are located just off the coast of Antarctica's Victoria Land.

name: Pleiades, The
summary: The Pleiades volcano consists of the small trachytic Mount Pleiones stratovolcano which, along with several lava domes and nested cinder cones with well-preserved craters, rises above the broad Evans Neve plateau.

name: Melbourne
summary: Mount Melbourne is a large undissected stratovolcano along the western coast of the Ross Sea in Antarctica's northern Victoria Land.

name: McMurdo Province at 76.8°S
summary: Magnetic and seismic data suggest that a submarine caldera with a central lava dome is present east of Granite Harbor and north of Ross Island, near the western coast of the Ross Sea and near the southern end of the submarine Victoria Land Basin.

name: Morning
summary: Mount Morning is a glaciated, undissected, alkalic shield volcano in the Erebus volcanic province SE of the south end of the Royal Society Range.

name: Erebus
summary: Mount Erebus overlooks the McMurdo research station on Ross Island and is the largest of three major volcanoes forming the roughly triangular Ross Island.

name: Royal Society Range
summary: A large number of basaltic cinder cones and lava flows are located in the Royal Society Range of southern Victoria Land.

name: Berlin
summary: Mount Berlin consists of two coalescing shield volcanoes, Berlin Crater and Merrem Peak, each with a 2-km-wide summit caldera.

name: Andrus
summary: Three coalescing trachytic shield volcanoes with a combined volume of 252 km3 formed during the Miocene along a N-S line in the Ames Range of western Marie Byrd Land.

name: Takahe
summary: Mount Takahe is an isolated shield volcano in eastern Marie Byrd Land with an 8-km-wide summit caldera.

name: Hudson Mountains
summary: The Hudson Mountains, located along the Walgreen Coast in Antarctica's western Ellsworth Land, contain many only slightly eroded cones forming nunataks protruding above the Antarctic icecap.

name: Deception Island
summary: Ring-shaped Deception Island, at the SW end of the South Shetland Islands, NE of Graham Land Peninsula, was constructed along the axis of the Bransfield Rift spreading center.

name: Penguin Island
summary: The 1.4 x 1.7 km Penguin Island is located off the SE coast of King George Island in Antarctica's South Shetland Islands, west of the axis of the Bransfield Rift.

name: Bridgeman Island
summary: Bridgeman Island is a small 600 x 900 m remnant of a much larger volcanic edifice that is now largely submerged.

name: Paulet
summary: Paulet is a 1.8 x 2.2 km island located east of the tip of Graham Land Peninsula composed of lava flows capped by scoria cones.

name: Southern Thule
summary: The Southern Thule island group, at the southern end of the South Sandwich island arc bordering the Scotia Sea, consist of three stratovolcanoes constructed along an E-W line.

name: Bristol Island
summary: The 9 x 10 km Bristol Island near the southern end of the South Sandwich arc lies across Fortser's Passage from the Southern Thule Islands and forms one of the largest islands of the chain.

name: Montagu Island
summary: The largest of the South Sandwich Islands, Montagu consists of a massive shield volcano cut by a 6-km-wide ice-filled summit caldera.

name: Saunders
summary: Saunders Island consists of a large central volcanic edifice intersected by two seamount chains, as shown by bathymetric mapping (Leat et al., 2013).

name: Candlemas Island
summary: The southern end of Candlemas Island consists of an eroded, glacier-covered basaltic stratovolcano cut by steep cliffs on the east.

name: Hodson
summary: The largely ice-covered, 5.5 x 7 km Visokoi Island consists of a single stratovolcano, Mount Hodson, whose rounded summit lies west of the center of the island.

name: Leskov Island
summary: The small crescent-shaped Leskov Island lies about 50 km W of the main axis of the South Sandwich Islands, but appears to be comparable in age to volcanoes along the main arc.

name: Zavodovski
summary: The 5-km-wide Zavodovski Island, the northernmost of the South Sandwich Islands, consists of a single basaltic stratovolcano with two cones on the east side.

name: Protector Seamounts
summary: The Protector Seamounts, located 30 km NW of Zavodovski Island, form the northernmost volcanic region of the South Sandwich volcanic arc.

name: Mount Haddington Volcanic Field
summary: The glacier-covered Mount Haddington shield volcano forms the high point of James Ross Island along the Larsen Rift near the northern tip of the Antarctic Peninsula.

name: Melville
summary: Melville Peak is an eroded stratovolcano on NE King George Island with a summit crater.
